Expression: TCGA-THYM tumor and normal (2 normal samples, so the default Tumor+Normal pair stays; both are lymphocyte-dominated thymus). ATAC null: THYM is not among the 23 TCGA ATAC-seq cohorts (Corces et al. 2018). No adult human thymus epigenome exists anywhere: Roadmap's two thymus epigenomes are E093 (fetal, 15 weeks) and E112 (a 3-year-old child), and ENCODE's human thymus tissue is the same child donor (ENCDO478OMA, six histone marks) plus fetal donors only (all DNase is embryonic). No thymic epithelial cell, thymoma or thymic carcinoma line or primary cell is in ENCODE (searches for thymic epithelial, thymoma, thymic carcinoma, IU-TAB-1, T1889, Ty-82 and medullary thymic return zero). repliseq null: nothing in the human RT universe is thymic epithelium or any third-pharyngeal-pouch derivative. roadmap and encode_chromatin are left null rather than filled with the child thymus, which is both non-adult and the wrong compartment (thymocyte chromatin, not epithelial). This row carries expression only; its chromatin and replication timing are expected to come from GENERIC if the own + GENERIC matrix is adopted. Assemblies: expression and GTEx gene-level only (no bigWig blocks).), built with sigmutselcovs : GTEx tissue-matched gene expression, TCGA per-sample gene expression, replication timing (mean replication time and CLR-transformed S-phase fractions), Roadmap Epigenomics histone marks, and TCGA ATAC-seq accessibility, indexed by Ensembl gene ID. Files: cov_matrix_full.parquet — the full matrix (all covariate columns of this cohort) cov_matrix_pca.parquet — the exact principal components of the combined matrix (this cohort's columns plus the GENERIC pool's) over all 18,967 genes, 1019 components, the smallest number reaching 99% cumulative explained variance (see pca_manifest.json) pca_loadings.parquet — the principal axes: one row per component, one column per covariate column, in standardized units (float32) pca_columns.parquet — each covariate column's centre and scale (the mean and standard deviation it was standardized with) and the decomposition's own centring pca_genes.parquet — every gene of the decomposition and whether all its covariates were observed ( complete ; 2,569 were not) pca_indicators.parquet — every gene, one 0/1 column per covariate block: 1 where the gene misses (part of) that block cov_matrix_columns.csv — a data dictionary: one row per column of the full matrix, with source, description, assembly, and units build_manifest.json , pca_manifest.json — build provenance, and how the decomposition was computed Full source citations and methodology: SOURCES.md . Release of 2026-10-26. Every chromatin and ATAC column is one track, summarized as log1p of the mean signal over the gene's CDS span (first to last coding base); replication timing covers chrX. cov_matrix_pca.parquet now reduces the combined matrix : this cohort's own covariates plus the tissue-agnostic GENERIC pool ( GENERIC record ), with the pool's columns for chromatin tracks this cohort already has left out. That is the matrix the sigmutsel covariate model is fitted on; it predicts held-out mutation counts better than the cohort's own matrix alone in the cohorts tested, so the first components of this artifact are the ones a model should use. Versions before 2026-10-26 reduced the own matrix alone. cov_matrix_full.parquet is still the cohort's own matrix; GENERIC's is in its record. pca_manifest.json reco

summary: Pre-built per-gene covariate matrices for TCGA-THCA (Thyroid carcinoma (TCGA-THCA: papillary thyroid carcinoma, from thyroid follicular epithelial cells). GTEx maps to Thyroid (representative gtex_thyroid). TCGA ATAC-seq covered (Corces et al. 2018; the tarball's bigWigs are named THCA_..., read from its first member). Expression: TCGA-THCA tumor and normal (59 solid-tissue normals, so the default Tumor+Normal pair stays). Roadmap null: none of its 127 epigenomes is thyroid. encode_chromatin: adult thyroid gland tissue from one ENTEx donor (ENCDO271OUW, female, 51y; THCA is about three-quarters female, so a female donor matches the cohort's chrX state) -- H3K27ac, H3K27me3, H3K36me3, H3K4me1, H3K4me3, H3K9me3 and DNase, all single-replicate. Three other adult donors (ENCDO845WKR male 37y, ENCDO451RUA male 54y, ENCDO793LXB female 53y, the last without H3K27me3) carry the same panel and are left out to keep one donor. No thyroid cell line has usable chromatin in ENCODE: K1 (the only thyroid-carcinoma line there, and an ICLAC-listed GLAG-66 derivative) has only a RAD21 ChIA-PET; TPC-1, B-CPAP, 8505C, FTC-133, Nthy-ori 3-1 return nothing. repliseq null: nothing in the replication-timing catalog is thyroid or follicular epithelium; the hESC-derived posterior-foregut endocrine Repli-chip profile is embryonic and pancreatic-lineage, rejected. GENERIC's pooled RT covers it. It also costs every chrX/chrY gene, the autosome-only MAT's standard price. No testis or germ-cell-tumor line exists in ENCODE's complete 182-experiment replication-timing catalog either.), built with sigmutselcovs : GTEx tissue-matched gene expression, TCGA per-sample gene expression, replication timing (mean replication time and CLR-transformed S-phase fractions), Roadmap Epigenomics histone marks, and TCGA ATAC-seq accessibility, indexed by Ensembl gene ID. summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/24385327 . ### Summary and Overall Assessment Camila Pontara's manuscript, "A Captura Silenciosa: Captura de Fecho, Opacidade e os Limites da Teoria da Governança Criminal" (Version 2), tackles an important blind spot in governance and institutional research. Most studies look at obvious bribery, political lobbying, or open territorial control. Pontara looks somewhere quieter and harder to detect: what she calls closure capture (*captura de fecho*). This happens inside final review and decision-making bodies when concentrated authority and closed-door procedures make it nearly impossible for outsiders to independently verify how a decision was actually reached. The strongest insight in this paper is how it applies the problem of observational equivalence (*equivalência observacional*). Pontara shows that when a final review body operates without real external transparency, an honest, by-the-book decision and a decision quietly shaped by outside interests can leave behind the exact same official paper trail. By refining Version 2 to treat Operações Munditia , Ethos , Scream Fake , and the Banco Master case as exploratory plausibility probes rather than claiming direct causal proof, she keeps the argument disciplined, fair, and grounded as a testable hypothesis. --- ### Core Strengths 1. Avoiding the "Secrecy Equals Guilt" Trap: Rather than treating institutional opacity as automatic proof of corruption, Pontara frames institutional verifiability as a measurable spectrum. That restraint makes her framework genuinely useful for researchers comparing different agencies or legal systems. 2. Connecting Criminal Governance to Financial Oversight: Including the Banco Master episode alongside judicial and administrative cases shows that closure capture is not just an organized-crime issue—it is a structural risk anywhere high-stakes financial or regulatory decisions are closed off from outside scrutiny. 3. Clear Boundaries in Version 2: Explicitly laying out alternative explanations and criteria that could disprove the hypothesis makes this a strong, portable starting point for future comparative studies. --- ### Constructive Suggestions for Revision 1. Addressing the "Missing Evidence" Problem in Process Tracing: Because closure capture works by hiding or blocking the paper trail needed to prove outside influence, researchers using process tracing face an uphill battle: the lack of a "smoking gun" in the file looks identical whether the institution acted cleanly or successfully hid its tracks. The paper would be stronger if it briefly explained how researchers can tell the difference—for example, by looking at unusual timing, sudden shifts in how cases are routed, or decisions that break sharply from normal institutional patterns. 2. Clarifying When Legitimate Confidentiality Becomes Closure Capture: In criminal investigations and banking supervision (like Banco Master ), temporary secrecy is often necessary to protect witnesses, ongoing inquiries, or financial stability. Drawing a clearer line around timing would sharpen the argument: legitimate confidentiality is temporary during an active review, whereas closure capture uses the final closing of a case to keep the record permanently locked away from retrospective audit. 3. Connecting to International Research on Institutional Opacity and Intermediary Entropy: Pontara's insight—that formal, closed procedures can look completely clean on the surface while masking hidden distortion underneath—connects directly to international work on the Systemic Intent Shadow (SIS) and The Zero-Defect Paradox (Rodriguez, 2026a, 2026b). That line of research examines how administrative delays and one-sided verification create "gray zones" where legitimate decisions and compromised ones look identical to outside auditors, and how rigid, box-ticking compliance degra

summary: This repository contains the source code, benchmark data, and computational results for FigEA, an evolutionary algorithm developed for the Minimum Fill-In Problem, also known as the chordal completion problem. FigEA represents candidate solutions through vertex elimination orderings and combines evolutionary operators with problem-specific constructive information. The repository includes the implementation of the algorithm, constructive heuristics used for comparison and initialization, benchmark instances, experimental scripts, and auxiliary files required to reproduce the computational experiments and analyze the reported results. The benchmark instances are based on the PACE 2017 Minimum Fill-In dataset. The materials are provided to facilitate reproducibility, verification of the reported results, and further experimentation with evolutionary approaches to chordal completion.
title: FigEA: An Evolutionary Algorithm for the Minimum Fill-In Problem — Code, Data, and Computational Results

summary: OpenEBench implementation of the ELIXIR 3D-BioInfo benchmark for discriminating physiological from crystallographic (non-physiological) protein homodimer interfaces: schema-validated OpenEBench metadata (Community, Benchmarking Event, Challenge, Metrics, Tools, Contacts), the datasets of 14 reference scoring methods (13 research groups and a random-forest consensus), the gold-standard labels, four homology-aware cross-validation fold assignments, the benchmark workflow scripts (validation, metric computation, consolidation), and a static web page that evaluates new predictions in the browser and ranks them against the reference methods. The benchmark has 1,671 entries (840 physiological and 831 non-physiological): the 1,677 entries of the curated annotation of the benchmark authors, without the six entries flagged for deletion. The labels are those of the curated annotation, which differs for 16 entries from the original publication (Schweke et al. 2023, Proteomics 23(17):e2200323, doi:10.1002/pmic.202200323; 836 physiological and 841 non-physiological interfaces). The scores of the 13 research groups are those submitted to the original benchmark repository; the random-forest consensus uses the leave-one-out probabilities provided there. Interactive page: https://elixir.unibo.it/tools/oeb_3dbioinfo_ppi_benchmark/ . Please cite the original publication as well as this package.
title: ELIXIR - Protein-Protein Interface Benchmark - OpenEBench Experiment

summary: Continual reinforcement learning requires adaptation to changing conditions while preserving performance under previously encountered dynamics. It was investigated whether specialists generated by evolutionary search can provide a reusable memory when combined with environment detection and failure-driven search. The Evolutionary Neuroplastic Agent (ENA) evolves small neural networks without gradients, archives selected policies by detected dynamic regime, and retrieves them through Bayesian policy reuse. The architecture was evaluated in non-stationary CartPole and HalfCheetah environments. In the 30-replicate CartPole ablation, the complete architecture achieved a mean success rate of 83.2% across the five test environments. Among variants that learned the harder CartPole environments, the complete architecture showed the most consistent retention. A selection ablation also showed that the retrieval rule affected performance. In the evaluated sequences, ENA adapted more slowly than PPO on CartPole and achieved lower returns than SAC on HalfCheetah. The evidence concerns the complete architecture and does not isolate gradient-free optimization as the cause of retention or establish superiority over other continual-learning methods.
title: Mitigating Catastrophic Forgetting with Physics-Indexed Specialist Memory: the Evolutionary Neuroplastic Agent

summary: Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDSs) must incrementally adapt to emerging attacks, even when only a limited amount of labeled network traffic is available. Consequently, Few-Shot Class-Incremental Learning (FSCIL)-based NIDSs have gained growing attention. However, existing FSCIL-based NIDSs are highly vulnerable to label noise in newly-observed attack classes. To address this limitation, we propose NAFN, a noise-aware FSCIL-based NIDS framework that reduces the impact of mislabeled data during incremental adaptation. NAFN consists of two components: (i) Noise Detection, which identifies and removes mislabeled biflows using noise-detection algorithms, and (ii) Feature Sampling, which estimates class-conditional embeddings from clean biflows, calibrates them with base-class statistics, and resamples synthetic features to recover the original biflow count. The framework follows the Rethink Few-Shot (RFS) teacher-student paradigm with lightweight nearest-neighbor or logistic regression classifiers, and various pretraining & memory selection strategies. Experiments on CSE-CIC-IDS2018, Edge-IIoT, and IoT-NID datasets show that NAFN effectively preserves prior knowledge and maintains strong incremental performance even under 50% label noise, consistently improving new-class F1-scores over non-denoised baselines, up to +52%, while being time-efficient and robust in cross-network and high-noise incremental settings. The implementation is publicly available to foster reproducibility.
title: Network Intrusion Detection Adaptability under Spurious Labels: A Noise-Aware Few-Shot Class-Incremental Learning Framework

summary: Generative artificial intelligence is entering the home. Cloud-based assistants face governance limitations in data transmission, continuous availability, and the reliability of physical actions, which are especially salient in households where devices remain online, data accumulate over time, and commands trigger real-world actions. Using the home local server as a unifying organizing axis, this article develops a design-oriented review framework. Sources from arXiv, CNKI, ACL Anthology, and official documentation were searched through November 2026 and coded into five evidence categories: reviews, system prototypes, benchmarks, HCI and eldercare studies, and official documentation. System designs were mapped onto shared architectural modules, identifying nine recurrent responsibilities of the home local server. Generative models support perceptual interpretation, intent understanding, and candidate planning, while deterministic validation, knowledge-graph constraints, and authorization leases confine candidate actions to an inspectable space. Home control, emotional companionship, and intelligent guarding can be compared within a common framework: they share state and memory but differ in latency, false positive and negative rates, proactivity, and permissions. Existing benchmarks rely on virtual environments and cannot substitute for real-deployment evaluation. Local deployment is not inherently safer, and technical continuity alone does not establish the social or medical effects of companionship and guarding. The article proposes a five-dimensional evaluation framework covering architectural capability, system resources, privacy, safety and reliability, and human experience, together with six design principles and a future research agenda for local-first intelligent home systems.
title: A Generative AI-Driven Architecture for Whole-Home Intelligent Services: Edge Models, Memory Management, and Household Applications

summary: Apple Reference Image (ARI) combines camera-sensor signatures, Secure Enclave attestation (SEP), cryptographic timestamp bounds, Private Cloud Compute (PCC), and a final post-quantum signature to establish photographic provenance. PCC is central to this process because it validates the secure digital negative and develops authenticated raw sensor measurements into a reference JPEG. Although the secure digital negative is encrypted during transmission, the authorized PCC workload must process the raw pixels in plaintext. This requirement creates a provenance-privacy paradox: cloud processing strengthens the provenance guarantee while giving an Apple-authorized, machine-learning-capable workload access to valuable, hardware-authenticated raw imagery. We argue that workload attestation and transparency-log inclusion verify software identity and authorization but do not, by themselves, prove that an authorized workload cannot learn from or retain information derived from the photograph. We implement this counterexample in a Python- and Docker-based experimental testbed that models relevant ARI and PCC functions. Across 27 public-domain photographs, a baseline workload and a learning-enabled workload both passed the same verification checks and returned byte-for-byte identical JPEGs. However, the learning-enabled workload retained a first-layer gradient of approximately 48 KB from which its 64 x 64 input was reconstructed with a maximum absolute per-pixel error of 6 x 10^-8. The additional processing overhead was small relative to image decoding and processing. These results do not demonstrate that Apple currently trains on ARI photographs or reproduce production PCC, but identify non-learning and non-retention as independently verifiable assurance requirements.
title: The Provenance-Privacy Paradox: Can Private Cloud Compute (PCC) Prove That Apple Reference Images Are Not Used for Learning?

summary: Weighted conformal p-values generalize conformal inference to cases with covariate shift. One way to use them is to pass them to the Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) procedure, either to decide which test units to select or to detect outliers. But weighted conformal p-values may not be positively dependent, so we want to know: does BH still control the false discovery rate (FDR) in finite samples? Based on experiments, it appears to, but we prove it doesn't. We give two counterexamples, certified in exact rational arithmetic, where the FDR exceeds its target level $q$. We also identify how large the difference between the FDR and $q$ can be. With $n$ calibration points, $m$ test units and weight ratio $B$, the relative excess $\mathrm{FDR}/q-1$ is bounded by a function of $n$, $m$, $B$ and $q$ that is of order $\sqrt{Bm/(nq)}$ when $Bm/(nq)$ is small. The bound holds for every configuration with $B\le n$ and every $n$. This order can be reached when multiple non-null test units share a common threshold: in a Poisson-limit model, that configuration's excess is $c(q)\sqrt{Bm/(nq)}$ to first order as $B/n\to0$ and then $m\to\infty$. For some fixed distributions with this structure, the excess decreases only like $n^{-1/2}$ as $n$ grows. If every test unit is null, the excess is $O(B/n)$ at fixed $m$, and in certain configurations it grows linearly with $m$. To assist practitioners in judging how large the FDR can be, we turn that bound, which depends only on $n$, $m$, $q$ and $B$, into a lowered BH level with proved finite-sample control, and give a much less conservative rule of thumb that covers every worst case we were able to find but provides no guarantee.
title: Almost Controlled: The FDR of Benjamini-Hochberg on Weighted Conformal p-Values

summary: Predicting metastable states with universal machine-learned interatomic potentials requires that they preserve the minima and saddles of the reference potential-energy surface. Here we identify local topology hallucination, in which distinct model minima relax into the same reference basin. This failure arises from mode-selective curvature-sign errors shared by MACE, CHGNet and M3GNet. Curvature signs predicted by two of the three models agreed with density-functional calculations in 55 of 57 positive but only 5 of 56 negative cases. In LiGe$_2$S, two MACE minima connected by a verified saddle relaxed into one density-functional basin. Reference relaxation likewise returned nine of ten selected model minima to their reference basins. A directional test with two displaced reference calculations rejected 9 of 12 prospectively tested model instabilities. Model agreement alone therefore cannot establish that predicted minima are distinct metastable states.
title: Local topology hallucinations in universal machine-learned interatomic potentials

summary: Persistent spatial understanding is essential for embodied agents to operate reliably in environments they repeatedly encounter. It requires recognizing revisited places despite viewpoint changes, distinguishing them from similar-looking rooms, and updating memories as environments change. Yet existing evaluations often leave physical place identity across separated visits implicit. We introduce ReSpaceBench, a benchmark comprising 3,244 questions across 590 synthetic and real-home scenes, organized into 9 tasks spanning room association, persistent state tracking, and downstream reasoning. Controlled walkthroughs define visits by physical room entry and deliberately include same-type room distractors and cross-session object changes. Our evaluation of 32 models and 3 agentic video-understanding frameworks reveals substantial limitations: the strongest evaluated zero-shot model achieves 50.5% overall accuracy and 52.2% on a 450-question subset, compared with 90.1% for human annotators. The evaluated agentic frameworks offer no overall improvement over direct inference with the same base model. Analysis of agent execution traces reveals evidence omissions and incorrect cross-visit room associations as major failure modes, suggesting that iterative evidence seeking alone does not ensure consistent spatial memory. Further analyses expose a gap between recognizing familiar rooms and identifying the correct visited room, while annotation-guided sampling highlights the importance of preserving intervening visits and transitions. We also provide RS-30K, a separate training dataset from synthetic sources with no template, scene, route, or video overlap with the benchmark. Fine-tuning Qwen3-VL-8B raises overall accuracy from 35.5% to 60.4%, with the largest gains in association and improvements extending to real-life scenes.
title: Lost in the Hallway: Benchmarking Persistent Spatial Memory Across Revisits

summary: The Flowering protocol of Delavenne, Medevielle and Roussel (ISIT 2025, arXiv:2501.14337) and its generalization by Delavenne and Lallemand (CANS 2025, arXiv:2508.10510) are Interactive Oracle Proofs of Proximity (IOPPs) for codes on graphs with Reed-Solomon local codes. Similarly to FRI for Reed-Solomon codes, the graph is recursively cut into isomorphic subgraphs and the word is folded along the cuts. We show that the soundness claims of both papers are false. The commit soundness proofs identify the vertex distance of a word to the code with the fraction of its unsatisfied local constraints, while only one inequality holds, in the wrong direction. We furthermore give an explicit counterexample.
title: A counterexample to the soundness of the Flowering IOPP for codes on graphs

summary: Atomistic machine learning can approximate expensive quantum mechanical calculations at a fraction of their computational cost, but accuracy depends strongly on how the three-dimensional atomic environments are represented. Invariant representations enable fast computation but can fail to distinguish geometrically distinct configurations, especially in highly symmetric environments. We introduce a lightweight benchmark to evaluate expressivity on $n$-fold symmetric configurations, and use it to expose degeneracies in both invariant and equivariant architectures. Guided by these results, we construct a new invariant basis for HIP-HOP which resolves most of the identified failures. On a methane simulation dataset, the extended basis achieves the lowest error among the HIP-HOP variants and has similar accuracy to EquiformerV3 while running $3.2\times$ faster at inference. These results show that carefully constructed invariant representations can mitigate key expressivity limitations while balancing accuracy and computational efficiency.
title: Rotation-Invariant Machine Learning for Highly Symmetric Molecular Configurations

summary: Language-model agents' beliefs can be manipulated through open channels such as social media, even when the information they receive is truthful. When agents fill gaps between fragments with self-induced relationships, they may accept those relationships as established facts and pass the resulting rumours to others. Drawing on cognitive theory of narrative understanding and film theory of montage, we introduce Generative Montage to operationalize this failure, termed narrative overfitting, by coordinating agents to arrange truthful fragments into misleading narratives. Across 1,090 rumour targets from six Twitter events, agents often accepted rumours overconfidently, with overall acceptance exceeding 65 percent in twelve of fourteen models. Acceptance remained above 50 percent after majority voting or review of the same evidence, showing how errors can reach downstream decisions. To explain this susceptibility, fragment interventions identify posts that influence belief within complete narratives. Synthetic controls then show that similar response patterns arise from valid evidence, separating belief influence from evidential support. This distinction motivates Grounded Monitor, a proof-of-concept neuro-symbolic runtime monitor that checks direct evidential support to guide agents' judgements, improving decision accuracy by 5.6 to 29.0 percentage points across original and anonymized settings. These findings expose a cognitive route to rumour amplification and support monitoring inferred relationships before agent-generated conclusions guide public decisions.
title: Language-model agents' beliefs can be manipulated via truthful evidence in open channel

summary: Large language models (LLMs) offer a potential route to automating scientific programming, but their usefulness depends on consistently producing numerically correct code. We extend FEM-Bench to 17 finite element tasks involving nonlinear and history-dependent mechanics and structural dynamics, and evaluate 15 models on implementation and test generation without execution feedback. The best model succeeds in 87.1% of single-pass implementation trials, but rankings differ between tracks. The leading implementer achieves 49.9% joint test success, while the leading tester reaches 82.6%. For six models, we compare single-pass generation with two agentic harnesses that allow code execution and revision. Agentic execution solves some tasks that never succeeded in single-pass trials and improves consistency on others, but gains vary across models and harnesses, and regressions also occur. Claude Opus 5 with SimpleAgent reaches 96.5% Pass@3, the probability of at least one success in three attempts, but 77.1% Pass$^3$, the probability that all three succeed. No model-harness combination exceeds 78.8% Pass$^3$. To understand why agents submit incorrect code after passing their own checks, we analyze 249 failed agentic trajectories and identify six categories of self-verification failure. The most common are inadequate test coverage (73.1%) and reliance on generic consistency checks (70.3%), and in 28.5% of cases the tests share an error with the implementation. Motivated by these findings, an exploratory configuration with separate coder and tester agents achieves the highest observed scores, with 97.6% Pass@3 and 88.8% Pass$^3$. These results identify consistency across attempts and independent verification as the main obstacles to trusting LLM-generated scientific code.
title: Scientific Coding with Large Language Models: Evidence from Finite Element Analysis

summary: After a large language model (LLM) agent generates an artifact, users often send edit requests for it. This paper studies whether an LLM can anticipate these requests before they are sent. Such anticipation is useful in practice because it reduces the effort of user review and feedback. We formalize this task as edit recommendation and build EditRecBench, a benchmark for evaluating the performance of LLMs on this task, from real-world conversation logs in WildChat-4.8M. Through benchmarking and failure analysis, we identify a practical challenge that some cases are inherently difficult to predict in real-world settings. To address this, we introduce decision model-based gating to filter out cases where predictions are unlikely to be correct before they are presented to the user. Our trained model outperforms existing decision models and raises pass@5 among shown suggestions by 12--25 points at a gating threshold. Our code is available at https://github.com/ntt-dkiku/llm-edit-recommendation.
title: Edit Recommendation: Can LLMs Anticipate Edit Requests from Users, and When?

summary: In this work, we study on-policy distillation (OPD) for transferring agentic coding capabilities from a large teacher model to a smaller student model. Prior work has focused primarily on reasoning and short-horizon agentic tasks. We present SWE-OPD, a minimal OPD study for software engineering, where the student interacts with executable repositories and the teacher supervises the prefixes visited by the student. Across three teacher--student pairs, two training sources, and three SWE benchmarks, we find that on-policy supervision transfers coding capability: supervision from Qwen3.6-27B increases the SWE-bench Pro resolve rate of Qwen3.5-9B from 35.9% to 39.4%. Refreshing trajectories is not strictly required either, as an offline variant with cached teacher scores still improves over the student baselines while cutting end-to-end GPU-hours by 59.4%--72.6% and halving peak GPU allocation, at benchmark-dependent accuracy. Furthermore, we extend the offline variant to corss-tokenizer scenarios: distilling GLM-4.5-Air from DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 raises its SWE-bench Pro and Multilingual resolve rate from 35.8% to 39.7% and from 41.8% to 46.2%, around 4% and 4.6% improvement, respectively. We also find that a decreasing loss, however, does not necessarily indicate improved agent performance: under top-$K$ reverse-KL loss, one student exhibits severe repetition despite a decreasing loss. We identify a support-mass gradient term as a potential mechanism underlying this failure.
title: SWE-OPD: On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Coding

summary: Delta debugging reduces a failing input by deleting chunks of it, keeping a deletion only if an oracle confirms the failure persists. It chunks the input based only on its length, so its deletions cut through units such as identifiers and delimited groups, wasting calls and leaving outputs large. Current state-of-the-art structural reducers avoid this by supplying grammars or built-in format knowledge. We show that structured reduction needs neither: a neutral word and delimiter pairs suffice, and both can be inferred from the failing input by asking only what delta debugging already asks its oracle: does the failure persist? A neutral word, such as a space, preserves the failure when inserted between such units but not inside them, so it splits the input into tokens. A delimiter pair is two tokens that preserve the failure only when added or removed together, so the span they bound can be reduced as a unit. We formalize both, state when the oracle can reveal them, and learn each with a bounded number of calls. AutoDiDact reduces the resulting tree of spans by hierarchical delta debugging (HDD) and shrinks each token across its occurrences. AutoDiDact finds a neutral word in 75 of 125 inputs from 18 format families. On these, it returns outputs 83% smaller than byte-level delta debugging with 37% fewer calls on geometric mean, inference included. The savings grow with input size, to 98% and 87% on inputs of at least 10 KiB. Without a grammar, AutoDiDact matches grammar-based HDD in output size at 3.85 times its calls, and uses 54% fewer calls than C-Reduce's language-agnostic mode. Because it needs only the oracle, AutoDiDact can minimize whatever a fuzzer finds, malformed inputs included.
title: AutoDiDact: Input Reduction over Inferred Structure

summary: While the ability of video generation models to accurately depict scientific phenomena has received growing attention, determining whether these models genuinely understand the underlying principles remains a critical challenge. Existing benchmarks typically evaluate video samples in isolation, making it difficult to expose models that simply fit superficial visual priors. In scientific experiments, a small change in one condition produces a markedly different outcome even when the rest of the setup remains fixed. Capitalizing on this sensitivity, we introduce SciWorldBench, a benchmark comprising paired scientific experiments. Each pair varies a single condition in an otherwise fixed setup, yielding two mutually exclusive expected outcomes. Each generation prompt specifies the condition but omits the expected outcome. We evaluate ten text-and-image-to-video (TI2V) models using an independent vision-language model (VLM) that assesses each video without access to the condition text or the label identifying the correct outcome. A pair is scored as correct only when both videos depict their respective scientifically correct outcomes. Across all ten models, we find that the two videos in an experimental pair frequently depict the same outcome even though the conditions require different results. This recurring failure suggests that current video world models struggle to apply the underlying scientific principles reliably during generation. We will publicly release the benchmark dataset and open-source the evaluation code.
title: SciWorldBench: Do Video World Models Really Understand Scientific Experiments?

summary: Agents are increasingly built to learn from experience: they keep conversation histories, memory files, retrieved notes and skills, and reuse what worked before. We show that this experience turns against them when their tools change silently. We test a range of models with tools defined as in the Model Context Protocol (MCP). After a silent change, experienced agents fail on most tasks, while agents new to the task mostly succeed. We call this failure Experience Rot. Experienced agents copy their earlier call instead of checking the current interface, even when the tool definition shows the change. Then they report success. When the documentation is incomplete, experience is what makes agents succeed. After a change, the same experience leaves them worse off than no experience at all. The failure appears in every form of memory we test and grows with the amount of experience. Simple remedies fall short: announcing the update barely helps, and pointing the agent to the documentation fails whenever the documentation does not spell out the answer.
title: Experience Rot: Experienced Agents Fail Where Novices Succeed

summary: Agent evaluations report task success and rarely say what an agent did at each decision. We score every decision node of three 12B to 14B instruct-tuned language models (LMs) playing five zero-sum imperfect-information games against four opponents on eight properties from decision and game theory, five of them against a CFR+ equilibrium reference. At each node, the LM also states a belief about the opponent's hidden state in a separate call. Without memory and at temperature 0, stated beliefs sit 0.250 to 0.288 in total variation distance from the equilibrium posterior, and where the action responds to the state its agreement with that belief exceeds chance by -0.04 to 0.19. The two calls frame the opponent differently, so the result is a behavioural inconsistency and makes no claim about internal beliefs. Under one prompt and greedy decoding, the LM's action never varies with the state in 10 of the 38 cells where the reference varies its own. Memory lowers the constant-action share in 9 of 13 testable ladders at temperature 0; at temperature 0.2 the cells at 1 fall from 16 to 5 of the 46 informative cells, while the belief results hold. A gate withholds, with a stated reason, any belief score the run cannot support, and seven of the eight non-zero defect rates are attributable to the instrument, a representation, or the LMs.
title: Instrumenting Failure: Scoring Language Model Agents at Every Decision Node in Imperfect-Information Games

summary: An agent that carries memory across tasks is only as good as the entries it keeps. We begin from an observation that is easy to reproduce and uncomfortable for the field: naively accumulating cross-task experience can make an agent \emph{worse} than one with no memory at all. On AgentBoard, a workflow-induction memory solves fewer tasks than a memoryless ReAct agent in seven of eight domains, and a per-step procedural store with no surrounding structure loses half of ReAct's completions on Jericho. We argue that the missing ingredients are per-action credit assignment and an explicit life cycle for stored entries, and present AdMem, which supplies both. Before each action the actor commits to an expected outcome; a concurrently running critic scores the realized outcome against that expectation and writes a procedural entry carrying a binary reward and a reflection, so credit lands on the action that earned it and no environment reward is required. Each entry then carries a scalar utility, updated online under a noisy-OR reward model, that ranks retrieval jointly with context similarity and drives eviction and merging, giving the store a forgetting and consolidation policy instead of unbounded growth. Across 707 tasks in eight AgentBoard domains AdMem solves 441 against 388 for ReAct and 312 for the workflow-induction baseline --- a pooled gain significant under a two-sided Fisher exact test, concentrated in the domains that supply transferable cross-task structure. All memory stays human-readable text, which is what makes the failures above diagnosable --- and, as we discuss, also makes the store an auditable but attackable surface.
title: AdMem: Expectation-Grounded Procedural Memory for Long-Horizon Task-Solving Agents

summary: Modern large language models (LLMs) increasingly support longer contexts and serve more concurrent requests, increasing both sequence lengths and batch sizes. Both trends increase KV-cache size and memory traffic during inference. KV-cache quantization reduces these costs, with recent approaches using codebook-based vector quantization to achieve extremely low bit widths. However, hardware constraints limit codebook size, and most methods reconstruct the cache in higher-precision floating-point formats for attention, limiting the computational benefits of quantization. To address these limitations, we introduce MiSTiQ, a drop-in replacement for codebook-based vector quantizers that combines trellis-coded storage with microscaling (MX) formats for low-precision computation. We combine trellis quantization with beam search to encode the KV cache over large reconstruction spaces without large codebooks. To support MX computation, we derive MX-Hash functions that generate reconstruction values directly in the target MX element format. These functions use the scale-conditioned marginal distribution of block-normalized Gaussian inputs. On Llama3 and Qwen3, MiSTiQ achieves lower WikiText perplexity and higher GSM8K accuracy than the evaluated baselines across several block-scale formats at approximately 1.25 effective bits per element. With NVFP4, it also achieves the highest LongBench average on both models.
title: MiSTiQ: MicroScaling Trellis Quantization for Extreme KV Cache Compression

summary: Gaia has observed every detected source on the sky 50 to 100 times, each time through a window of about 1 by 2 arcseconds at a different scan angle. The resulting one-dimensional flux profiles to be released in Gaia DR4 encode the two-dimensional arrangement of nearby point sources at ~0.1 arcsecond resolution. Repeated observations also constrain their relative motion. We present a method to model the scene with a mixture of moving point sources. Complementing Gaia DPAC's source-environment reconstruction, our approach focuses on close, blended companions and models their relative motion. We first fit each window with a few point sources and obtain their along-scan positions. We then triangulate these positions from different scan angles to identify candidate sources on the sky. A joint forward model of all windows measures positions, fluxes, relative proper motions, and parallax differences, even for blended components. In simulations, we recover companions at separations smaller than the instrumental profile width. For a moving companion at ~75 mas separation with a flux ratio of ~0.2, we obtain a separation precision of ~0.1 mas and a relative proper-motion precision of ~0.1 mas/yr per component, even in a scene contaminated by a third source. These precisions assume a known instrumental profile and independent Gaussian noise. We also recover differential parallax for a chance-aligned source. Modeling nearby contaminants prevents significant biases. With a Gaia-like instrumental profile, sampling and scan law, we show a sensitivity of ~5 mag in contrast at separations of 50-150 mas, and we discuss its dependence on the color term of Gaia's line-spread function. The method could extend the census of close companions and provide relative astrometry, and so dynamical information, along short orbital arcs. External measurements could also guide retrospective searches in Gaia's windows.
title: Gaia as a 0.1 arcsec point-source survey across the sky: dynamical scene reconstruction from one-dimensional scans

summary: A conformal surface that alternates between sectoral low scattering and directive telemetry poses a shared-hardware inverse problem when both modes must use one finite passive impedance alphabet, although their spatial codebooks may differ. This paper formulates and solves that mixed continuous--discrete problem at the effective impedance-boundary level. Reference-centered Tikhonov preimages prescribe restricted radiation data; inverse-source null-space freedom then moves each current within its data-equivalent class toward impedance profiles quantizable by the same alphabet. A line-searched Gauss--Newton update, common-state assignment and projected-centroid updates, and exact forward refinement determine the currents, two codebooks, and one passive library. Data invariance, the current-to-impedance differential, the optimal state update, monotonic mismatch reduction, and a forward perturbation bound are derived. A full-mutual-coupling two-dimensional TM study of a $4λ_0$-diameter cylinder uses 64 physical cells and one shared eight-state library. On a 256-unknown validation model, the worst power ratio over $\pm10^{\circ}$ monostatic sectors and incidence angles from $-30^{\circ}$ to $30^{\circ}$ is $-11.6$~dB relative to a PEC cylinder; telemetry directivity is 13.1~dB with $-13.6$-dB peak sidelobes and a $1^{\circ}$ pointing error. A separate Fourier--Galerkin formulation, converged through 513 complex modes without reoptimization, gives $-11.36$~dB and 13.02~dB for the corresponding worst-sector and directivity metrics. The results establish feasibility at the effective impedance-boundary level; they do not establish unit-cell, bias-network, or platform-level realizability.
title: Shared-State Inverse Synthesis of Dual-Mode Conformal Metasurfaces for Low Scattering and Telemetry

summary: Bug fixes Fixed caching of timing properties in Scan and Kymo with recent cachetools versions, where using cachedmethod beneath @property could raise TypeError: Decorating class methods is not supported . The fix preserves read-only access and invalidation when the instance cache is cleared. Fixed timestamp mismatches in PiezoTrackingCalibration , PiezoForceDistance and force-baseline fitting/correction with ForceBaseLine by cropping native force and trap-position channels to their shared time range before matching sample rates. Only complete averaging blocks are retained. Incompatible sampling grids now raise an informative error suggesting native channels instead of manually downsampled data. Fixed potential complex-to-real casting warnings in the kymotracker geometry tests by explicitly taking the real parts of reference eigenvalues and eigenvectors for real symmetric matrices. Also corrected assertion failure messages in the candidate-direction test. These are test-only changes. The geometry implementation and tracking results are unchanged. Ensured Scan.export_video() and ImageStack.export_video() use a Python integer for the default stop-frame index, improving compatibility when the frame count is a NumPy integer. This silences some warnings that pop up during testing. Fixed alignment of values in calibration tables for ForceCalibrationItem and CalibrationResults with tabulate 0.10 by explicitly preserving whitespace, while retaining compatibility with older supported versions.
title: lumicks/pylake: v1.8.1

summary: Recent megajoule laser inertial confinement fusion (ICF) experiments have demonstrated thermonuclear target gain above unity, yet scaling pulsed laboratory ignition to commercial 1–20 Hz Inertial Fusion Energy (IFE) power plants remains obstructed by six coupled physics and engineering bottlenecks: hydrodynamic Rayleigh–Taylor (RT) and Richtmyer–Meshkov instabilities, core contamination from mechanical target support tents and fill tubes, parasitic cross-beam energy transfer (CBET) and stimulated Brillouin/Raman backscatter (SBS/SRS), critical-density reflection and solid gold cone vaporization in petawatt fast ignition, dielectric mirror blistering and positive plasma pulse dispersion, and the absence of non-destructive focal-plane phase diagnostics in high vacuum. This paper presents an integrated theoretical and reactor-engineering solution derived from the Lorentz Invariant / Localized Intrinsic Field Equilibrium (LIFE) framework, governed by the exact four-dimensional covariant divergence of the Maxwell stress-energy tensor (∂ μ T μν = 0). By arranging subsets of N beam ≥ 4 coherent laser beamlines into mutually orthogonal pairs with quadratic sinusoidal cross-beam phase modulation, directional wave operators annihilate longitudinal radiation-drag force densities (f x = f z ≡ 0) while enforcing strictly forward longitudinal Poynting transport (S x, S z ≥ 0), eliminating coherent backscatter and replacing chaotic CBET with deterministic transverse Poynting routing. Along the mutual orthogonal axis, optical-cycle averaging via the Jacobi–Anger Bessel expansion establishes a stationary three-dimensional ponderomotive restoring lattice with zero net volume momentum bias, enabling both stalk-free high-vacuum cryogenic pellet levitation and dynamic RT shear damping during implosion. For fast-ignition architectures, orthogonal precursor guide beams induce an effective curved optical metric (n eff = c/v g > 1) forming an exponentially self-confined slow-light channel I core (r) = I 0 exp(−k|r|) that guides petawatt ignitor pulses directly into the stagnated fuel core without solid gold cones. Combined with coating-free corrugated monolithic bulk tungsten negative-dispersion wall optics and sub-millisecond vacuum three-beam differential interferometric and dual-divergence (∇·E, ∇·H) electro-optic feedback, the LIFE architecture provides a non-invasive upgrade path for existing megajoule and petawatt laser facilities as well as next-generation commercial IFE power plants. Keywords: Laser Inertial Confinement Fusion (ICF); Inertial Fusion Energy (IFE); Localized Intrinsic Field Equilibrium (LIFE); Fast Ignition; Rayleigh–Taylor Stabilization; Jacobi–Anger Ponderomotive Lattice; Cross-Beam Energy Transfer (CBET); Curved Optical Metric; Negative Group Delay Dispersion; Tungsten Plasma-Facing Optics PACS / PhySH: 52.57.-z (Laser inertial confinement); 52.57.Kk (Fast ignition of compressed cores); 52.38.-r (Laser-plasma interactions); 42.65.-k (Nonlinear optics); 52.35.Py (Macroscopic plasma instabilities) SSRN JEL Codes: Q42 (Alternative Energy Sources); O32 (Management of Technological Innovation and R&D); L94 (Electric Utilities); C61 (Optimization Techniques)
title: Three-Dimensional Synchro-Resonant Electromagnetic Confinement, Ponderomotive Rayleigh–Taylor Stabilization, and Cone-Free Slow-Light Fast Ignition in Multi-Beam Laser Fusion Reactors within the LIFE Framework

title: AetherHuman: Human Participation in Autonomous Agent Ecosystems

summary: Python code accompanying the manuscript "Thermal Mode Coupling and Identifiability Limits in Photothermal Diffraction Tomography". It implements the exact Ewald accessibility test, Fourier-chain harmonic and transient solutions of the heat equation with spatially varying conductivity, the first-order rank analysis, noise-scenario detection power, the positive-source counterexample and an independent finite-volume check. All calculations are analytic or synthetic; no measured data are included. Running analysis.py and expanded_figures.py reproduces all tables and figures of the manuscript.

summary: Python code reproducing all numerical results and figures of the manuscript “Certified First-Passage Bounds and Critical Failure-Time Scaling in Conserved-Pool Models of Mitotic Checkpoint Safeguards” (B. Ibrahim, submitted to SIAM Journal on Life Sciences). The scripts integrate the conserved-pool model of mitotic checkpoint safeguards, test the safety and failure certificates, compute the near-critical failure-time law and its constants, and calibrate static and feedback model variants to published single-cell timing data. The README maps each script to the result it produces. Single-cell times digitised from Kim et al. (bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.06.14.659703) are not redistributed; the scripts regenerate them from the preprint.
title: Certified First-Passage Bounds and Critical Failure-Time Scaling in Conserved-Pool Models of Mitotic Checkpoint Safeguards

summary: This database has eight zip files, each containing monthly netcdfs of daily 1/24-degree (~4 km) gridded counterfactual climate data for the western US. Variables represented are daily precipitation total (prec; mm), maximum and minimum temperature (tmax and tmin, respectively; degrees C), mean vapor pressure (hPa), mean 2-m wind velocity (m/s), mean downwelling solar and longwave radiation at the surfae (solar and longwave, respectively; W/m2), and surface pressure (hPa). The counterfactual dataset is meant to represent an alternative realization of the observed climate from 1951–2025 from which anthropogenic trends in background means and daily variances about those means have been removed. The observed climate dataset is available from https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19636838. Anthropogenic trends in background means and daily variances are estimatated to be represented by a weighted mean of trends simulated by 24 CMIP6 climate models under the historical (1850–2014) and SSP2-4.5 (2015–2100) scenarios. Trends in background means and daily variances are assessed relative to a baseline period of 1851–1900 (1851–1910 for daily variances). Model trends are weighted based on a combination of performance and independence following the ClimWIP method, where performace is assessed as agreement with the observed linear trend in global mean surface temperature from 1961–2025 and independence is assessed based on inter-model differences in maps of historical climatological mean surface air temperature and sea-level pressure. The methods used to produce the observational dataset, CMIP6 model weightings, and the counterfactual dataset are described in a manuscript submitted to Earth System Science Data. This dataset will be made publicly available upon publication of the corresponding paper.
title: Couterfactual version of 1/24-degree gridded daily observed climate for the western United States after removal of CMIP6 trends in background means and daily variances, 1951–2025

summary: These are audio recordings taken by an Eclipse Soundscapes (ES) Data Collector during the week of the April 08, 2024 Total Solar Eclipse.  It was decided to include only raw, unprocessed audio data files in each site-specific Zenodo record. This decision was so that any researcher can independently verify, reproduce, and extend the analysis performed. As a result, some sites have WAV files with 0 bytes of data or timestamps outside the range of probable recording times. Procedures used by the Eclipse Soundscapes team to process audio data for its purposes are outlined in the Data Management reports located in the Eclipse Soundscapes Zenodo community. Data with 0 bytes of data were included for completeness. When possible, all site-specific files, including the audio files, are included in a single zip file for ease of download. If a single zip file upload was not possible due to upload or bandwidth limitations, audio files are included in multiple zip files based on the day of the observation. summary: Positioning: PubMed stores scientific papers. ScientificClaims.org stores the evolving answers to scientific questions. The Scientific Claim Registry (SCR) is infrastructure for the memory of science — not its truth, consensus, or recommendations. It registers, it does not arbitrate . What v0.5 adds over v0.4: v0.4 made every evidence link independently verified. v0.5 is the first version in which the registry has been kept current by its own Layer 1 surveillance loop (retrieve → classify → dual-model verify → promote/corroborate → recompile → version), and it reports what that took, including where it failed. Growth through the loop, not manual curation. From v0.4 to v0.5 the lipedema pilot grew from 347 to 526 evidence claims and from 423 to 626 evidence records (895 question–claim links, 383 distinct DOIs) under the same 42 versioned questions. Sources: (1) an unattended weekly rotating contradiction sweep (R-AI-12), June–September 2026, pairing each topical retrieval with a null/negative/opposing-evidence pass; (2) a library-scale backfill re-running all 42 questions against the author’s curated lipedema library (4,563 structured records) plus Europe PMC. Verification across the registry: 614 verified, 5 disputed (kept and flagged), 7 unverified ; 19 records contradict the claim they sit under. Each changed answer received a new immutable version with a “what changed” note. Operational honesty. Unattended operation exposed failures a demo never shows, documented with the guarantees added: (a) eight silent weeks in which a missing LLM credential made every run fail while the rotation still advanced and logged the questions as swept — the rotation now advances only on successful runs, and a missing credential is a loud warning; (b) silently degraded semantic retrieval, now with keyword fallback and a self-started library service; (c) a malformed model response that discarded a whole run (atomic writes kept the registry intact), now parsed leniently on retry. A memory system that hides its own gaps contradicts its premise. Object model (unchanged). The scientific question (e.g. SQ-LIP-000007) is the primary navigable object. Underneath it, claims (SCR-LIP-000001) are structured, versioned units of evidence with an explicit role (supporting / contradicting / refines / context), PECO context, a GRADE rating, dated provenance, a change log, sentence-level provenance and an independent verification verdict. summary: Autonomous agents often reason and coordinate through labels that do not reveal which external information they denote. We present Sema, a content-addressed reference system for reasoning and communication that creates hash-based verifiable words: participants encode and hash information under an agreed representation, then reuse the content address as a term, optionally with a human-readable handle. Sema can use any representation if participants agree on how content is encoded, hashed, resolved, and decoded. This paper develops one concrete realization based on canonicalized JSON-compatible objects, field-level Merkle commitments, explicit identity rules, and content-addressed references. Full-reference verification establishes identity of the resolved hashed content, while semantic equivalence, correctness, and compliance remain separate questions. As a worked application of the Sema primitive, we introduce Pattern Cards, a concrete schema for deliberate, System 2-style reasoning. They make often-skipped reasoning moves explicit through contracts for mechanisms, conditions, invariants, typed dependencies, and failure modes. Within one agent, resolving a card can make a reusable reasoning procedure explicit. Across agents, the same content-addressed definitions support coordination: agents can verify that they resolved the same definitions; in strict mode, an enforced handshake halts on mismatch. A bootstrap library of more than six hundred cards demonstrates the design. Its contract fields averaged 26.7 times the tokens of short wire references—a transmission-compression result, not an inference-token saving, because definitions were hydrated before use. Illustrative agent demonstrations examine coordination behavior. The same primitive could support a Living Taxonomy of Thought; its utility, evolution, and governance remain open questions.
title: Sema: When the Hash Is the Word

summary: Standard nanoindentation analysis suppresses the time-dependent response of a tested material, discarding the property that governs how a heritage paint film survives climatic loading: its viscoplastic dissipation potential. We recover it, together with the elastic modulus, from a single displacement-controlled relaxation indent by Bayesian inverse identification through a Gaussian-process surrogate of a finite-element contact model. The central difficulty is that the constitutive law is adequate during relaxation but structurally violated during loading, where the particulate film deforms by granular compaction. Overweighting the loading forces the optimiser to absorb this model-form discrepancy into the constitutive parameters, leaving a deceptively good global fit. We expose this failure mode through a three-way audit of weighting schemes: expert-encoded physics, Fisher-information optimality, and a data-driven Empirical Bayes filter. Information-optimal weighting under model-form error produces the most biased parameters with an equally tight posterior, an effect we term Constitutive Overfitting. A polycarbonate control, for which the model is uniformly adequate, confirms that the three schemes converge, establishing the audit as a diagnostic of model inadequacy rather than a pipeline artefact. This work has two outcomes. The first is the complete viscoplastic dissipation potential of a heritage paint film, the rate-dependent descriptor that fracture and digital-twin models require, from a single high-information indent. The second is the audit: an unaudited inversion would report a tight posterior on a biased modulus, whereas the three-way comparison separates reliable parameters from artefacts wherever constitutive fidelity varies within a single experiment. Population-level variability is deferred to a forthcoming multi-indent study.
title: Regime-Aware Bayesian Identification of the Viscoplastic Dissipation Potential in Heritage Paint Films from Nanoindentation

summary: Methods that localise social bias in large language models to individual attention heads and remove it by ablation are validated by their effect on a fairness metric, never by evidence that the statistic selecting the heads measures bias. We audit this on Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. The head map correlates at $ρ= -0.950$ and $-0.768$ with a label-blind response-length map, apparently identifying a surface confound. An intervention that breaks the length-label coupling rejects this reading: with the prompt held fixed, response length explains 1% of the statistic's variance. What does explain it is prompt identity, at 64% of variance, in an ordering that is not monotonic in length. Within any fixed prompt the fairness label, response length and the presence of a protected-group token are collinear at $φ= 0.95$, partly by definition of the labelling rule, so no observational analysis can attribute the map to any of them, and no method in this family performs an experiment that could. The substantive claims fail independently: bias selectivity is not late-layer-concentrated on either model under either reference reading, and no head set we tested reduces the unfairness rate when ablated. Its complement, scored on the opposite label, reliably destroys refusal behaviour ($p = 2.7\times10^{-5}$), demonstrating that the pipeline detects effects at this scale.
title: What Does a Bias Head Measure? Non-Identifiability in Head-Level Bias Attribution

summary: This research archive presents a detailed continuum-model derivation of the electron anomalous magnetic moment g−2 within the electron sector of a broader common-continuum theoretical framework. It consolidates the historical Paper02 construction with the current Model113 formulation through A3.8328 and provides a complete derivational record of the intrinsic anomaly, second-normal residual dynamics, mechanical magnetic-current correction, gradient contribution, and the subsequently developed propagated electromagnetic-return channel. The current construction begins from the fixed electron structural parameter N2, the tangent-sector magnetic-current source, and the second-normal residual inventory Delta_infinity = 1 / [12 N2^2 (N2 - 1)]. The previously frozen mechanical magnetic correction is retained without modification. A distinct electromagnetic-return contribution is constructed through four separately typed factors: the electromagnetic-to-strong support ratio 1/N2, two-dimensional transverse spreading 1/(2 pi), the three-dimensional-to-two-dimensional ring-plane projection sqrt(2/3), and the inherited gradient enhancement 1 + 2/(pi N2). The resulting electromagnetic-return contribution is delta a_EM = Delta_infinity × (1/N2) × (1/2pi) × sqrt(2/3) × [1 + 2/(pi N2)]. Combining the inherited mechanical operator and the newly closed electromagnetic-return operator gives a_e = 0.0011596521805908756337882909101487… The archive explicitly preserves the earlier Paper02 precision-test failure rather than retrospectively rewriting the historical operator. The electromagnetic-return term was developed subsequently and is therefore reported as a new model-internal operator. Its close numerical agreement with the measured electron anomaly is treated as a retrospective consistency test rather than as a blind prediction. Particular attention is given to the provenance and physical identity of every factor, the separation of mechanical and electromagnetic readout channels, source-field-receiver typing, amplitude-versus-inventory distinctions, NoAlias constraints, NoDoubleCount constraints, and high-precision numerical reproducibility. The deposit contains the full derivation, historical operator record, Model113 provenance, numerical reproduction materials, formula freezes, and source-audit files intended to make the construction independently inspectable and reproducible.
tags: electron g-2; anomalous magnetic moment; electron magnetic moment; continuum model; Model113; second-order dynamics; electromagnetic return; electromagnetic feedback; magnetic moment; tangent-sector current; second-normal dynamics; two-dimensional diffusion; Gaussian propagation; finite-shell electron; unified continuum theory; precision physics; theoretical physics; reproducible derivation
title: A Continuum-Model Derivation of the Electron Anomalous Magnetic Moment (g−2): Model113, Second-Order Residual Dynamics, and Electromagnetic Return

summary: Source-code archive accompanying the manuscript "PFOA and PFOS leave distinct signatures in sex hormones and bone: population, genetic and molecular evidence from three NHANES periods" (version 15, 15 November 2026). Scope. The archive contains the analysis and plotting programs, the fixed analytical specifications, dependency information, a code-to-manuscript correspondence map, and a license. It does not contain participant-level data, GWAS extracts, expression matrices, fitted-model caches, manuscript documents, finished figures, supplementary workbooks, or build history. What version 15 changes. This is a language pass with no change to analysis code, parameters or results. The two protocol documents (analysis_protocol.md, bounded_review_protocol.md) were translated from Chinese into English; Chinese comments in 08_cellcomm.py, coloc_full_region.R, extract_outcomes.py, dl_eqtlgen.py, extract_regions.py and render_pdf_backend.py were rendered in English; and filenames of local working files cited by six build-utility scripts were transliterated, with a header note recording that those files are build history and are not distributed. No source line changed in meaning, and every manifest digest was recomputed. What version 14 changes. Colocalization for the expression-based instruments was recomputed, and the pipeline that produces the reported posteriors is included. The previous implementation, eqtl_mr_colocalization.py, is retained unchanged for provenance but is superseded: it carried the regional input as variants selected at FDR < 0.05 rather than the complete regional set, and it fixed the shared-variant prior at 1e-8 without exposing p12. Running it will not reproduce Table S17. The recomputation changed the reported posteriors, most visibly for ESR1 against FinnGen osteoporosis (PP.H4 8.6e-3 in the earlier implementation, 0.661 in version 14). The four programs added are dl_eqtlgen.py (resumable block download of the complete eQTLGen release), extract_regions.py (every tested SNP-gene pair within 1 Mb of each gene centre, with no significance filter), extract_outcomes.py (outcome signals matched by rsID, because FinnGen release 11 is on GRCh38 and eQTLGen on GRCh37) and coloc_full_region.R (coloc.abf with p1=p2=1e-4, p12=5e-6 varied over 1e-6 to 1e-5, all five posteriors reported). Contents. source/analysis/baseline holds the population, genetic, molecular and transcriptomic analyses, including direct-exposure checks and period and confounding comparisons. source/analysis/current holds the corrected indirect-association, WQS/BKMR and DXA-selection analyses with their fixed specifications, the version 13 programs, and the complete-region colocalization pipeline added in version 14. source/analysis/review_20261017 holds the sex-specific age models, corrected first-leg genetic estimates, reporting families and reviewed panel producers. source/analysis/clinical_extension holds the clinical DXA and endocrine-period comparisons. source/analysis/source_snapshot holds the molecular docking programs. figures/render_fig2.py generates the current 21-panel Figure 2. Correspondence. CODE_MAP.tsv links every current figure panel and supplementary location to the code that produces it (158 records). EXTERNAL_INPUTS.tsv records the expected paths, sizes and SHA-256 digests of the directly mapped external inputs (320 assets), which are supplied separately and are not redistributed here. FILE_MANIFEST.tsv records sizes and SHA-256 digests of the 204 archived files.
