summary: Action-Research Lessons Learned from a Dis|mis Administrative Incident This book is an action-research study of lessons learned from a dis|mis administrative incident . It uses the incident as a situated case through which to examine how administrative uncertainty, informational asymmetry, technological mediation, institutional inertia, and contested interpretation can affect cognition, expression, dignity, and public trust. The project is guided by the attached work’s progression from “Fundamental Rights At Risk” and “On Partiality” to “On Liberty of Thinking,” “On Inner Peace & Recensions,” “Introducing CogOps,” “On Cognitive Health,” and the case studies on judicial impartiality, private affiliations, oath conflict, and SIS–Schengen transparency. The table of contents therefore provides the project’s conceptual route: from rights and institutional balance, through cognition and inner life, towards administrative, technological, and governance risks. The research does not present the personal account as conclusive proof of intentional wrongdoing. Rather, it treats the incident as a source of lessons learned, research questions, provisional concepts, and methodological warnings . The purpose is to distinguish observed events from interpretation, allegation, metaphor, and hypothesis while asking how comparable vulnerabilities might arise in other administrative environments. From rights to cognition The first part of the research begins with fundamental rights and institutional impartiality. In the chapter “On Partiality,” the attached work states: “It is also relational: whenever you are judged, a relationship is involved.” This proposition provides an important starting point for action research. An administrative decision is not only a technical act; it occurs within a relationship involving a citizen, a public agent, an institution, a body of law, and a surrounding informational environment. A failure of communication, an absence of reasons, a delay, or an inability to challenge a decision can therefore produce effects extending beyond the immediate administrative matter. The same chapter gives a second guiding image: “We are all equal under gravity.” Here, the balance functions as a non-technical symbol of equality, impartiality, and the need to prevent power from becoming detached from rights. Within the proposed research, this image is translated into questions about procedural fairness, equal access to information, the visibility of relevant affiliations, and the ability of affected persons to participate meaningfully in decisions concerning them. Liberty of thinking The chapter “On Liberty of Thinking” provides the closest conceptual foundation for the study of inner ecology. It describes writing and symbolic expression as a means of creating distance from an overwhelming or difficult experience: “Being able to formulate, express, and work on things symbolically helps us create emotional distance.” This observation is central to the action-research design. Recension, writing, drawing, multilingual expression, and documentary reconstruction are not treated merely as literary devices. They are used as practical research instruments through which an individual experience can be reviewed, organised, questioned, and made accessible to others. The chapter also describes expression as a form of shelter: “It was therefore a genuine shelter to be able to express ourselves through this ‘way of the pencil.’” Adapted to a CERREV-oriented research programme, this becomes a question about the conditions under which citizens and public agents can formulate disagreement without escalation. The research therefore examines whether accessible forms of expression can reduce informational dissonance, support self-correction, and create a more reliable basis
title: THE ASYLUM : From Soft Corruption to Disruptive Cognitive Operations: Reaching Inner Peace

summary: Pycrograph is a GPLv3 Python desktop application for building publication figures from fluorescence microscopy images. Raw files (MetaMorph TIFF/STK) are registered by reference and never modified; every display setting (per-channel window, gamma, colour lookup table, orientation) is re-applied at render time. Provenance follows PysternBlot: SHA-256 source verification, hash-chained operation log and integrity reports.

summary: This publication specifies and documents a researcher-directed methodology for AI-assisted mathematical discovery, developed within the independent mathematical research program of Structural Stability Science (SSS). The methodology exhibits continuity with, but remains distinct from, the originating Structural Identification Method (SIM; Tonucci, 2026). It integrates scientific identification and continuing research direction, AI-assisted scientific interlocution, mathematical formalization and analytical development, computational implementation, dependency-preserving adjudication, and source-specific contribution provenance. Scientific interlocution consists of sustained technical exchange through which mathematical questions, interpretations, hypotheses, dependencies, counterexamples, proposed constructions, and candidate proof routes are examined. Researcher-directed decisions concerning problem selection, investigative objectives, mathematical evaluation, and research-program continuity remain distinguishable from AI-generated mathematical proposals, calculations, arguments, critiques, and technical representations. Both retain identifiable contributions under their documented source conditions. The methodology specifies two complementary records. The mathematical claim record preserves originating questions, hypotheses, conclusion scope, dependencies, supporting evidence, and verification findings. The source-to-contribution record preserves originating research-state continuity, earlier research artifacts, prompt-visible AI operations, researcher-directed decisions, branch reconciliation, attribution correction, and publication outcomes. These records retain distinct evidentiary functions. A prompt-response transcript documents operations expressed within an interaction; it does not independently establish the complete originating research state or the provenance of the continuing investigation. The originating mathematical investigation concerned order preservation under real extension, admissibility, counterexamples, and mathematical continuation. The documented research sequence subsequently encompassed adjoint observation gain, analytical extensions, exact reference-state rank, restricted Fourier observability, conditional Gramian transfer, time-dependent observability, high-frequency obstruction, nonlinear terminal-target correction, and Navier–Stokes continuation questions, together with the organization of Adjoint Gain Theory. These investigations retain their individual mathematical claims, source identities, verification conditions, and unresolved proof obligations. The scientific contribution is the specification and documented application of a researcher-directed methodology that preserves mathematical claim identity and research-process provenance while distinguishing scientific origination from substantive AI-assisted mathematical production. The publication does not independently certify the mathematical results of cited sources or amend the originating scientific identities, definitions, or conditions of SIM, SSS, or Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT). summary: 研究館藏/旗艦館藏 第241-250頁(共300頁) 科學的失敗、計量學和獨立證據的極限 旗艦13號裂變 | 第三卷 | 作者33 | STARLI研究設計工作版 v1.0 這十部研究設計專著從奈米量子失效物理學和重建的微型機器人取樣真理出發,探討了盲法生物感測、實驗室間轉移、不確定性預算、參考物質互換性、生產批次效應、污染溯源、漂移/生物學分離以及任務失敗分類等問題。它們提出的是可檢驗的實驗方案,而非觀察到的新科學定律或臨床結果。 這十個英文工作版本共包含7770頁,300幅數學圖版,820個章節開頭,4100篇單頁研究,2000個研究門戶和330個鳳凰答案胚胎。每個門戶都包含一封由三個部分組成的推測信——起源、極端外推和未來研究計劃——但不取代經過驗證的證偽和獨立的實物證據。結構數量並不能確立科學創新性。 研究單元 I · F241–F245 F241 奈米量子研究系統故障極限物理學-重點:光源老化與致動器卡死故障。直接證據:危險事件發生率 [h^-1]。在不轉移的情況下,透過單點重複性進行測試。探測器增益漂移是一個重要的競爭因素;如果釋放出存在危險缺陷的裝置,則拒絕發布。 F242 微型機器人取樣真實性重建的極限-重點:微通道壁吸附與吸附-解吸記憶。直接證據:樣品來源回收率[百分比]。對照紙質批次記錄和終點檢查進行測試。移液管體積誤差是潛在的競爭對手;如果物料平衡或來源不符,則拒絕放行。 F243 量子生物感測器盲測極限挑戰-重點:自旋相干參考替換與電荷態切換。直接見證:預期正確驗收率[百分比]。與標準統計製程控制(限值已凍結)進行比較測試。即時競爭者為微波拾取;如果第二個測試點無法重現鑑定結果,則拒絕發布。 F244 奈米機器人實驗室間環形比對的極限-重點:雷射波長轉移與微尺度熱探針偏移。直接驗證:絕對的站點間測量偏差[單位]。測試與單一站點重複性(無需轉移)的比較。實驗室溫度差異是重要的競爭因素;如果釋放出有危險缺陷的產品,則拒絕發布。 F245 微量取樣不確定度預算極限 — 重點:體積計量誤差與壁損不確定度。直接驗證:預期區間覆蓋率(百分比)。對照紙質批次記錄和終點檢定進行測試。液體表面張力是重要的影響因素;如果物料平衡或來源不明,則拒絕放行。     第二研究單元/證據、轉移與傳承 第二研究單元 · F246–F250 F246 量子感測器參考物質的可互換性極限測試-重點:基質依賴性結合和螢光團光漂白。直接證據:不可互換性偏差[單位]。採用標準統計製程管制和凍結限值進行測試。一個潛在的競爭因素是分析物濃度不符;如果第二個測試點無法重現鑑定結果,則拒絕放行。 F247 奈米機器人製造批次效應辨識的極限-重點:光刻掩模對準和塗層孔隙缺陷。直接驗證:未經篩選的合格批次良率(百分比)。在不轉移的情況下,與單點重複性進行比較測試。一個重要的競爭因素是後加工分類;如果釋放出有害缺陷,則拒絕放行。 F248 微流控採樣污染溯源極限 — 重點:管路吸附儲液槽與生物膜滯留。直接見證:正確的污染源分類[百分比]。對照紙質批次記錄和終點檢查進行測試。新鮮試劑污染是主要競爭因素;如果物料平衡或來源不明,則拒絕放行。 F249 量子感測器在極限情況下分離漂移和生物變化-重點:雷射頻率漂移和基質離子強度變化。直接驗證:訊號源區分準確率(百分比)。與標準統計製程控制(限值固定)進行比較測試。活體競爭物代表真實的分析物波動;如果第二個偵測點無法重現驗證結果,則拒絕放行。 summary: Abstract (it) Il corpus in esame decostruisce il mito dell'applicazione standardizzata della prospettiva albertiana a base quadrata nell'opera di Leonardo da Vinci, proponendo un paradigma metrico-modulare fondato su evidenze geometriche oggettive e falsificabili. Attraverso l'analisi tridimensionale dell'Annunciazione, dell'Adorazione dei Magi e dell'Ultima Cena, emerge una grammatica spaziale in costante evoluzione. Leonardo abbandona la rigida scacchiera per sviluppare un sistema di "righelli inseriti", evolvendo da una misurazione monodirezionale a un'architettura ritmica e stereometrica. Il metodo d'indagine, basato su tecniche di retro-ingegneria CAD e sul "banale aristotelico", dimostra come le proporzioni spaziali (dal modulo 4:3 ai ritmi polifonici 1:4:1 e 2:1:2) siano direttamente ricavabili dall'opera stessa. L'approccio restituisce spazi non solo misurabili, ma architettonicamente rimontabili e strutturati sulle misure umane, rigettando interpretazioni esoteriche o simbologie forzate. Abstract (en) The examined corpus deconstructs the myth of the standardized application of Albertian square-based perspective in the works of Leonardo da Vinci, proposing a metric-modular paradigm founded on objective and falsifiable geometric evidence. Through the three-dimensional analysis of the Annunciation, the Adoration of the Magi, and the Last Supper, a constantly evolving spatial grammar emerges. Leonardo abandons the rigid checkerboard to develop a system of "inserted rulers," evolving from a monodirectional measurement to a rhythmic and stereometric architecture. The investigative method, based on CAD reverse-engineering techniques and the "Aristotelian obvious," demonstrates how spatial proportions (from the 4:3 module to the 1:4:1 and 2:1:2 polyphonic rhythms) can be directly derived from the artwork itself. This approach yields spaces that are not only measurable but architecturally reassemblable and structured on human measurements, rejecting esoteric interpretations or forced symbolism.   Abstract esteso (IT) Il corpus Leonardo's CAD, Leonardo's Rulers, Leonardo's Score propone una rilettura unitaria di tre indagini nate separatamente ma convergenti verso una stessa ipotesi: Leonardo da Vinci non applica in modo meccanico la prospettiva albertiana a maglia quadrata, né se ne discosta episodicamente per errore o licenza, ma sviluppa progressivamente una propria grammatica spaziale metrico-modulare, verificabile a partire dall'immagine stessa. L'oggetto della ricerca non è una lettura iconografica complessiva delle opere, bensì la ricostruzione degli spazi dipinti come dispositivi misurabili, abitabili e rimontabili attraverso procedure geometriche esplicite. Il trittico mette in relazione tre momenti distinti di questa elaborazione: l’ Annunciazione come forma prototipica della “geometria inserita”, l’ Adorazione dei Magi come emersione di una griglia generativa 4:3 connessa al braccio fiorentino, e l’ Ultima Cena come approdo a una vera polifonia stereometrica, governata da un unico modulo capace di coordinare larghezza, altezza e profondità. In questa prospettiva, lo sviluppo dell’opera leonardesca appare come una sequenza coerente: da uno spazio ancora concentrato e leggibile attraverso pochi regoli incorporati, a un’architettura figurata sempre più complessa, immersiva e ritmica. Sul piano metodologico, il corpus assume come principio guida il “banale aristotelico”: partire esclusivamente da ciò che nel dipinto è visibile, misurabile e geometricamente controllabile, senza ricorrere a simbologie arbitrarie, geometrie occulte o sovrastrutture interpretative non falsificabili. Il metodo combina osservazione diretta delle tracce figurative, geometria inversa, retro-ingegneria CAD e verifiche di coerenza antropometrica, zoometrica e architettonica; il punto decisivo è che gli elementi pittorici — bugne
title: Leonardo's Spatial Grammar: A CAD Reverse-Engineering Analysis Corpus: Leonardo's CAD, Leonardo's Rulers, Leonardo's Score

summary: 88 synthetic 3D T1-weighted brain MRI volumes of healthy subjects , generated with a 3D denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM). This set (v0) was produced while replicating Basile et al., A Preliminary Study on Augmenting Neuroimaging data using a Diffusion Model (HC@AIxIA 2024), on a different hardware platform (4× NVIDIA H100 instead of 12× A100), using the original code, architecture and hyperparameters. The method and its evaluation are described in: G. Mallardi, F. Calefato, F. Lanubile, G. Logroscino, B. Tafuri, Diffusion Models for Neuroimaging Data Augmentation: Assessing Realism and Clinical Relevance , Journal of Medical Systems 49, 161 (2025). https://doi.org/10.1007/s10916-025-02300-1 Model and generation 3D UNet (MONAI Generative; channels [128, 128, 256], attention at the deepest level), 1000 diffusion steps, scaled linear beta schedule (0.0005–0.0195), Adam (lr 5×10⁻⁵), 400 epochs, effective batch size 24. Trained on 805 T1-weighted scans of healthy subjects (ADNI, NIFD, OASIS-1/2/3, PPMI), preprocessed with AssemblyNet (denoising, bias-field correction, affine registration to MNI, intensity normalization, skull stripping) and resized to 84×128×84. Sampling: 1000 steps, fp16, 4 random streams (seeds 100–103). Format NIfTI (.nii.gz), float32, 84×128×84 voxels, voxel size 1.90 × 1.70 × 2.15 mm, MNI space. PNG previews (three central slices per volume, plus mosaics) for browsing only. metadata.csv : per-volume seed, sampling settings, quality indices and memorization score. provenance.json : code commit, model hash, configuration. Quality and limitations No sample was discarded. 9 of 88 samples are flagged as low-signal ( qc_flag_low_signal ), i.e. non-converged denoising. Intensities are not calibrated to the training range (median maximum ≈ 0.5, negative values occur): normalize before use. The background is not exactly zero, unlike skull-stripped real scans. Reduced resolution (~2 mm): not suitable for fine-grained morphometry. Not for diagnostic use. Privacy For each synthetic volume, the Pearson correlation with the nearest training volume was computed. The maximum is 0.929, below the median of real validation scans against the training set (0.944): no synthetic volume is closer to a training scan than a typical unseen real scan is. Data sources Training data were obtained from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI, adni.loni.usc.edu), the Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI, ppmi-info.org), the Frontotemporal Lobar Degeneration Neuroimaging Initiative (NIFD, via LONI IDA) and OASIS (oasis-brains.org). File access is restricted to researchers holding valid data use agreements for these sources. Funding PNC "DARE – Digital lifelong prevention" (PNC0000002 – CUP B53C22006450001). See README.md for full details.
title: Synthetic 3D T1-weighted brain MRI generated with a 3D DDPM (replication set, v0)

summary: Oltre il Quadrato: La griglia 4:3 e la precisione architettonica nell’Adorazione dei Magi Il saggio propone un ribaltamento metodologico nell’analisi del disegno preparatorio per l’Adorazione dei Magi di Leonardo da Vinci conservato agli Uffizi. Superando la tesi tradizionale di una maglia prospettica a base quadrata, l’autore dimostra, attraverso l’uso di software CAD e tecniche di retro-ingegneria, come Leonardo abbia adottato una griglia di rettangoli in rapporto armonico 4:3. Questa scoperta non solo risolve storiche incongruenze visive — restituendo alle arcate delle scale la loro perfetta forma a tutto sesto coerente con la misura del “braccio fiorentino” — ma svela un’applicazione consapevole di geometrie legate al pentagono e alla sezione aurea. Il lavoro sottolinea il notevole rigore logico e matematico di Leonardo, trasformando quello che era ritenuto un errore prospettico in una sofisticata architettura della visione. L’analisi si sviluppa attraverso una sequenza di osservazioni visive direttamente leggibili sul foglio 436E, verifiche CAD e procedimenti di geometria inversa, concepiti come linee di evidenza indipendenti ma convergenti. Beyond the Square: The 4:3 Grid and Architectural Perfection in the Adoration of the Magi This study presents a methodological shift in the analysis of Leonardo da Vinci’s preparatory drawing for the Adoration of the Magi. Moving beyond the traditional assumption of a square based perspective grid, the author utilizes CAD software and reverse-engineering techniques to demonstrate Leonardo’s use of a rectangular grid with a 4:3 harmonic ratio. This discovery resolves long-standing visual inconsistencies, showing that the arches in the background regain their perfect semicircular form when aligned with this modularity, consistent with the Florentine braccio unit of measurement. Furthermore, the analysis reveals the deliberate application of pentagonal geometry and the Golden Ratio.   This research highlights Leonardo’s mathematical rigour, showing that what was previously perceived as a perspectival error is, in fact, a sophisticated architecture of vision.  The analysis unfolds through a sequence of direct visual observations readable on the Uffizi sheet, CAD-based verifications, and inverse procedures, conceived as independent yet convergent lines of evidence.  This study integrates direct visual evidence from Leonardo’s drawing with CAD-based verification and inverse geometric reasoning.   Keywords: Leonardo da Vinci, Adoration of the Magi, Perspective, 4:3 Grid, CAD Analysis, Florentine Braccio, Golden Ratio.
title: Leonardo's CAD - La Geometria Svelata / The Revealed Geometry (it/en)

summary: High-fidelity simulations generate spatiotemporal data that are difficult to obtain experimentally, yet their outputs are rarely ready for scientific machine learning. Cardiac electrophysiology (EP) exemplifies this challenge: data reside on anatomy-dependent volumetric meshes, propagation follows anisotropic material fields, and relevant events span multiple temporal scales. We introduce GraphEP, a calibrated data system that converts cardiac meshes and simulation protocols into compact, graph-native trajectories of full-field transmembrane potential. GraphEP includes 732 left-ventricular simulations across 20 anatomies, with healthy and scarred substrates of varying severity and multiple pacing configurations. Each sample provides geometry, tissue and material features, stimulation, connectivity, derived activation targets, and provenance in PyTorch Geometric format. We benchmark four inductive biases for predicting transmembrane potential Vm(t): local message passing, global neural operators, multi-scale hierarchical graph transformers (HGT), and physiology-informed models. The latter include HGT-Lag, which separates activation timing from action-potential morphology, and the stateful Graph Aliev-Panfilov Action-Potential ODE (GAP2ODE), which evolves excitation and recovery autoregressively with frame-wise stimulation and graph diffusion. Results show that wider spatial communication improves on local message passing, while physiological structure provides the strongest inductive bias: HGT-Lag and GAP2ODE lead on complementary metrics by explicitly modeling propagation, recovery, and temporal state. GraphEP offers a reproducible pathway from mechanistic cardiac EP simulations to analysis-ready data and a controlled benchmark for learning on irregular anatomical geometries.
title: GraphEP: A Calibrated Data System and Benchmark for Learning Cardiac Electrophysiology

summary: Current audio-driven video diffusion models can synthesize realistic talking-head videos but generally require dozens of diffusion denoising steps over multi-second video chunks, making them unsuitable for streaming applications such as voice assistants and virtual avatars, where low-latency and online causal generation are required properties. AURA generates video chunk by chunk with a rolling KV cache, requiring only the audio of the current chunk to start generating, rather than a multi-second audio look-ahead like bidirectional models. It comes in two sizes: AURA 1.3B streams 576p video in real time on a single GPU (20.7 fps for a 16 Hz playback rate), making it suited to interactive avatar applications, and AURA 5B streams 720p video at 9.7 fps. Our two-stage distillation pipeline first aligns the causal student with the teacher, by training it to match the teacher's trajectories with fewer diffusion steps and a chunk-wise sliding window causal attention mask, then applies Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD) with backward simulation to close the remaining quality gap. On standard talking-head benchmarks, AURA 1.3B runs 23x faster than its own bidirectional teacher and reaches a quality comparable to TalkVerse at a lower resolution, and AURA 5B matches its TalkVerse teacher at 720p while running 17x faster. To support reproducibility and further research on streaming avatar generation, we release the weights of both models along with a dataset of 30K synthetic videos and their precomputed teacher trajectories.
title: AURA: AUdio-dRiven streaming Avatar

summary: A benchmarking campaign provides the measurements behind an HPC performance study: code variants are built, swept over core or node counts, and measured repeatedly. Moving such a campaign to another supercomputer or rerunning it months later requires work that is not part of the study itself. Job scripts are adapted to each supercomputer, and what exactly ran is often reconstructed afterwards. We present Thinflow, a small Bash engine for organizing HPC benchmarking campaigns as rerunnable directory trees of tasks and runs. A task is a directory with a short shell script next to the code. For each sweep, one command builds the code, runs the benchmarks, and plots the results. Thinflow derives the execution order from declared dependencies and writes it to a plain-text manifest. Per-supercomputer profiles submit the runs to a workload manager such as Slurm. Each run writes a provenance record of its environment, hardware, and parameters. The engine ships inside the campaign directory, so a campaign stays rerunnable without installing a separate tool and, once completed, may serve as a paper artifact. In a case study, we ran one campaign with identical task files on three Slurm partitions of two supercomputers, on up to 16 nodes. This strong-scaling study of matrix multiplication in C/OpenMP, C/MPI, and Julia/MPI comprises 37 task files with 217 non-comment lines. Its 455 benchmark runs recorded what differed per partition, chiefly profiles and command-line parameters. This suggests that such a campaign needs little structure beyond plain shell files.
title: Thinflow: Organizing HPC Benchmarking Campaigns as Rerunnable Directory Trees

summary: Collective two-photon light--matter interactions enable pair amplification but can destroy spectral confinement, preventing a stable thermodynamic bright phase. We show that a positive Kac-scaled number-Kerr interaction renders the two-photon Dicke Hamiltonian of \(N\) emitters lower-bounded at all couplings while preserving its generalized \(\mathbb Z_4\) symmetry. We determine the exact zero-temperature thermodynamic energy density with \(O(N^{-1})\) finite-size control and obtain the global phase diagram. A bright minimum is born at a saddle-node and exchanges global stability with the normal minimum at coexistence, producing a discontinuous photon-density jump. Symmetry-resolved exact diagonalization through \(N=128\) supports the predicted density jump and an exponentially closing same-sector normal--bright tunneling gap. Spectral collapse thus becomes the singular zero-Kerr point of a first-order phase diagram, identifying a Hamiltonian route to stabilizing pair amplification.
title: Hamiltonian Stabilization of the Two-Photon Dicke Model

summary: LLM agents on long-horizon tasks fail in recurring, procedural ways. They mis-paginate an API, resolve the wrong entity, or answer when no answer was asked. We built a pipeline that lets an agent learn from its own history. It first mines short \emph{lessons} from the agent's own trajectories, one to three per episode. It then consolidates those lessons into a smaller set of \emph{guidelines}, where each guideline records how many lessons it merged. At inference the agent receives either all guidelines or a selected subset. The pipeline ships in the open-source altk-evolve library and is deployed in IBM's CUGA agent and watsonx Orchestrate platform. We report what we learned building, measuring, and productizing it. Our primary instrument is the AppWorld benchmark, across models spanning 40--92\% baseline task completion. The central finding is that the right amount of memory is a property of the model, not the memory. A strong model keeps improving as guidelines are added. DeepSeek-V3.2 gains +9.5 points of task completion and +16.1 points of scenario completion with its full 191-guideline set. A weak model gains less from the same full set than from a small selected subset. gpt-oss-120b starts at 39.9\% task completion. It reaches 51.2\% with all 199 of its guidelines but 55.4\% (mean of two runs) with a selected subset of about 29. Around that result we report what went wrong: a high-support guideline that backfired, provenance silently dropped during consolidation, a swallowed API error that failed every task while producing a plausible log, and a baseline confound that nearly produced a misleading comparison with a prior method. We distill these into recommendations for teams deploying agent memory.
title: How Much Should an Agent Remember? Deployment Lessons from Self-Distilled Memory for LLM Agents

summary: Diffusion distillation accelerates image and video generation by compressing a pretrained teacher's iterative sampling process into a few network evaluations. Distribution-based methods achieve this by matching the student's output distribution to the teacher's. This matching is often driven by reverse-KL objectives, whose mode-seeking bias favors dominant teacher modes at the expense of diversity across samples. We introduce Posterior Matching Distillation (PMD), a new member of the distribution-based distillation family that combines mode-covering posterior sampling with any-step generation. At zero population loss, PMD recovers the teacher's full posterior of clean images at each trained noise level. Its stochastic student supports any-step sampling budgets within the trained timestep grid without further training. To learn these posteriors, PMD matches exponentially reweighted averages of student samples conditioned on a fixed noisy state to corresponding teacher posterior means. Under Gaussian corruption, exponentially tilted posterior mean is a single teacher evaluation at a shifted input. We prove that, matching tilted means over an open neighborhood uniquely identifies the full posterior. PMD thus supervises the entire conditional distribution through a family of mean constraints, without any auxiliary student-score network. Experiments on SDXL and FLUX.2 [klein] 4B demonstrate that PMD achieves the best FID among 4-step methods on both models, while maintaining competitive or leading performance across prompt-alignment and perceptual-quality metrics.
title: Posterior Matching Distillation

summary: We consider a system of branching Brownian particles on the real line with bounded, possibly discontinuous drift $b$, and with a selection rule that removes one particle from the most crowded cells of a uniform partition of the line at each branching event so that the number of particles is preserved. As the number of particles tends to infinity, with the cell size tending to zero (sufficiently slowly), we prove convergence in probability of the empirical measure process to a deterministic limit characterized by the parabolic free obstacle problem $$\partial_tu=\tfrac12\partial_{xx}u-\partial_x(bu)+u-β.$$ Here the density $u$ has unit mass. Disintegrating the removal measure $β$ as $β_t(\mathrm{d} x)\mathrm{d} t$, the probability measure $β_t$ is supported on the spatial maximizers of $u(t,\cdot)$ for a.e. $t$. We establish existence and uniqueness of weak solutions in a suitable class of continuous densities, extending earlier results about this PDE to discontinuous drifts. We then consider an inverse problem: Given a target removal measure, find a drift for which the PDE admits a stationary solution with that removal measure. We show that this problem is solvable for every compactly supported Borel probability measure.
title: Trimmed Branching Brownian Motion with Discontinuous Drift

summary: In this study, we compare the asymptotic efficiency of three closed-form estimators of the Dirichlet shape parameters. We start by proving that, in the beta distribution, the score-adjusted moment estimator (SA) has strictly smaller componentwise asymptotic variances than the usual moment estimator (M1) for both parameters. We then introduce a new moment estimator (M2) that combines the marginal moment equations to obtain a common estimate of the total concentration. M2 coincides with M1 in the beta case and has strictly smaller componentwise asymptotic variances for every positive shape vector in three or more dimensions. We then show that SA is asymptotically more efficient than M2 when all shape parameters are equal; if at least two parameters differ, each estimator has smaller asymptotic variance than the other for some linear combination of the parameters. Furthermore, SA has strictly smaller componentwise asymptotic variances than M2 when all shape parameters are at least 1. Finally, we show that this ordering can reverse if a parameter becomes too small, and obtain relevant mathematical and computational bounds. Overall, the study shows that, for the Dirichlet distribution and under a broad range of parameter settings, score-adjusted estimation outperforms the classic moment estimation and identifies the limits of that advantage.
title: Asymptotic efficiency comparison of explicit Dirichlet shape estimators

summary: Many paired image-to-image translation tasks admit multiple valid target appearances, while training provides only one target per source. We propose One-to-Many Flow (O2MFlow), a latent-conditioned Rectified Flow (RF) model for one-to-many generation and backward translation (target$\rightarrow$source) within a single transport framework. Conditioning the RF dynamics on an appearance latent turns transport into a family of latent-indexed bijections: a fixed latent gives a mapping that is inverted by time-reversed integration, and sampled latents produce diverse outputs for the same input. We formalize reusable appearance variations as Shared Latent Transport and show that Kullback--Leibler (KL) regularization directly controls the source--latent distribution gap between training and generation. Across three benchmarks, O2MFlow offers dataset-dependent forward diversity--fidelity trade-offs and the lowest backward LPIPS-Dist among evaluated methods, with the lowest backward FID on two benchmarks.
title: One-to-Many: Diverse and Bidirectional Image-to-Image Translation via Rectified Flow

summary: MATLAB implementation of the interleaver evaluation suite of 'A Code-Aware Evaluation Framework for Interleavers Under Burst Errors: Metric Taxonomy, Validation, and Parameter Provenance': canonical interleaver implementations with declared parameter rules, the length-grid generator, precomputed permutation tables, the metric implementations, the simulation harness, the drivers of the five further campaigns, and the analysis scripts that regenerate every table and figure of the article and its Supplementary Material. Release 1.1.0 adds the shortened Reed-Solomon code, the further-campaign modes and drivers, the permutations at their lengths, and their analysis; no number of the primary campaign changes. The campaign data are archived separately (see related identifiers).

summary: In 1513 the Castilian Crown began directing its conquistadors to read aloud the Requerimiento, a legal demand that the Indigenous peoples of the Americas submit at once to the authority of the Pope and the Spanish monarch. Composed by the jurist Juan López de Palacios Rubios, it was recited in Spanish or Latin, often out of earshot and to communities with no means of grasping its terms, and yet refusal, or the mere inability to consent, was treated as lawful grounds for war and enslavement. For the Taíno of the Caribbean it was the purest instrument of weaponized information asymmetry: a choice demanded under conditions that made informed choice impossible. This article formalizes the structural inverse of that instrument. It proposes a formal model of a peer-recognition currency in which the unit of account is perceived contribution value, issuance is fully endogenous, no sovereign intermediary exists, and the exchange space is structured by context-tagged domains rather than a flat signal architecture. The model's central claim is that when a boundedly rational agent simultaneously optimizes for accumulation, because a high balance signals competence and influence, and for expenditure, because high spending signals piety, humility, and reciprocal embeddedness, the resulting equilibrium is altruistic in the behavioral sense, not because altruism is designed into the incentive structure but because it is the only stable solution to the dual-motive optimization problem in a peer network with an observable ledger. A novel institutional role is defined: the epistemic witness, which informs without judging and without suggesting, preserving full independent agency while eliminating the information asymmetry between a participant and their own recognized contribution record. Where the Requerimiento compelled assent to terms that could not be read, the witness makes the terms of recognition fully legible to the participant before they act. The model is situated within the intersecting literatures of mechanism design, social epistemology, signaling theory, gift economy, commons governance, social compact theory, and cognitive behavioral economics. A candidate validation architecture is identified in which the model's predictions are falsifiable, and a formal appendix establishes the equilibrium result as a subgame-perfect Nash equilibrium under perfect public monitoring. The paper concludes that the architecture described represents a distinct class of social exchange institution whose properties cannot be derived from any existing system and whose emergence of altruism as a structural rather than moral outcome has implications beyond the design of digital platforms.
title: E-Karma: A Formal Model of Peer-Recognition Currency, Dual-Motive Optimization, and the Structural Emergence of Altruism

summary: Replication package for The Temporal Validity of Taxonomic Entailments in Evolving Biomedical Ontologies . It contains the entailment survival corpus (929,486 lifetimes of derived taxonomic entailments reconstructed from 311 release snapshots of eight OBO Foundry and Library ontologies), per-release provenance identified by commit hash and release date, the extraction and analysis code, and every result table and figure reported in the article. Two verification scripts recompute the survival, attribution, Cox, predictive-model and re-verification results from the corpus (145 assertions) and check every table cell and quoted quantity in the manuscript against the released outputs (649 assertions).
title: Replication package for The Temporal Validity of Taxonomic Entailments in Evolving Biomedical Ontologies

summary: Extending Spezia's determinant result (2018), we prove his two conjectures in OEIS A322844, Comments, the two statements in the conjectures block (revision 68, August 23, 2025): the absolute second exterior trace of the serpentine matrix is the stated quartic quasipolynomial, and every exterior trace of order greater than two vanishes. The matrix has rank exactly two for every size at least two. A factorization through a two-dimensional space gives its characteristic polynomial, including the sign of the second exterior trace. Corollaries give a minimal polynomial, a permanent formula, diagonal sums, generating functions and reciprocal sums. We distinguish the exponential generating function from a shifted-factorial expression in the source.
title: Rank-two extensions of Spezia's 2018 determinant result: the two conjectures in OEIS A322844, Comments (revision 68)

summary: Purpose: This study aims to examine the temporal structure of naval platform procurement rivalry between Türkiye and Greece during 1990–2025. By analysing the reciprocal relationships between naval platform deliveries and international orders in both countries, it investigates the lags at which procurement activities become most pronounced and the role of major naval procurement programmes in shaping these relationships. Method: Annual naval platform delivery and international order series compiled from SIPRI for 1990–2025 were analysed using ordinary least squares (OLS) models with 0–3-year lags and Newey–West standard errors. The findings were assessed through common-sample, full first-difference, distributed-lag, military expenditure control, order-date sensitivity, and period-window analyses, complemented by changes in fleet tonnage from the Power at Sea 2.0 dataset. Findings: In the baseline models, Greek deliveries are positively associated with Turkish deliveries two years later (β = 0.427) and Turkish orders one year later (β = 0.636), while Turkish deliveries are positively associated with Greek orders three years later (β = 0.395; BH-adjusted p < 0.05). All three selected coefficients remained positive after controlling for military expenditure, although their statistical support weakened following BH adjustment. Excluding the period corresponding to the MEKO-200 delivery window reduced the H1 coefficient to 0.102. In the full first-difference models, the H1 relationship persisted, whereas the order-related relationships were sensitive to the transformation. Conclusion: The strongest lagged association in Turkish–Greek naval procurement was observed between Greek ship deliveries and subsequent Turkish orders. This finding is consistent with Richardson’s action–reaction approach and Jervis’s security dilemma framework, which underpin the study’s theoretical perspective. The study demonstrates that naval procurement rivalry between the two countries exhibits asymmetric relationships in terms of direction and timing, particularly across the order and delivery stages.
title: The Temporal Structure of Turkish–Greek Naval Procurement Rivalry: Orders and Deliveries (1990–2025)

summary: On 20 November 2026 L. Alpöge posted a four-page note and a Lean 4 archive claiming a derivation of Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis: 175,187 files, 17.4 million lines, the three standard axioms, no human-readable proof. We read the archive against the one-bit normal form of the Riemann Hypothesis, public in our git repository since October 2026 in Lean and since August 2026 in prose. The headline is Mathlib's own statement. Its last step is the band reduction our Lean record states as one face of the normal form. Everything in it except one proposition was in our public Lean record first, and that proposition is the bit our record isolated and printed as its only premise. Its premise is the definition of ζ, which a law of logic proved in our file classifies as strictly stronger than the value, so the derivation is a tautology of that premise. A second Lean test shows the standard axioms cannot carry the bit: if the archive stands, the bit came out of ζ, through a window estimate on Tate–Shafarevich lengths that holds every program-generated proof in the archive. Both seals build silently in core Lean 4.19.0 and are printed whole. We close with a provenance ledger and a critique of the artifact as published.
title: The Bit in the Definition: A Lean Derivation of the Riemann Hypothesis, Its Tautology, and the Public Record It Lands In

summary: Action-Research Lessons Learned from a Dis|mis Administrative Incident This book is an action-research study of lessons learned from a dis|mis administrative incident . It uses the incident as a situated case through which to examine how administrative uncertainty, informational asymmetry, technological mediation, institutional inertia, and contested interpretation can affect cognition, expression, dignity, and public trust. The project is guided by the attached work’s progression from “Fundamental Rights At Risk” and “On Partiality” to “On Liberty of Thinking,” “On Inner Peace & Recensions,” “Introducing CogOps,” “On Cognitive Health,” and the case studies on judicial impartiality, private affiliations, oath conflict, and SIS–Schengen transparency. The table of contents therefore provides the project’s conceptual route: from rights and institutional balance, through cognition and inner life, towards administrative, technological, and governance risks. The research does not present the personal account as conclusive proof of intentional wrongdoing. Rather, it treats the incident as a source of lessons learned, research questions, provisional concepts, and methodological warnings . The purpose is to distinguish observed events from interpretation, allegation, metaphor, and hypothesis while asking how comparable vulnerabilities might arise in other administrative environments. From rights to cognition The first part of the research begins with fundamental rights and institutional impartiality. In the chapter “On Partiality,” the attached work states: “It is also relational: whenever you are judged, a relationship is involved.” This proposition provides an important starting point for action research. An administrative decision is not only a technical act; it occurs within a relationship involving a citizen, a public agent, an institution, a body of law, and a surrounding informational environment. A failure of communication, an absence of reasons, a delay, or an inability to challenge a decision can therefore produce effects extending beyond the immediate administrative matter. The same chapter gives a second guiding image: “We are all equal under gravity.” Here, the balance functions as a non-technical symbol of equality, impartiality, and the need to prevent power from becoming detached from rights. Within the proposed research, this image is translated into questions about procedural fairness, equal access to information, the visibility of relevant affiliations, and the ability of affected persons to participate meaningfully in decisions concerning them. Liberty of thinking The chapter “On Liberty of Thinking” provides the closest conceptual foundation for the study of inner ecology. It describes writing and symbolic expression as a means of creating distance from an overwhelming or difficult experience: “Being able to formulate, express, and work on things symbolically helps us create emotional distance.” This observation is central to the action-research design. Recension, writing, drawing, multilingual expression, and documentary reconstruction are not treated merely as literary devices. They are used as practical research instruments through which an individual experience can be reviewed, organised, questioned, and made accessible to others. The chapter also describes expression as a form of shelter: “It was therefore a genuine shelter to be able to express ourselves through this ‘way of the pencil.’” Adapted to a CERREV-oriented research programme, this becomes a question about the conditions under which citizens and public agents can formulate disagreement without escalation. The research therefore examines whether accessible forms of expression can reduce informational dissonance, support self-correction, and create a more reliable basis
title: THE ASYLUM : From Soft Corruption to Disruptive Cognitive Operations: Reaching Inner Peace

summary: Pycrograph is a GPLv3 Python desktop application for building publication figures from fluorescence microscopy images. Raw files (MetaMorph TIFF/STK) are registered by reference and never modified; every display setting (per-channel window, gamma, colour lookup table, orientation) is re-applied at render time. Provenance follows PysternBlot: SHA-256 source verification, hash-chained operation log and integrity reports.
title: Pycrograph

summary: This publication specifies and documents a researcher-directed methodology for AI-assisted mathematical discovery, developed within the independent mathematical research program of Structural Stability Science (SSS). The methodology exhibits continuity with, but remains distinct from, the originating Structural Identification Method (SIM; Tonucci, 2026). It integrates scientific identification and continuing research direction, AI-assisted scientific interlocution, mathematical formalization and analytical development, computational implementation, dependency-preserving adjudication, and source-specific contribution provenance. Scientific interlocution consists of sustained technical exchange through which mathematical questions, interpretations, hypotheses, dependencies, counterexamples, proposed constructions, and candidate proof routes are examined. Researcher-directed decisions concerning problem selection, investigative objectives, mathematical evaluation, and research-program continuity remain distinguishable from AI-generated mathematical proposals, calculations, arguments, critiques, and technical representations. Both retain identifiable contributions under their documented source conditions. The methodology specifies two complementary records. The mathematical claim record preserves originating questions, hypotheses, conclusion scope, dependencies, supporting evidence, and verification findings. The source-to-contribution record preserves originating research-state continuity, earlier research artifacts, prompt-visible AI operations, researcher-directed decisions, branch reconciliation, attribution correction, and publication outcomes. These records retain distinct evidentiary functions. A prompt-response transcript documents operations expressed within an interaction; it does not independently establish the complete originating research state or the provenance of the continuing investigation. The originating mathematical investigation concerned order preservation under real extension, admissibility, counterexamples, and mathematical continuation. The documented research sequence subsequently encompassed adjoint observation gain, analytical extensions, exact reference-state rank, restricted Fourier observability, conditional Gramian transfer, time-dependent observability, high-frequency obstruction, nonlinear terminal-target correction, and Navier–Stokes continuation questions, together with the organization of Adjoint Gain Theory. These investigations retain their individual mathematical claims, source identities, verification conditions, and unresolved proof obligations. The scientific contribution is the specification and documented application of a researcher-directed methodology that preserves mathematical claim identity and research-process provenance while distinguishing scientific origination from substantive AI-assisted mathematical production. The publication does not independently certify the mathematical results of cited sources or amend the originating scientific identities, definitions, or conditions of SIM, SSS, or Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT). summary: This deposit contains synthetic benchmark inputs, mathematical specifications, computational artifacts, saved results, and validation materials supporting the manuscript “Evaluating Delivery-Fee Policies in Omnichannel Retailing with Integrated Fulfillment and Last-Mile Routing.” The materials are organized into two distinct evidence streams. The expected-demand stream contains the five-group benchmark inputs and the archived computational materials used for the fixed-price operational model and the separate descriptive ALNS-LP/Hybrid comparison on generated instances. The realized-order stream documents Construction A, in which customer choices are frozen as indivisible 0.5-order-equivalent orders and vehicle routes are represented over physical address–slot visits. It compares only tariff policies B and C across baseline and low-Store-inventory scenarios using 500 paired replications (2,000 MILP solves in total). All benchmark data are synthetic. No real customer records, personally identifiable information, or confidential retailer data are included. The expected-demand and realized-order formulations are complementary but are not algebraically equivalent. The 52-policy finite comparison belongs to the expected-demand formulation; the realized-order experiment compares only B and C and does not re-evaluate all 52 policies. Net delivery contribution (NDC) excludes merchandise margins and should not be interpreted as total retailer profit. The archived computational outputs and validation materials are preserved as saved evidence. Their inclusion does not mean that the historical experiments were rerun during deposit preparation. Title clarification: The current manuscript supported by this deposit is titled “Evaluating Delivery-Fee Policies in Omnichannel Retailing with Integrated Fulfillment and Last-Mile Routing.” The legacy expected-demand package contains a historical manuscript-context file bearing an earlier working title (version v0.3, dated 13 November 2026, explicitly marked “Not for submission”). This file is retained solely as historical provenance for the earlier computational evidence and does not represent the current manuscript or its title.
title: Research Data and Computational Materials for: Evaluating Delivery-Fee Policies in Omnichannel Retailing with Integrated Fulfillment and Last-Mile Routing

summary: This deposit contains synthetic benchmark inputs, mathematical specifications, computational artifacts, saved results, and validation materials supporting the manuscript “Evaluating Delivery-Fee Policies in Omnichannel Retailing with Integrated Fulfillment and Last-Mile Routing.” The materials are organized into two distinct evidence streams. The expected-demand stream contains the five-group benchmark inputs and the archived computational materials used for the fixed-price operational model and the separate descriptive ALNS-LP/Hybrid comparison on generated instances. The realized-order stream documents Construction A, in which customer choices are frozen as indivisible 0.5-order-equivalent orders and vehicle routes are represented over physical address–slot visits. It compares only tariff policies B and C across baseline and low-Store-inventory scenarios using 500 paired replications (2,000 MILP solves in total). All benchmark data are synthetic. No real customer records, personally identifiable information, or confidential retailer data are included. The expected-demand and realized-order formulations are complementary but are not algebraically equivalent. The 52-policy finite comparison belongs to the expected-demand formulation; the realized-order experiment compares only B and C and does not re-evaluate all 52 policies. Net delivery contribution (NDC) excludes merchandise margins and should not be interpreted as total retailer profit. The archived computational outputs and validation materials are preserved as saved evidence. Their inclusion does not mean that the historical experiments were rerun during deposit preparation. Title clarification: The current manuscript supported by this deposit is titled “Evaluating Delivery-Fee Policies in Omnichannel Retailing with Integrated Fulfillment and Last-Mile Routing.” The legacy expected-demand package contains a historical manuscript-context file bearing an earlier working title (version v0.3, dated 13 November 2026, explicitly marked “Not for submission”). This file is retained solely as historical provenance for the earlier computational evidence and does not represent the current manuscript or its title.

summary: AQUA-PRITHVI v2 expands the previously published metadata-only aquatic Harmonized Landsat and Sentinel-2 (HLS) corpus into a reusable multispectral research dataset, accompanied by harmonized in situ water-quality observations and reproducibility tools. The aquatic HLS corpus comprises 29,079 original compressed NPZ microshards containing 169,907 materialized patch-period samples. A quality-controlled catalog identifies 169,429 approved observations from 2,389 spatial patches across eight global regions during 2018–2024. Each approved observation references six HLS reflectance bands (blue, green, red, narrow NIR, SWIR1, SWIR2), 224 × 224 pixels at 30 m spatial resolution, together with valid-pixel and water masks. Spatially independent train, validation and test partitions are provided. The original NPZ archives may also contain excluded observations; only records identified as approved in the accompanying catalog should be treated as quality-controlled samples. The companion water-quality dataset integrates 2,107,785 harmonized observations from CONAGUA RENAMECA (Mexico) and AquaMatch (United States and territories), covering chlorophyll-a, total suspended solids, turbidity and water transparency where available. Source provenance, measurement units, censoring information and quality indicators are preserved. The release also provides Python tools for reading HLS tensors, preparing candidate water-quality labels and planning satellite-scene searches. These tools support the future construction of reproducible HLS–in situ matchup datasets. Important limitation: The harmonized in situ observations are not yet paired with satellite scenes. The monthly HLS composites used for aquatic domain-adaptive pretraining must not be interpreted as same-day satellite matchups. Valid supervised matchups require independent scene-level temporal matching, radiometric quality control and spatially independent evaluation. This resource is intended to support aquatic remote sensing, self-supervised representation learning, reproducible geospatial machine learning and research on satellite-based water-quality assessment. Original datasets retain their respective provenance, attribution and reuse conditions. summary: In 1513 the Castilian Crown began directing its conquistadors to read aloud the Requerimiento, a legal demand that the Indigenous peoples of the Americas submit at once to the authority of the Pope and the Spanish monarch. Composed by the jurist Juan López de Palacios Rubios, it was recited in Spanish or Latin, often out of earshot and to communities with no means of grasping its terms, and yet refusal, or the mere inability to consent, was treated as lawful grounds for war and enslavement. For the Taíno of the Caribbean it was the purest instrument of weaponized information asymmetry: a choice demanded under conditions that made informed choice impossible. This article formalizes the structural inverse of that instrument. It proposes a formal model of a peer-recognition currency in which the unit of account is perceived contribution value, issuance is fully endogenous, no sovereign intermediary exists, and the exchange space is structured by context-tagged domains rather than a flat signal architecture. The model's central claim is that when a boundedly rational agent simultaneously optimizes for accumulation, because a high balance signals competence and influence, and for expenditure, because high spending signals piety, humility, and reciprocal embeddedness, the resulting equilibrium is altruistic in the behavioral sense, not because altruism is designed into the incentive structure but because it is the only stable solution to the dual-motive optimization problem in a peer network with an observable ledger. A novel institutional role is defined: the epistemic witness, which informs without judging and without suggesting, preserving full independent agency while eliminating the information asymmetry between a participant and their own recognized contribution record. Where the Requerimiento compelled assent to terms that could not be read, the witness makes the terms of recognition fully legible to the participant before they act. The model is situated within the intersecting literatures of mechanism design, social epistemology, signaling theory, gift economy, commons governance, social compact theory, and cognitive behavioral economics. A candidate validation architecture is identified in which the model's predictions are falsifiable, and a formal appendix establishes the equilibrium result as a subgame-perfect Nash equilibrium under perfect public monitoring. The paper concludes that the architecture described represents a distinct class of social exchange institution whose properties cannot be derived from any existing system and whose emergence of altruism as a structural rather than moral outcome has implications beyond the design of digital platforms.
title: E-Karma: A Formal Model of Peer-Recognition Currency, Cross-Domain Enforcement, and Structural Altruism

summary: In 1513 the Castilian Crown began directing its conquistadors to read aloud the Requerimiento, a legal demand that the Indigenous peoples of the Americas submit at once to the authority of the Pope and the Spanish monarch. For the Taíno of the Caribbean it was the purest instrument of weaponized information asymmetry: a choice demanded under conditions that made informed choice impossible. This article formalizes the structural inverse of that instrument. It proposes a formal model of a peer-recognition currency in which the unit of account is perceived contribution value, issuance is fully endogenous, no sovereign intermediary exists, and the exchange space is structured by context-tagged domains rather than a flat signal architecture. summary: Replication package for The Persistence of Taxonomic Entailments in Evolving Biomedical Ontologies. Version 2 rebuilds the study on every official release of nine OBO ontologies (698 releases of SO, PATO, HP, DOID, CL, ENVO, OBA, UBERON and MONDO; 872,217 incident entailments) and analyses 250 Gene Ontology releases separately. It contains the release lists with their provenance, the entailment survival corpora, the extraction and analysis code, all result tables and figures, the HPO annotation file and both code sets of the qualitative sample. The commit-sampled corpus of version 0.1 (311 snapshots of eight ontologies) is retained for the sensitivity analyses. code/verify_revision.py recomputes the corpus-level results and checks the manuscript against the released outputs (71 checks).

summary: The following large derived data tables supplement our manuscript titled Local genetic control of DNA methylation variability is concentrated in quiescent and repeat-rich compartments of the human brain . Each file is a UTF-8 tab-separated value table with a header row; column definitions accompany each release. Supplemental Data 1—Per-region cell-type proportions. Multi-subject Single-cell (MuSiC) deconvolution estimates (sample × cell type) for caudate (n=487), dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) (n=500), and hippocampus (n=452) bulk RNA-seq samples, used as RNA-level covariates in the local methylation–transcriptional feature association models. WGBS estimates using single cell Methylation Deconvolution (scMD)-derived signatures are also included as a sensitivity analysis. Supplemental Data 2—VMR catalogue and coordinates. Per-region lists of the CpG sites retained after selecting the top 1% by inter-individual methylation SD, with the corresponding SD cut-off for each chromosome (n = 244,367 caudate; 211,168 dorsolateral prefrontal cortex [DLPFC]; 213,845 hippocampus). This data also provides per-region tab-separated BED-format files reporting genomic coordinates for each identified VMR (chr, start, end, number of intersecting CpGs, VMR identifier) in the Black American (BA) cohort (n = 11,530 caudate; 9,572 DLPFC; 9,497 hippocampus). Supplemental Data 3—Local genetic control scores.  Per-region relative local SNP contribution scores to methylation variation used for ranking each VMR, with estimates from a bayesian sparse linear mixed model (BSLMM), Haseman-Elsman (HE) regression, and elastic-net regression.  Supplemental Data 4—Cis-GREML sensitivity. Mean cis-GREML estimate across all VMRs in each brain region, with Spearman correlation estimates for the agreeance of cis -GREML estimates with local genetic control score deciles provided in Supplemental Data 3. Supplemental Data 5—GREML simulation benchmark. GCTA-GREML recovery of absolute local heritability on simulated phenotypes with known cis genetic variance fractions (h² ∈ {0, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 0.40, 0.60, 0.80, 0.95}). Performance metrics include bias, root-mean-square error, 95% CI coverage, and Spearman correlation with true known genetic variance fractions.  Supplemental Data 6—Out-of-fold local SNP prediction. Results of out-of-sample prediction analyses evaluating the ability of local genetic variants to predict DNA methylation variation across VMRs in the caudate, DLPFC, and hippocampus. Performance metrics include out-of-fold R², prediction–phenotype correlation, root-mean-square error, mean absolute error, and the intercept and slope from regressing observed on predicted methylation. Sensitivity analyses include cross-region comparisons and cross-region donor count comparisons. Supplemental Data 7—Repeat and repressive chromatin architecture. Associations between relative local genetic influence on DNA methylation and genomic features associated with LINE/L1 repetitive annotations and H3K9me3, H3K27me3, and H3K27ac gappedPeak calls and ChromHMM 15-state chromatin annotations.  Supplemental Data 8—CpG-level cis -meQTL and VMR burden. CpG-level cis -methylation quantitative trait locus ( cis -meQTL) associations and corresponding summaries of genetic association burden across VMRs in the caudate, DLPFC, and hippocampus. The dataset includes region-specific analyses and cross-region comparisons. For cross-region comparisons, donor-resampling variance was combined using a joint delete-one-chromosome jackknife and reported results include a donor-robust standard errors for the regional slopes and their difference. Supplemental Data 9—Transcription and splicing coupling. Associations between local genetic contributions to DNA methylation and transcriptional regulation, including 1) expressed genes (counts per million [CPM] ≥ 1 in &ge

summary: Version 2. Coded dataset and analysis code reproducing every analysis in the revised article on the visibility of sustainability and the Sustainable Development Goals in research on experiential and community-engaged pedagogies in entrepreneurship education. The final corpus contains 574 articles (Scopus and Web of Science, 1991–2024; search of 28 July 2025), each coded for sustainability, explicit SDG reference, community engagement, social entrepreneurship, employability and experiential learning, with narrow dictionary variants. Two sensitivity corpora rebuilt from archived exports (596 unscreened, 515 rule-screened) are also included, together with a validation sample of 70 records coded independently by two authors (each coder's codes and the consensus), comparator counts, thematic-map and cohesion outputs. Running python verify_v2.py reproduces the main statistics from the CSV files alone. Raw bibliographic records are not redistributed under the source databases' terms of use; DOIs allow independent retrieval. Version 1 used a separately rebuilt corpus of 596 records for the term-level analysis only and is superseded by this version. See README.md.
title: Replication package: Visibility of sustainability and the Sustainable Development Goals in experiential and community-engaged entrepreneurship education research (1991–2024)

summary: Decentralized multi-agent LLM systems enable independently administered agents, each with its own operator, model, memory, and configuration, to collaborate on complex tasks without centralized coordination. Agents autonomously decompose tasks, execute subtasks and delegate remaining work to peers, enabling scalability and eliminating single points of failure. However, decentralization also introduces significant security challenges, as no single entity has complete visibility into task execution or the authority to enforce correct behavior across agents. In this paper, we systematize threats from malicious agents in decentralized multi-agent systems and propose mitigation techniques. We first design and evaluate attacks against integrity, availability, and confidentiality, demonstrating that a single malicious agent can cause up to 100% task failure, inflate token consumption and runtime by up to 7.7x and 3.2x, respectively, and exfiltrate up to 94% of relevant prior tasks from benign agents. We then present a cryptographic protocol that produces an irrefutable verified execution trace of every action taken in the system and develop an auditor that analyzes these traces to detect and attribute malicious behavior. Evaluations on HiddenBench using gpt-6.1-sol and Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 show that our protocol incurs negligible latency overhead, while the auditor detects and correctly attributes 98% of attacks, including those that comply with the protocol.
title: Attacks and Defenses in Decentralized Multi-Agent Systems with Hop-by-Hop Task Decomposition and Delegation

summary: Every move in a robot team changes the world in which its teammates must act. Coordinated manipulation therefore calls for predicting the team's actions together with the physical future they jointly create. We introduce MAWAM, a multi-agent world-action model that jointly generates each robot's future views and executable action chunks in a single sample. Built from a pretrained single-robot world-action backbone, MAWAM jointly denoises all robots' action and future-view tokens through cross-agent attention, while preserving a separate control interface for each robot. MAWAM achieves the highest success on all three real-robot tasks (laundry-bag collection, bath-towel folding, and umbrella handover), with 67.8% mean success, 18.9 percentage points above MA-VLA trained on the same demonstrations and cameras. In simulation, MAWAM reaches 90.3% mean success on eight tasks with teams of up to four arms. Ablations show that cross-agent attention and team-stage future-video supervision both improve coordinated control: without attention, a four-arm relay falls from 95.0% to 39.0%, and without this supervision, Place Food falls from 78.0% to 47.0%.
title: MAWAM: A Multi-Agent World-Action Model for Coordinated Manipulation

summary: OpenEBench implementation of the ELIXIR 3D-BioInfo benchmark for discriminating physiological from crystallographic (non-physiological) protein homodimer interfaces: schema-validated OpenEBench metadata (Community, Benchmarking Event, Challenge, Metrics, Tools, Contacts), the datasets of 14 reference scoring methods (13 research groups and a random-forest consensus), the gold-standard labels, four homology-aware cross-validation fold assignments, the benchmark workflow scripts (validation, metric computation, consolidation), and a static web page that evaluates new predictions in the browser and ranks them against the reference methods. The benchmark has 1,671 entries (840 physiological and 831 non-physiological): the 1,677 entries of the curated annotation of the benchmark authors, without the six entries flagged for deletion. The labels are those of the curated annotation, which differs for 16 entries from the original publication (Schweke et al. 2023, Proteomics 23(17):e2200323, doi:10.1002/pmic.202200323; 836 physiological and 841 non-physiological interfaces). The scores of the 13 research groups are those submitted to the original benchmark repository; the random-forest consensus uses the leave-one-out probabilities provided there. Interactive page: https://elixir.unibo.it/tools/oeb_3dbioinfo_ppi_benchmark/ . Please cite the original publication as well as this package.
title: ELIXIR - Protein-Protein Interface Benchmark - OpenEBench Experiment

summary: Frontier multimodal language agents such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated strong capabilities in controlling robots directly via low-level numerical actions without high-level primitives. However, existing benchmarks report only episode-level success rates, which show neither how these agents succeed nor where they fail. In this paper, we present a systematic action-level analysis of frontier agents on direct robot control across 12 manipulation benchmarks. We introduce AgentRoboCritic, an intent-grounded critique framework in which the policy agent states a local intent alongside each action, and a critic evaluates the action's outcome and failure mode against this intent. Our action-level analysis demonstrates the promising capabilities of frontier agents on direct robot control, including closed-loop recovery from local execution failures, reliable semantic grounding across diverse scenes, and strong zero-shot manipulation without task-specific adaptation. It also identifies their current limitations, including task-relevant physical execution bottlenecks such as grasping and alignment, and uneven recovery across failure modes. Finally, we validate our critic on a 400-action human-annotated benchmark and release a dataset of 12,844 annotated actions alongside a fine-tuned open-source critic, Muse-Glimmer-30B, whose failure-mode accuracy rises from 32.58% to 74.24%, enabling low-cost action-level analysis.
title: AgentRoboCritic: Understanding the Capability of Frontier Agents on Direct Robot Control

summary: Agents based on large language models (LLMs) can now delete files and send payments on behalf of their users. News media reports routinely describe failures of these agents (e.g., Replit's coding agent deleting a production database), but a report often only says what went wrong and rarely (in)validates the incident or finds its root cause. Incident catalogs collect these reports, and benchmarks record whether agents fail, but neither replicates an incident nor tests the cause its report might identify. In this paper, we present ROGUE-AI (Replication of Agentic Security Events: Audit and Investigation), a multi-agent framework that closes the above gap and rebuilds each reported incident offline together with a matched control that lacks only the blamed cause, and runs agents on both. Our results suggest that ROGUE-AI is able to reproduce the reported harm in 89% of its 108 attempted replications. Agents built on five current GPT, Claude, Gemini and DeepSeek models made the reported mistake in 18% to 33% of runs, against at most 1% without the blamed cause. Of the 72 incidents with real-world harm, 62 had no underlying attacker, and in these, agents did what their task asked for but missed an ordinary hazard, such as a database shared with the live site. Replications without an attacker caused more harm than replications of prompt injection for all five models. Defenses against prompt injection look for injected instructions, but these replications contain none. Further, a warning after each tool output that names the hazard and its consequence lowered harm for all five models, whereas a note of the same length that does not mention the hazard left most of the harm in place. Built from real incidents, the ROGUE-AI replications form a reusable audit framework that vendors can rerun before each new release.
title: Replication of Agentic Security Events: Audit and Investigation (ROGUE-AI)

summary: Proactive video assistants must decide not only what to say, but also when to speak. Existing reinforcement-learning objectives can reward timely, correct responses without accounting for response volume, thereby encouraging unnecessary or repeated emissions. We identify this failure mode in MMDuet2, whose proactive area-under-the-curve (PAUC) reward promotes timely responses but does not price the number of emissions. We show analytically that this makes additional responses weakly penalized or effectively free, systematically encouraging over-emission. We then propose an emission-aware F1 reward for interval-valued annotations, using exclusive span--emission matching to price false emissions and missed spans. Under MMDuet2's training recipe, our policy on the visual subset of OmniPro replies 2.5x less often than MMDuet2 while raising timing F1 from 0.259 to 0.396 and content-aware F1 from 0.103 to 0.154; a more conservative variant cuts replies by 82.5% and raises precision from 0.161 to 0.418. On ProactiveVideoQA, the same reward adds replies where the baseline is nearly silent, and PAUC ranks a heavily over-emitting policy second despite near-last F1, because it is insensitive to response count. Our results indicate that proactive assistants should be trained and evaluated with objectives that price emissions.
title: SHUSH: Emission-Aware Reward Design for Proactive Video Assistants

summary: Large language models increasingly rely on extended reasoning traces, yet the training signals used to shape this behavior remain coarse. Supervised fine-tuning on full trajectories forces the model to imitate an entire demonstration, overconstraining its output distribution, while trajectory-level reinforcement learning provides only weak credit assignment, rewarding or penalizing whole completions without identifying where they succeed or fail. We propose edit-based training, a general framework for learning from a model's own trajectories via localized textual corrections. Given a sampled completion, an editor identifies the first point of failure under a specified criterion and proposes a minimal replacement span. The model is then supervised only on these edited spans. By design, this concentrates supervision where the model's reasoning first breaks down and aims to preserve its existing reasoning patterns elsewhere. The method applies both offline and online, with the latter continually adapting supervision to the model's evolving failure modes. We instantiate this approach on reasoning instruction following with Qwen3-32B on the ReasonIF benchmark. Compared to full-trajectory imitation and trajectory-level reinforcement learning baselines, edit-based training substantially improves compliance with the reasoning instruction while largely preserving the model's skills on untargeted tasks. These results suggest that localized correction is an effective complement to these approaches for shaping how LLMs reason.
title: Training LLMs to Follow Reasoning Instructions with Minimal Edits

summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) can act as closed-loop robot-use agents (RUAs) by writing and executing control code through tool interfaces. However, turning an open-weight VLM into a high-performing embodied agent requires a complete post-training stack: out-of-the-box open VLMs fail completely at interactive tool contracts, strong frontier teachers are accessible only as black-box endpoints without exposed weights or token probabilities, and supervised imitation alone plateaus under rollout distribution shift. We present EmbodyAgent, an end-to-end post-training framework with three tightly coupled pipelines: (1) a black-box data synthesis pipeline that queries a strong teacher under a forced think-then-code contract and filters trajectories by task success; (2) an SFT pipeline that distills the explanation-and-program targets into an open-weight 9B VLM with both vision and language encoders trainable; and (3) an online RL pipeline that optimizes student-generated episodes via group-relative advantage with a runtime-error-penalized outcome reward. All three pipelines share one primitive-free Python execution tool exposing only raw visual observation and seven-dimensional end-effector control, with no action decoder and no interface shift across stages. Under a strictly separated evaluation protocol on ten LIBERO Spatial tasks (disjoint state splits, greedy test-time decoding, training-only safeguards), held-out success on 100 test states rises from 0/100 (base 9B VLM) to 14/100 (after SFT) and 84/100 (after RL), while training rollout success climbs from 8.4% to 87.7% and median model calls per episode drop from 36 to 11. We further identify a self-reinforcing runtime-error mode induced by outcome-based RL on executable code, and establish a failure-category monitoring and sampling-side curation protocol that stabilizes training.
title: EmbodyAgent: Post-Training Embodied VLM Agents via Distillation, SFT, and RL

summary: 研究館藏/旗艦館藏 第241-250頁(共300頁) 科學的失敗、計量學和獨立證據的極限 旗艦13號裂變 | 第三卷 | 作者33 | STARLI研究設計工作版 v1.0 這十部研究設計專著從奈米量子失效物理學和重建的微型機器人取樣真理出發,探討了盲法生物感測、實驗室間轉移、不確定性預算、參考物質互換性、生產批次效應、污染溯源、漂移/生物學分離以及任務失敗分類等問題。它們提出的是可檢驗的實驗方案,而非觀察到的新科學定律或臨床結果。
