ONE FAMILY, FIVE INCOMMENSURATE EVIDENCE STREAMS The first temptation in an integrated research civilization is to take five measurements and make one score. This is dangerous when their physical units have different meanings. A response in micrometers per kilopascal cannot be added meaningfully to a cell speed in micrometers per hour. Neither can be averaged with a degradation half-life in days or a pore oxygen flux in moles per unit surface and time. Even a dimensionless stability index requires an operational definition and a prespecified acceptable region. A scientifically defensible integration records the full vector and permits a hard stop when any essential component fails. Suppose a matrix allows quicker cell movement while the frequency of adverse changes in cell identity rises. An averaged numerical improvement might hide this problem. A research contract instead keeps separate thresholds for structural fidelity, independent physiology, matrix compatibility, calibrated uncertainty and process safety. The cross-family interface can share measured quantities and evidence packages while refusing to transfer conclusions that have not been independently established. That refusal is itself a form of technological maturity. THIRTY MATHEMATICAL PLATES AND FORTY-TWO RECONSTRUCTABLE SURFACES A formula becomes valuable when its domain of validity is written beside it. The third family preserves the source atlas's thirty candidate formula positions and distinguishes generic test-logic equations from specific physical companion interpretations. For a quasi-elastic response, strain is the ratio of stress to modulus under a declared small-strain regime. That is not enough to describe a hydrogel that relaxes, erodes and remodels while cells exert force. Migration tracking must remove moving substrate landmarks; degradation kinetics must separate dry polymer mass from swollen water; oxygen flux must connect gradient, diffusivity, tortuosity and the actual pore network; remodeling stability must declare how long a bounded trajectory is monitored. Forty-two synthetic three-dimensional models make sensitivities visible across registered parameter ranges. Each saved graph belongs to a CSV numeric grid and a reproducible Python reconstruction program, with units for all axes. They are proposed model objects, not measured cells. Their purpose is to help another investigator find a discontinuity, a nonidentifiable parameter combination or a wrong prediction before undertaking a biological assay. When a future experimental series disagrees with a curve, that discrepancy should be welcomed as evidence, not repaired away by changing the axis limits. TWO HUNDRED RESEARCH GATES AS A LIBRARY OF DISAGREEMENT The 200 Research Gates are not decorative questions. Each door begins with a distinct local investigation and asks why that problem matters, how the most serious competing explanation could account for the visible pattern, and what a successor could do with a simple independent witness. Across gel stiffness, migration, degradation, pore transport and remodeling, the language and scale change. Some doors begin from an intriguing contour, others from a physical contradiction or a failed denominator. Some describe a world in which swelling accounts for everything. Others imagine a pore network that is beautiful but disconnected, an apparently motile cell that is actually being carried by its gel, or a stable feedback trace that conceals tissue identity loss. Their future plans ask for blind sample exchange, matched budget controls, withheld perturbations, new batches, sealed negative specimens and automatic refusal. A Gate has done its work when it leaves a person outside the current research group with enough information to prove the attractive explanation wrong. The failure scenario is therefore not an embarrassment; it is an inheritance. The archive should preserve it with the same care as the favored result. THIRTY-THREE PHOENIX EMBRYOS AND A CIVILIZATION THAT CAN STOP The Phoenix possibilities develop small prototypes rather than claiming completed machines. Their names suggest instrument exchanges, counterfactual matrix libraries, pore-network tomography challenges, mechanical memory loops, independent material reference standards and new methods for storing negative outcomes. Each idea includes a minimum test and a reason to retire it. In a mature autonomous experimental environment, this has consequences beyond documentation. Controllers must abstain when calibration disappears. Hardware or material intervention cannot proceed merely because a prediction model is confident. Human permission, biological source provenance and contamination controls remain external authority constraints. A system that pauses when its assumptions collapse is often more useful than one that always returns an answer. The same principle applies to writing and publication: a research program can be inspirational without presenting synthetic models as achieved biological capabilities. The open scientific record grows stronger when authors state what has not yet been built, measured or validated. THE SCIENTIFIC INHERITANCE The supplied STARLI F18 organ-on-chip monograph reminds this family of a central distinction: geometric precision is not physiological function. In a material-focused family, the same argument has multiple forms. An excellent modulus map is not morphogenesis. A migrating centroid is not necessarily a migrating cell. A fall in wet weight is not always polymer cleavage. A large apparent flux is not necessarily oxygen supply to living tissue. And a stable material signal is not proof of organ-specific homeostasis. Published work on organoid hydrogels, synthetic matrices, viscoelasticity and dynamic mechanics offers methodological precedents. Those sources do not experimentally verify the five new STARLI couplings. This research family offers a plan for making such claims testable, including measurements, strong baselines, uncertainty accounting, data reconstruction and stopping conditions. The long-term goal is not to build a library of conclusions that cannot be questioned, but an open architecture of precise experimental doors. Each generation should be free to improve the questions, reject a mistaken mechanism and keep whatever remains genuinely useful. Let beauty have the ability to continue happening. ONE FAMILY, FIVE INCOMMENSURATE EVIDENCE STREAMS The first temptation in an integrated research civilization is to take five measurements and make one score. Neither can be averaged with a degradation half-life in days or a pore oxygen flux in moles per unit surface and time. Even a dimensionless stability index requires an operational definition and a prespecified acceptable region. A scientifically defensible integration records the full vector and permits a hard stop when any essential component fails. Suppose a matrix allows quicker cell movement while the frequency of adverse changes in cell identity rises. An averaged numerical improvement might hide this problem. A research contract instead keeps separate thresholds for structural fidelity, independent physiology, matrix compatibility, calibrated uncertainty and process safety. The cross-family interface can share measured quantities and evidence packages while refusing to transfer conclusions that have not been independently established. That refusal is itself a form of technological maturity. THIRTY MATHEMATICAL PLATES AND FORTY-TWO RECONSTRUCTABLE SURFACES A formula becomes valuable when its domain of validity is written beside it. The third family preserves the source atlas's thirty candidate formula positions and distinguishes generic test-logic equations from specific physical companion interpretations. For a quasi-elastic response, strain is the ratio of stress to modulus under a declared small-strain regime. That is not enough to describe a hydrogel that relaxes, erodes and remodels while cells exert force. Migration tracking must remove moving substrate landmarks; degradation kinetics must separate dry polymer mass from swollen water; oxygen flux must connect gradient, diffusivity, tortuosity and the actual pore network; remodeling stability must declare how long a bounded trajectory is monitored. Forty-two synthetic three-dimensional models make sensitivities visible across registered parameter ranges. Each saved graph belongs to a CSV numeric grid and a reproducible Python reconstruction program, with units for all axes. They are proposed model objects, not measured cells. Their purpose is to help another investigator find a discontinuity, a nonidentifiable parameter combination or a wrong prediction before undertaking a biological assay. When a future experimental series disagrees with a curve, that discrepancy should be welcomed as evidence, not repaired away by changing the axis limits. TWO HUNDRED RESEARCH GATES AS A LIBRARY OF DISAGREEMENT The 200 Research Gates are not decorative questions. Each door begins with a distinct local investigation and asks why that problem matters, how the most serious competing explanation could account for the visible pattern, and what a successor could do with a simple independent witness. Across gel stiffness, migration, degradation, pore transport and remodeling, the language and scale change. Some doors begin from an intriguing contour, others from a physical contradiction or a failed denominator. Some describe a world in which swelling accounts for everything. Others imagine a pore network that is beautiful but disconnected, an apparently motile cell that is actually being carried by its gel, or a stable feedback trace that conceals tissue identity loss. Their future plans ask for blind sample exchange, matched budget controls, withheld perturbations, new batches, sealed negative specimens and automatic refusal. A Gate has done its work when it leaves a person outside the current research group with enough information to prove the attractive explanation wrong. The failure scenario is therefore not an embarrassment; it is an inheritance. The archive should preserve it with the same care as the favored result. THIRTY-THREE PHOENIX EMBRYOS AND A CIVILIZATION THAT CAN STOP The Phoenix possibilities develop small prototypes rather than claiming completed machines. Their names suggest instrument exchanges, counterfactual matrix libraries, pore-network tomography challenges, mechanical memory loops, independent material reference standards and new methods for storing negative outcomes. Each idea includes a minimum test and a reason to retire it. In a mature autonomous experimental environment, this has consequences beyond documentation. Controllers must abstain when calibration disappears. Hardware or material intervention cannot proceed merely because a prediction model is confident. Human permission, biological source provenance and contamination controls remain external authority constraints. A system that pauses when its assumptions collapse is often more useful than one that always returns an answer. The same principle applies to writing and publication: a research program can be inspirational without presenting synthetic models as achieved biological capabilities. The open scientific record grows stronger when authors state what has not yet been built, measured or validated. THE SCIENTIFIC INHERITANCE The supplied STARLI F18 organ-on-chip monograph reminds this family of a central distinction: geometric precision is not physiological function. In a material-focused family, the same argument has multiple forms. An excellent modulus map is not morphogenesis. A migrating centroid is not necessarily a migrating cell. A fall in wet weight is not always polymer cleavage. A large apparent flux is not necessarily oxygen supply to living tissue. And a stable material signal is not proof of organ-specific homeostasis. Published work on organoid hydrogels, synthetic matrices, viscoelasticity and dynamic mechanics offers methodological precedents. Those sources do not experimentally verify the five new STARLI couplings. This research family offers a plan for making such claims testable, including measurements, strong baselines, uncertainty accounting, data reconstruction and stopping conditions. The long-term goal is not to build a library of conclusions that cannot be questioned, but an open architecture of precise experimental doors. Each generation should be free to improve the questions, reject a mistaken mechanism and keep whatever remains genuinely useful. Let beauty have the ability to continue happening. Neither can be averaged with a degradation half-life in days or a pore oxygen flux in moles per unit surface and time. Even a dimensionless stability index requires an operational definition and a prespecified acceptable region. A scientifically defensible integration records the full vector and permits a hard stop when any essential component fails. Suppose a matrix allows quicker cell movement while the frequency of adverse changes in cell identity rises. An averaged numerical improvement might hide this problem. A research contract instead keeps separate thresholds for structural fidelity, independent physiology, matrix compatibility, calibrated uncertainty and process safety. The cross-family interface can share measured quantities and evidence packages while refusing to transfer conclusions that have not been independently established. That refusal is itself a form of technological maturity. THIRTY MATHEMATICAL PLATES AND FORTY-TWO RECONSTRUCTABLE SURFACES A formula becomes valuable when its domain of validity is written beside it. The third family preserves the source atlas's thirty candidate formula positions and distinguishes generic test-logic equations from specific physical companion interpretations. For a quasi-elastic response, strain is the ratio of stress to modulus under a declared small-strain regime. That is not enough to describe a hydrogel that relaxes, erodes and remodels while cells exert force. Migration tracking must remove moving substrate landmarks; degradation kinetics must separate dry polymer mass from swollen water; oxygen flux must connect gradient, diffusivity, tortuosity and the actual pore network; remodeling stability must declare how long a bounded trajectory is monitored. Forty-two synthetic three-dimensional models make sensitivities visible across registered parameter ranges. Each saved graph belongs to a CSV numeric grid and a reproducible Python reconstruction program, with units for all axes. They are proposed model objects, not measured cells. Their purpose is to help another investigator find a discontinuity, a nonidentifiable parameter combination or a wrong prediction before undertaking a biological assay. When a future experimental series disagrees with a curve, that discrepancy should be welcomed as evidence, not repaired away by changing the axis limits. TWO HUNDRED RESEARCH GATES AS A LIBRARY OF DISAGREEMENT The 200 Research Gates are not decorative questions. Each door begins with a distinct local investigation and asks why that problem matters, how the most serious competing explanation could account for the visible pattern, and what a successor could do with a simple independent witness. Across gel stiffness, migration, degradation, pore transport and remodeling, the language and scale change. Some doors begin from an intriguing contour, others from a physical contradiction or a failed denominator. Some describe a world in which swelling accounts for everything. Others imagine a pore network that is beautiful but disconnected, an apparently motile cell that is actually being carried by its gel, or a stable feedback trace that conceals tissue identity loss. Their future plans ask for blind sample exchange, matched budget controls, withheld perturbations, new batches, sealed negative specimens and automatic refusal. A Gate has done its work when it leaves a person outside the current research group with enough information to prove the attractive explanation wrong. The failure scenario is therefore not an embarrassment; it is an inheritance. The archive should preserve it with the same care as the favored result. THIRTY-THREE PHOENIX EMBRYOS AND A CIVILIZATION THAT CAN STOP The Phoenix possibilities develop small prototypes rather than claiming completed machines. Their names suggest instrument exchanges, counterfactual matrix libraries, pore-network tomography challenges, mechanical memory loops, independent material reference standards and new methods for storing negative outcomes. Each idea includes a minimum test and a reason to retire it. In a mature autonomous experimental environment, this has consequences beyond documentation. Controllers must abstain when calibration disappears. Hardware or material intervention cannot proceed merely because a prediction model is confident. Human permission, biological source provenance and contamination controls remain external authority constraints. A system that pauses when its assumptions collapse is often more useful than one that always returns an answer. The same principle applies to writing and publication: a research program can be inspirational without presenting synthetic models as achieved biological capabilities. The open scientific record grows stronger when authors state what has not yet been built, measured or validated. THE SCIENTIFIC INHERITANCE The supplied STARLI F18 organ-on-chip monograph reminds this family of a central distinction: geometric precision is not physiological function. In a material-focused family, the same argument has multiple forms. An excellent modulus map is not morphogenesis. A migrating centroid is not necessarily a migrating cell. A fall in wet weight is not always polymer cleavage. A large apparent flux is not necessarily oxygen supply to living tissue. And a stable material signal is not proof of organ-specific homeostasis. Published work on organoid hydrogels, synthetic matrices, viscoelasticity and dynamic mechanics offers methodological precedents. Those sources do not experimentally verify the five new STARLI couplings. This research family offers a plan for making such claims testable, including measurements, strong baselines, uncertainty accounting, data reconstruction and stopping conditions. The long-term goal is not to build a library of conclusions that cannot be questioned, but an open architecture of precise experimental doors. Each generation should be free to improve the questions, reject a mistaken mechanism and keep whatever remains genuinely useful. Let beauty have the ability to continue happening. Even a dimensionless stability index requires an operational definition and a prespecified acceptable region. A scientifically defensible integration records the full vector and permits a hard stop when any essential component fails. Suppose a matrix allows quicker cell movement while the frequency of adverse changes in cell identity rises. An averaged numerical improvement might hide this problem. A research contract instead keeps separate thresholds for structural fidelity, independent physiology, matrix compatibility, calibrated uncertainty and process safety. The cross-family interface can share measured quantities and evidence packages while refusing to transfer conclusions that have not been independently established. The third family preserves the source atlas's thirty candidate formula positions and distinguishes generic test-logic equations from specific physical companion interpretations. For a quasi-elastic response, strain is the ratio of stress to modulus under a declared small-strain regime. That is not enough to describe a hydrogel that relaxes, erodes and remodels while cells exert force. Migration tracking must remove moving substrate landmarks; degradation kinetics must separate dry polymer mass from swollen water; oxygen flux must connect gradient, diffusivity, tortuosity and the actual pore network; remodeling stability must declare how long a bounded trajectory is monitored. Forty-two synthetic three-dimensional models make sensitivities visible across registered parameter ranges. Each saved graph belongs to a CSV numeric grid and a reproducible Python reconstruction program, with units for all axes. They are proposed model objects, not measured cells. Their purpose is to help another investigator find a discontinuity, a nonidentifiable parameter combination or a wrong prediction before undertaking a biological assay. When a future experimental series disagrees with a curve, that discrepancy should be welcomed as evidence, not repaired away by changing the axis limits. Each door begins with a distinct local investigation and asks why that problem matters, how the most serious competing explanation could account for the visible pattern, and what a successor could do with a simple independent witness. Across gel stiffness, migration, degradation, pore transport and remodeling, the language and scale change. Some doors begin from an intriguing contour, others from a physical contradiction or a failed denominator. Some describe a world in which swelling accounts for everything. Others imagine a pore network that is beautiful but disconnected, an apparently motile cell that is actually being carried by its gel, or a stable feedback trace that conceals tissue identity loss. Their future plans ask for blind sample exchange, matched budget controls, withheld perturbations, new batches, sealed negative specimens and automatic refusal. A Gate has done its work when it leaves a person outside the current research group with enough information to prove the attractive explanation wrong. The failure scenario is therefore not an embarrassment; it is an inheritance. The archive should preserve it with the same care as the favored result. THIRTY-THREE PHOENIX EMBRYOS AND A CIVILIZATION THAT CAN STOP The Phoenix possibilities develop small prototypes rather than claiming completed machines. Their names suggest instrument exchanges, counterfactual matrix libraries, pore-network tomography challenges, mechanical memory loops, independent material reference standards and new methods for storing negative outcomes. Each idea includes a minimum test and a reason to retire it. In a mature autonomous experimental environment, this has consequences beyond documentation. Controllers must abstain when calibration disappears. Hardware or material intervention cannot proceed merely because a prediction model is confident. Human permission, biological source provenance and contamination controls remain external authority constraints. A system that pauses when its assumptions collapse is often more useful than one that always returns an answer. The same principle applies to writing and publication: a research program can be inspirational without presenting synthetic models as achieved biological capabilities. The open scientific record grows stronger when authors state what has not yet been built, measured or validated. THE SCIENTIFIC INHERITANCE The supplied STARLI F18 organ-on-chip monograph reminds this family of a central distinction: geometric precision is not physiological function. In a material-focused family, the same argument has multiple forms. An excellent modulus map is not morphogenesis. A migrating centroid is not necessarily a migrating cell. A fall in wet weight is not always polymer cleavage. A large apparent flux is not necessarily oxygen supply to living tissue. And a stable material signal is not proof of organ-specific homeostasis. Published work on organoid hydrogels, synthetic matrices, viscoelasticity and dynamic mechanics offers methodological precedents. Those sources do not experimentally verify the five new STARLI couplings. This research family offers a plan for making such claims testable, including measurements, strong baselines, uncertainty accounting, data reconstruction and stopping conditions. The long-term goal is not to build a library of conclusions that cannot be questioned, but an open architecture of precise experimental doors. Each generation should be free to improve the questions, reject a mistaken mechanism and keep whatever remains genuinely useful. Let beauty have the ability to continue happening. Neither can be averaged with a degradation half-life in days or a pore oxygen flux in moles per unit surface and time. Even a dimensionless stability index requires an operational definition and a prespecified acceptable region. A scientifically defensible integration records the full vector and permits a hard stop when any essential component fails. Suppose a matrix allows quicker cell movement while the frequency of adverse changes in cell identity rises. An averaged numerical improvement might hide this problem. A research contract instead keeps separate thresholds for structural fidelity, independent physiology, matrix compatibility, calibrated uncertainty and process safety. The cross-family interface can share measured quantities and evidence packages while refusing to transfer conclusions that have not been independently established. That refusal is itself a form of technological maturity. THIRTY MATHEMATICAL PLATES AND FORTY-TWO RECONSTRUCTABLE SURFACES A formula becomes valuable when its domain of validity is written beside it. The third family preserves the source atlas's thirty candidate formula positions and distinguishes generic test-logic equations from specific physical companion interpretations. For a quasi-elastic response, strain is the ratio of stress to modulus under a declared small-strain regime. That is not enough to describe a hydrogel that relaxes, erodes and remodels while cells exert force. Migration tracking must remove moving substrate landmarks; degradation kinetics must separate dry polymer mass from swollen water; oxygen flux must connect gradient, diffusivity, tortuosity and the actual pore network; remodeling stability must declare how long a bounded trajectory is monitored. Forty-two synthetic three-dimensional models make sensitivities visible across registered parameter ranges. Each saved graph belongs to a CSV numeric grid and a reproducible Python reconstruction program, with units for all axes. They are proposed model objects, not measured cells. Their purpose is to help another investigator find a discontinuity, a nonidentifiable parameter combination or a wrong prediction before undertaking a biological assay. When a future experimental series disagrees with a curve, that discrepancy should be welcomed as evidence, not repaired away by changing the axis limits. TWO HUNDRED RESEARCH GATES AS A LIBRARY OF DISAGREEMENT The 200 Research Gates are not decorative questions. Each door begins with a distinct local investigation and asks why that problem matters, how the most serious competing explanation could account for the visible pattern, and what a successor could do with a simple independent witness. Across gel stiffness, migration, degradation, pore transport and remodeling, the language and scale change. Some doors begin from an intriguing contour, others from a physical contradiction or a failed denominator. Some describe a world in which swelling accounts for everything. Others imagine a pore network that is beautiful but disconnected, an apparently motile cell that is actually being carried by its gel, or a stable feedback trace that conceals tissue identity loss. Their future plans ask for blind sample exchange, matched budget controls, withheld perturbations, new batches, sealed negative specimens and automatic refusal. A Gate has done its work when it leaves a person outside the current research group with enough information to prove the attractive explanation wrong. The failure scenario is therefore not an embarrassment; it is an inheritance. The archive should preserve it with the same care as the favored result. THIRTY-THREE PHOENIX EMBRYOS AND A CIVILIZATION THAT CAN STOP The Phoenix possibilities develop small prototypes rather than claiming completed machines. Their names suggest instrument exchanges, counterfactual matrix libraries, pore-network tomography challenges, mechanical memory loops, independent material reference standards and new methods for storing negative outcomes. Each idea includes a minimum test and a reason to retire it. In a mature autonomous experimental environment, this has consequences beyond documentation. Controllers must abstain when calibration disappears. Hardware or material intervention cannot proceed merely because a prediction model is confident. Human permission, biological source provenance and contamination controls remain external authority constraints. A system that pauses when its assumptions collapse is often more useful than one that always returns an answer. The same principle applies to writing and publication: a research program can be inspirational without presenting synthetic models as achieved biological capabilities. The open scientific record grows stronger when authors state what has not yet been built, measured or validated. THE SCIENTIFIC INHERITANCE The supplied STARLI F18 organ-on-chip monograph reminds this family of a central distinction: geometric precision is not physiological function. In a material-focused family, the same argument has multiple forms. An excellent modulus map is not morphogenesis. A migrating centroid is not necessarily a migrating cell. A fall in wet weight is not always polymer cleavage. A large apparent flux is not necessarily oxygen supply to living tissue. And a stable material signal is not proof of organ-specific homeostasis. Published work on organoid hydrogels, synthetic matrices, viscoelasticity and dynamic mechanics offers methodological precedents. Those sources do not experimentally verify the five new STARLI couplings. This research family offers a plan for making such claims testable, including measurements, strong baselines, uncertainty accounting, data reconstruction and stopping conditions. The long-term goal is not to build a library of conclusions that cannot be questioned, but an open architecture of precise experimental doors. Each generation should be free to improve the questions, reject a mistaken mechanism and keep whatever remains genuinely useful. Let beauty have the ability to continue happening. Even a dimensionless stability index requires an operational definition and a prespecified acceptable region. A scientifically defensible integration records the full vector and permits a hard stop when any essential component fails. Suppose a matrix allows quicker cell movement while the frequency of adverse changes in cell identity rises. An averaged numerical improvement might hide this problem. The third family preserves the source atlas's thirty candidate formula positions and distinguishes generic test-logic equations from specific physical companion interpretations. For a quasi-elastic response, strain is the ratio of stress to modulus under a declared small-strain regime. That is not enough to describe a hydrogel that relaxes, erodes and remodels while cells exert force. Each saved graph belongs to a CSV numeric grid and a reproducible Python reconstruction program, with units for all axes. They are proposed model objects, not measured cells. Their purpose is to help another investigator find a discontinuity, a nonidentifiable parameter combination or a wrong prediction before undertaking a biological assay. Each door begins with a distinct local investigation and asks why that problem matters, how the most serious competing explanation could account for the visible pattern, and what a successor could do with a simple independent witness. Across gel stiffness, migration, degradation, pore transport and remodeling, the language and scale change. Some doors begin from an intriguing contour, others from a physical contradiction or a failed denominator. Some describe a world in which swelling accounts for everything. Others imagine a pore network that is beautiful but disconnected, an apparently motile cell that is actually being carried by its gel, or a stable feedback trace that conceals tissue identity loss. Their future plans ask for blind sample exchange, matched budget controls, withheld perturbations, new batches, sealed negative specimens and automatic refusal. A Gate has done its work when it leaves a person outside the current research group with enough information to prove the attractive explanation wrong. The failure scenario is therefore not an embarrassment; it is an inheritance. The archive should preserve it with the same care as the favored result. THIRTY-THREE PHOENIX EMBRYOS AND A CIVILIZATION THAT CAN STOP The Phoenix possibilities develop small prototypes rather than claiming completed machines. Their names suggest instrument exchanges, counterfactual matrix libraries, pore-network tomography challenges, mechanical memory loops, independent material reference standards and new methods for storing negative outcomes. Each idea includes a minimum test and a reason to retire it. In a mature autonomous experimental environment, this has consequences beyond documentation. Controllers must abstain when calibration disappears. Hardware or material intervention cannot proceed merely because a prediction model is confident. Human permission, biological source provenance and contamination controls remain external authority constraints. A system that pauses when its assumptions collapse is often more useful than one that always returns an answer. The same principle applies to writing and publication: a research program can be inspirational without presenting synthetic models as achieved biological capabilities. The open scientific record grows stronger when authors state what has not yet been built, measured or validated. THE SCIENTIFIC INHERITANCE The supplied STARLI F18 organ-on-chip monograph reminds this family of a central distinction: geometric precision is not physiological function. In a material-focused family, the same argument has multiple forms. An excellent modulus map is not morphogenesis. A migrating centroid is not necessarily a migrating cell. A fall in wet weight is not always polymer cleavage. A large apparent flux is not necessarily oxygen supply to living tissue. And a stable material signal is not proof of organ-specific homeostasis. Published work on organoid hydrogels, synthetic matrices, viscoelasticity and dynamic mechanics offers methodological precedents. Those sources do not experimentally verify the five new STARLI couplings. This research family offers a plan for making such claims testable, including measurements, strong baselines, uncertainty accounting, data reconstruction and stopping conditions. The long-term goal is not to build a library of conclusions that cannot be questioned, but an open architecture of precise experimental doors. Each generation should be free to improve the questions, reject a mistaken mechanism and keep whatever remains genuinely useful. Let beauty have the ability to continue happening. Even a dimensionless stability index requires an operational definition and a prespecified acceptable region. The third family preserves the source atlas's thirty candidate formula positions and distinguishes generic test-logic equations from specific physical companion interpretations. For a quasi-elastic response, strain is the ratio of stress to modulus under a declared small-strain regime. That is not enough to describe a hydrogel that relaxes, erodes and remodels while cells exert force. Migration tracking must remove moving substrate landmarks; degradation kinetics must separate dry polymer mass from swollen water; oxygen flux must connect gradient, diffusivity, tortuosity and the actual pore network; remodeling stability must declare how long a bounded trajectory is monitored. Each door begins with a distinct local investigation and asks why that problem matters, how the most serious competing explanation could account for the visible pattern, and what a successor could do with a simple independent witness. Across gel stiffness, migration, degradation, pore transport and remodeling, the language and scale change. Some doors begin from an intriguing contour, others from a physical contradiction or a failed denominator. Some describe a world in which swelling accounts for everything. Others imagine a pore network that is beautiful but disconnected, an apparently motile cell that is actually being carried by its gel, or a stable feedback trace that conceals tissue identity loss. Their future plans ask for blind sample exchange, matched budget controls, withheld perturbations, new batches, sealed negative specimens and automatic refusal. A Gate has done its work when it leaves a person outside the current research group with enough information to prove the attractive explanation wrong. The failure scenario is therefore not an embarrassment; it is an inheritance. The archive should preserve it with the same care as the favored result. Their names suggest instrument exchanges, counterfactual matrix libraries, pore-network tomography challenges, mechanical memory loops, independent material reference standards and new methods for storing negative outcomes. Each idea includes a minimum test and a reason to retire it. In a mature autonomous experimental environment, this has consequences beyond documentation. Controllers must abstain when calibration disappears. Hardware or material intervention cannot proceed merely because a prediction model is confident. Human permission, biological source provenance and contamination controls remain external authority constraints. A system that pauses when its assumptions collapse is often more useful than one that always returns an answer. The same principle applies to writing and publication: a research program can be inspirational without presenting synthetic models as achieved biological capabilities. The open scientific record grows stronger when authors state what has not yet been built, measured or validated. In a material-focused family, the same argument has multiple forms. An excellent modulus map is not morphogenesis. A migrating centroid is not necessarily a migrating cell. A fall in wet weight is not always polymer cleavage. A large apparent flux is not necessarily oxygen supply to living tissue. And a stable material signal is not proof of organ-specific homeostasis. Published work on organoid hydrogels, synthetic matrices, viscoelasticity and dynamic mechanics offers methodological precedents. Those sources do not experimentally verify the five new STARLI couplings. This research family offers a plan for making such claims testable, including measurements, strong baselines, uncertainty accounting, data reconstruction and stopping conditions. The long-term goal is not to build a library of conclusions that cannot be questioned, but an open architecture of precise experimental doors. Each generation should be free to improve the questions, reject a mistaken mechanism and keep whatever remains genuinely useful. Let beauty have the ability to continue happening. For a quasi-elastic response, strain is the ratio of stress to modulus under a declared small-strain regime. That is not enough to describe a hydrogel that relaxes, erodes and remodels while cells exert force. Migration tracking must remove moving substrate landmarks; degradation kinetics must separate dry polymer mass from swollen water; oxygen flux must connect gradient, diffusivity, tortuosity and the actual pore network; remodeling stability must declare how long a bounded trajectory is monitored. Their purpose is to help another investigator find a discontinuity, a nonidentifiable parameter combination or a wrong prediction before undertaking a biological assay. Each door begins with a distinct local investigation and asks why that problem matters, how the most serious competing explanation could account for the visible pattern, and what a successor could do with a simple independent witness. Across gel stiffness, migration, degradation, pore transport and remodeling, the language and scale change. Some doors begin from an intriguing contour, others from a physical contradiction or a failed denominator. Some describe a world in which swelling accounts for everything. Others imagine a pore network that is beautiful but disconnected, an apparently motile cell that is actually being carried by its gel, or a stable feedback trace that conceals tissue identity loss. Their future plans ask for blind sample exchange, matched budget controls, withheld perturbations, new batches, sealed negative specimens and automatic refusal. A Gate has done its work when it leaves a person outside the current research group with enough information to prove the attractive explanation wrong. The failure scenario is therefore not an embarrassment; it is an inheritance. The archive should preserve it with the same care as the favored result. Their names suggest instrument exchanges, counterfactual matrix libraries, pore-network tomography challenges, mechanical memory loops, independent material reference standards and new methods for storing negative outcomes. Each idea includes a minimum test and a reason to retire it. In a mature autonomous experimental environment, this has consequences beyond documentation. Controllers must abstain when calibration disappears. Hardware or material intervention cannot proceed merely because a prediction model is confident. Human permission, biological source provenance and contamination controls remain external authority constraints. A system that pauses when its assumptions collapse is often more useful than one that always returns an answer. The same principle applies to writing and publication: a research program can be inspirational without presenting synthetic models as achieved biological capabilities. The open scientific record grows stronger when authors state what has not yet been built, measured or validated. THE SCIENTIFIC INHERITANCE The supplied STARLI F18 organ-on-chip monograph reminds this family of a central distinction: geometric precision is not physiological function. In a material-focused family, the same argument has multiple forms. An excellent modulus map is not morphogenesis. A migrating centroid is not necessarily a migrating cell. A fall in wet weight is not always polymer cleavage. A large apparent flux is not necessarily oxygen supply to living tissue. And a stable material signal is not proof of organ-specific homeostasis. Published work on organoid hydrogels, synthetic matrices, viscoelasticity and dynamic mechanics offers methodological precedents. Those sources do not experimentally verify the five new STARLI couplings. This research family offers a plan for making such claims testable, including measurements, strong baselines, uncertainty accounting, data reconstruction and stopping conditions. The long-term goal is not to build a library of conclusions that cannot be questioned, but an open architecture of precise experimental doors. Each generation should be free to improve the questions, reject a mistaken mechanism and keep whatever remains genuinely useful. Let beauty have the ability to continue happening. summary: Reproducibility companion for a powder X-ray diffraction reference-library holdout audit. The package includes Python scripts, checksum-verified source provenance, nominal-label crosswalks, per-query and aggregate results, and figures. It compares the minimum total-variation error for selection of an eligible label with that for a convex blend, using scan/sample-ID, whole-recipe and (where applicable) filename-series holdouts. The nested Archive A bundle includes unchanged files from the Bickmore–Terry–Eberl archive (CC BY 4.0, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23692859). Archive B patterns are obtained separately from the Pabst et al. archive (CC BY 4.0, doi:10.5281/zenodo.18235708) and checksum-verified by the scripts. These are analyses of public measurements against nominal labels; no new measurements were collected. See README.txt and SOURCE-ATTRIBUTION.txt for reproduction and attribution.
title: Data and code for "Copying and blending reference compositions in powder diffraction: a two-archive holdout audit"

summary: The work continues the geometric model of the distribution of primes [2] and the work “The Number Arrow and the Line 1/2” [1]. The geometric formula for the number of odd composites up to p², N(p) = 1 + 3(p − 1)(p − 3)/8, is treated as the first level of a ladder in which the scale is squared at each step: 5² → 5⁴ → 5⁸ → 5¹⁶. It is shown that this formula is the best quadratic formula for the level up to 5⁴: it is exact everywhere except for one compensating pair of misses (p = 15 and p = 17). The quadratic lattice of a level holds up to the basis 7 inclusive and breaks down right after it. The error of the formula splits into two superimposed tables: a smooth level correction and an oscillation which, in the explicit formula, is a sum of cosines over the zeros of the zeta function. The main result is a law of levels, checked on exact values of π (x) up to 3³² ≈ 1.9 · 10¹⁵: when the scale is squared, the relative error of the prime count is squared, and the error itself is inverse to the linear scale p = √x obtained from the difference of squares: ε · p stays of order one at all checked steps. The law holding at all steps is equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis (von Koch, 1901). The author puts forward the hypothesis that the self-similarity of the ladder may become a route to its proof: for this one must show that the step structure itself does not allow ε · p to grow faster than a power of the logarithm. This step is named but not taken. The method may become the basis for an exact count of prime density by levels without the exponential and the logarithm in the level formula. Section 7 gives a geometric reading for a reader without mathematical training: why the basis of the model is 2, 3, 5, 7, how the seam 8–9 links the linear and the quadratic levels, why the centres of the seam differ by exactly ¼ and how π arises from all the differences together, where zero is on the arrow and why the whole arrow projects into one circle. The similarity with the construction of the Birth of Dimensions model is shown. Section 8 shows that the accumulated mismatch over the seams is Euler's sine at one half ( π ), while accumulation over the primes gives γ (Mertens); that the error of the prime count at a step is of the order of the square root of the mismatch of the frame; and that the transfer of the observer changes nothing if and only if all zeros lie on the axis 1/2 — this is the Hilbert — Pólya programme. Each seam is a right triangle in a circle: the centre along the line is the radius, the centre on the circle the cosine, the hole the sine, and sin² + cos² = 1. The author believes that this work can become a proof of the Riemann hypothesis; the missing step is to show that the unity of the process makes the transfer of the observer a symmetry. The work is laid out as a programme of proof: the missing step is formulated as a target statement resting on the birth of the arrow — a pure projection from one unit, the product over the primes. The missing step is also written as a statement about positivity: from Mertens' square 2(1 + cos θ )², which pushes the zeros away from 1, to the square of Weil's energy, which must hold them on ½ and forbid pairs of zeros on opposite sides of the circle. The work rests on classical results — Pell–Lagrange, Legendre's sieve, the explicit formula of Riemann and von Mangoldt — and proposes a new linking of them: the geometry of the seam as a model of the process linking the primes. The author's answer to Riemann's question is geometric: on each range chosen in a definite way, the process of the link of the primes is seen as the unit circle and a sinusoid around it; for his work the author regards this answer as a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, and what in it is accepted as an initial

summary: The judgments measured at the 3,000-token generation cap that back section 4.6 of the ablation paper. One file per condition, one line per (run, question, criterion), with the judge's verdict, the points the board assigns, the area of law and the criterion class — the same schema as version 1.0. Three constructions are covered at the new cap: the frozen grid, the full-coverage v3 corpus, and the ten-seed matched pair that isolates corpus form from token volume and composition. These judgments are additive to the 1,500-token-cap judgments of version 1.0, which still back tables 1 to 4; they do not replace them. 196 files. 0.33 GB uncompressed. Every file's path. size. line count and SHA-256 are in the included MANIFESTO.json ; the package carries its own README and licence.
title: Judgments of 180 trained conditions on a Brazilian Bar Examination benchmark (v1.1)

summary: This dataset accompanies the manuscript entitled "Cross-model TEAD inhibitor resistance programs and their clinical associations in pleural mesothelioma". The Excel workbook provides derived supplementary data supporting the cross-model analysis of TEAD inhibitor resistance in pleural mesothelioma. It includes: Table S1: Study cohorts, sample characteristics, and analysis roles. Table S2: Fixed gene-program memberships and scoring definitions. Table S3: Cross-model differential expression results for 15,508 comparable genes and pathway enrichment analyses. Table S4: Patient malignant-cell state comparisons and program coverage. Table S5: TCGA-MESO histological associations, expression correlations, and overall survival analyses. Table S6: Sensitivity analyses, model diagnostics, and spatial transcriptomic results. The public dataset retains the 223-gene Shared_up program, the 200-gene Hallmark EMT set, and the reported statistical results. A total of 675 third-party tS/tE and meS/meE gene-membership records were excluded from the public workbook because redistribution permissions could not be independently confirmed. Their original sources and reconstruction procedures are documented in the accompanying README. The dataset contains derived research results, not raw sequencing data or directly identifying patient information. Source datasets, analytical conventions, attribution, and reuse information are described in README.txt. The associated manuscript was prepared for submission to Clinical and Translational Oncology.

summary: Pretrained language models (LMs) remain unreliable on exact multi-digit arithmetic without gradient fine-tuning or external tool interpreters. We introduce closed-form, zero-gradient circuit-grafting primitives that compile deterministic computation directly into pretrained LM weights using zero training examples and zero runtime hooks, while bounding per-layer normalization drift and preserving natural-language (NL) competence. Our construction combines three analytical mechanisms: (1) two-layer Mellin-GLU quadrature over bias-free SwiGLU/GeGLU layers, turning unknown per-token RMSNorm scaling into translation along a log-spaced gate grid ($>250\times$ dynamic range) with IEEE 754 error bounds; (2) cross-token scale cancellation via signed Chebyshev Indefinite-RoPE self-sink attention and memoryless SiLU-antisymmetric GatedDeltaNet shifts; and (3) axis-aligned width extension ($d \to d+K$) with $\sqrt{d/(d+K)}$ norm compensation, Base-1000 canonical BPE emission, and differential $(+254,-256)$ tied unembeddings. An automated 5-stage compiler synthesizes 4-8 digit signed $\{+,-,\times\}$ circuits in constant $\mathsf{TC}^0$ depth alongside 3-literal Boolean (100%, $N=1{,}728$; plus 42-layer Gemma 4 E4B audits) and 5-bit Majority/Parity (100%) circuits. On 6-digit arithmetic ($N=1{,}200$, BF16), IBM Granite 4.2 3B (1.07M-1.33M active non-zeros, $\le 0.036\%$) and Alibaba Qwen 3.5 4B (2.25M-2.39M non-zeros, $\le 0.057\%$) reach 99.17% and 100.00% ALU-prefix accuracy (100% with an FP32 sidecar) and 98%-100% mid-sentence resumption, outperforming 12.8K-sample LoRA (42.2% / 61.7%, 0% inline continuation). A factorized block-sparse sidecar holds A100 memory at 7.89 / 10.65 GiB (4.60 / 8.14 GiB under INT8/INT4 + FP32 sidecar) while passing all 14/14 pre-registered $>2$K-token Tango splits ($N=4{,}392$; 0/11,134 OOD triggers).
title: A CPU Inside an LLM: Zero-Gradient Compilation of Exact Circuits into Pretrained Weights

summary: Resistive random-access memory (ReRAM)-based processing-in-memory (PIM) accelerators offer a highly efficient platform for parallel matrix-vector multiplications (VMM) in neural networks, leveraging analog computation, high density, low leakage, and non-volatility. However, their susceptibility to permanent faults, such as stuck-at-high (\textit{SaH}) and stuck-at-low (\textit{SaL}) resistance states, permanently corrupts the convolutional neural networks (CNNs) weights mapped onto ReRAM cell conductance values, thereby degrading inference accuracy and leading to system unreliability in safety-critical applications. Fault injection is a commonly used technique to assess the vulnerability of neural networks by systematically injecting faults into individual parameters and measuring the resulting accuracy degradation. Although this method is accurate, it is prohibitively time-consuming and computationally expensive, especially for large-scale CNNs. In this paper, we propose a fast, scalable, and analytical framework to quantify the fault vulnerability of convolutional neural networks deployed on ReRAM-based PIM accelerators. This method quantifies vulnerability at different granularities, including weights, kernels, and layers, without the need for exhaustive simulation, enabling the design of fault-tolerant accelerators for edge and safety-critical applications. The comparison between the results of the proposed vulnerability score (VS) metrics with performance metric of CNNs captured with fault injection simulations confirms the effectiveness of our proposed method. Unlike exhaustive fault injection, which requires days or weeks, whereas the proposed approach achieves a speedup of about $10^4\times-10^5\times$, enabling fast and accurate vulnerability analysis for large-scale CNNs within only a few minutes or hours.
title: Scalable fault vulnerability analysis for ReRAM-based process-in-memory CNN accelerators

summary: This study examines the relationship between age falsification in the Nigerian public service and youth unemployment, with specific reference to the National Assembly Service Commission from 2004 to 2024. The study adopts an extant review approach, drawing on existing empirical and theoretical literature to explore the prevalence, causes, and implications of age falsification within public institutions. The analysis is anchored on rational choice and anomie perspectives to explain individual motivations and systemic pressures that sustain the practice, while social restorative theory provides a framework for institutional response. Findings reveal that age falsification is widespread and driven by factors such as job insecurity, weak pension systems, poor record keeping, and ineffective enforcement mechanisms. The practice contributes significantly to workforce stagnation by delaying retirement and limiting employment opportunities for younger entrants. Evidence further shows that weak recruitment governance, patronage networks, and fragmented identity verification systems exacerbate the problem. Comparative analysis indicates that while Nigeria struggles with enforcement and verification gaps, countries such as the United Kingdom have reduced incentives for falsification through the removal of rigid retirement structures, Ghana has strengthened identity management through centralized biometric systems, and Rwanda has achieved greater control through early and comprehensive digitization of personnel records. The study concludes that age falsification is not merely an administrative irregularity but a structural governance issue with direct implications for youth employment and public sector efficiency. It recommends comprehensive reforms in verification systems, recruitment processes, and enforcement mechanisms to restore integrity and promote equitable access to public service employment.

title: Age Falsification in The Nigerian Public Service and Youth Unemployment: An Extant Review of The National Assembly Service Commission, 2004-2024

summary: Erman and Sam asked whether every integral point on a pure ray of the Boij-Söderberg cone is the Betti table of a finite length module over k[x,y,z] or over the enveloping algebra U of the Heisenberg Lie algebra; Jiang, Li, Sun, Wang, Xiao and Yu answered negatively. We study the point (1,2,2,1) on (0,e,3e,4e), excluded over k[x,y,z] and passing their test over U. It is realized by U/U(x^e,y^e) if and only if char k = 0 or char k >= 2e, and in characteristic 2 no module with at most one more relation than generators has finite length over U. In odd characteristic p we prove a criterion for pairs of forms with a central commutator, with explicit pure pairs for e = 0 or 1 modulo p, and pull-backs along endomorphisms of U. For the pairs x^e + alpha y^t, y^e + beta x^t we prove that coprimality conditions, two congruences and one scalar condition give the pure Hilbert function when p >= 2t, and the pure pair when one more coprimality holds; explicit short pairs are pure for p = 2e - 1 (every prime p >= 5) and for p = 2e - 3 (the primes below 2,000,000). Searches in weight-class strata, lists of forms, the filter for every exponent and the members fixed by the exchange of x and y settle the other pairs. The point is realized in every characteristic other than 2 for 2 <= e <= 16 except e = 11, where characteristic 3 is open. A census of the 220 rays with d_3 <= 12 over k[x,y,z] realizes the primitive point on 193 and excludes it on 12; in characteristic 0 the least counterexample has d_3 = 10. Source code, data and computational records: https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_RESEARCH (branch develop). The paper does not claim a negative answer to Question 6.1 of Erman and Sam, which is due to Jiang, Li, Sun, Wang, Xiao and Yu, and claims no priority for any other result.
title: Primitive Betti points over k[x,y,z] and the Heisenberg enveloping algebra: the point (1,2,2,1) on (0,e,3e,4e) fails only in characteristic 2 for 2 <= e <= 16 with e != 11, is realized whenever an odd prime p divides e(e-1) or equals 2e-1, and a census for d_3 <= 12

summary: On 20 November 2026 L. Alpöge posted a four-page note and a Lean 4 archive claiming a derivation of Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis: 175,187 files, 17.4 million lines, the three standard axioms, no human-readable proof. We read the archive against the one-bit normal form of the Riemann Hypothesis, public in our git repository since October 2026 in Lean and since August 2026 in prose. The headline is Mathlib's own statement. Its last step is the band reduction our Lean record states as one face of the normal form. Everything in it except one proposition was in our public Lean record first, and that proposition is the bit our record isolated and printed as its only premise. Its premise is the definition of ζ, which a law of logic proved in our file classifies as strictly stronger than the value, so the derivation is a tautology of that premise. A second Lean test shows the standard axioms cannot carry the bit: if the archive stands, the bit came out of ζ, through a window estimate on Tate–Shafarevich lengths that holds every program-generated proof in the archive. Both seals build silently in core Lean 4.19.0 and are printed whole. We close with a provenance ledger and a critique of the artifact as published.
title: The Bit in the Definition: A Lean Derivation of the Riemann Hypothesis, Its Tautology, and the Public Record It Lands In

summary: Action-Research Lessons Learned from a Dis|mis Administrative Incident This book is an action-research study of lessons learned from a dis|mis administrative incident . It uses the incident as a situated case through which to examine how administrative uncertainty, informational asymmetry, technological mediation, institutional inertia, and contested interpretation can affect cognition, expression, dignity, and public trust. The project is guided by the attached work’s progression from “Fundamental Rights At Risk” and “On Partiality” to “On Liberty of Thinking,” “On Inner Peace & Recensions,” “Introducing CogOps,” “On Cognitive Health,” and the case studies on judicial impartiality, private affiliations, oath conflict, and SIS–Schengen transparency. The table of contents therefore provides the project’s conceptual route: from rights and institutional balance, through cognition and inner life, towards administrative, technological, and governance risks. The research does not present the personal account as conclusive proof of intentional wrongdoing. Rather, it treats the incident as a source of lessons learned, research questions, provisional concepts, and methodological warnings . The purpose is to distinguish observed events from interpretation, allegation, metaphor, and hypothesis while asking how comparable vulnerabilities might arise in other administrative environments. From rights to cognition The first part of the research begins with fundamental rights and institutional impartiality. In the chapter “On Partiality,” the attached work states: “It is also relational: whenever you are judged, a relationship is involved.” This proposition provides an important starting point for action research. An administrative decision is not only a technical act; it occurs within a relationship involving a citizen, a public agent, an institution, a body of law, and a surrounding informational environment. A failure of communication, an absence of reasons, a delay, or an inability to challenge a decision can therefore produce effects extending beyond the immediate administrative matter. The same chapter gives a second guiding image: “We are all equal under gravity.” Here, the balance functions as a non-technical symbol of equality, impartiality, and the need to prevent power from becoming detached from rights. Within the proposed research, this image is translated into questions about procedural fairness, equal access to information, the visibility of relevant affiliations, and the ability of affected persons to participate meaningfully in decisions concerning them. Liberty of thinking The chapter “On Liberty of Thinking” provides the closest conceptual foundation for the study of inner ecology. It describes writing and symbolic expression as a means of creating distance from an overwhelming or difficult experience: “Being able to formulate, express, and work on things symbolically helps us create emotional distance.” This observation is central to the action-research design. Recension, writing, drawing, multilingual expression, and documentary reconstruction are not treated merely as literary devices. They are used as practical research instruments through which an individual experience can be reviewed, organised, questioned, and made accessible to others. The chapter also describes expression as a form of shelter: “It was therefore a genuine shelter to be able to express ourselves through this ‘way of the pencil.’” Adapted to a CERREV-oriented research programme, this becomes a question about the conditions under which citizens and public agents can formulate disagreement without escalation. The research therefore examines whether accessible forms of expression can reduce informational dissonance, support self-correction, and create a more reliable basis
title: THE ASYLUM : From Soft Corruption to Disruptive Cognitive Operations: Reaching Inner Peace

summary: This publication specifies and documents a researcher-directed methodology for AI-assisted mathematical discovery, developed within the independent mathematical research program of Structural Stability Science (SSS). The methodology exhibits continuity with, but remains distinct from, the originating Structural Identification Method (SIM; Tonucci, 2026). It integrates scientific identification and continuing research direction, AI-assisted scientific interlocution, mathematical formalization and analytical development, computational implementation, dependency-preserving adjudication, and source-specific contribution provenance. Scientific interlocution consists of sustained technical exchange through which mathematical questions, interpretations, hypotheses, dependencies, counterexamples, proposed constructions, and candidate proof routes are examined. Researcher-directed decisions concerning problem selection, investigative objectives, mathematical evaluation, and research-program continuity remain distinguishable from AI-generated mathematical proposals, calculations, arguments, critiques, and technical representations. Both retain identifiable contributions under their documented source conditions. The methodology specifies two complementary records. The mathematical claim record preserves originating questions, hypotheses, conclusion scope, dependencies, supporting evidence, and verification findings. The source-to-contribution record preserves originating research-state continuity, earlier research artifacts, prompt-visible AI operations, researcher-directed decisions, branch reconciliation, attribution correction, and publication outcomes. These records retain distinct evidentiary functions. A prompt-response transcript documents operations expressed within an interaction; it does not independently establish the complete originating research state or the provenance of the continuing investigation. The originating mathematical investigation concerned order preservation under real extension, admissibility, counterexamples, and mathematical continuation. The documented research sequence subsequently encompassed adjoint observation gain, analytical extensions, exact reference-state rank, restricted Fourier observability, conditional Gramian transfer, time-dependent observability, high-frequency obstruction, nonlinear terminal-target correction, and Navier–Stokes continuation questions, together with the organization of Adjoint Gain Theory. summary: AQUA-PRITHVI v2 expands the previously published metadata-only aquatic Harmonized Landsat and Sentinel-2 (HLS) corpus into a reusable multispectral research dataset, accompanied by harmonized in situ water-quality observations and reproducibility tools. The aquatic HLS corpus comprises 29,079 original compressed NPZ microshards containing 169,907 materialized patch-period samples. A quality-controlled catalog identifies 169,429 approved observations from 2,389 spatial patches across eight global regions during 2018–2024. Each approved observation references six HLS reflectance bands (blue, green, red, narrow NIR, SWIR1, SWIR2), 224 × 224 pixels at 30 m spatial resolution, together with valid-pixel and water masks. Spatially independent train, validation and test partitions are provided. The original NPZ archives may also contain excluded observations; only records identified as approved in the accompanying catalog should be treated as quality-controlled samples. The companion water-quality dataset integrates 2,107,785 harmonized observations from CONAGUA RENAMECA (Mexico) and AquaMatch (United States and territories), covering chlorophyll-a, total suspended solids, turbidity and water transparency where available. Source provenance, measurement units, censoring information and quality indicators are preserved. The release also provides Python tools for reading HLS tensors, preparing candidate water-quality labels and planning satellite-scene searches. These tools support the future construction of reproducible HLS–in situ matchup datasets. Important limitation: The harmonized in situ observations are not yet paired with satellite scenes. The monthly HLS composites used for aquatic domain-adaptive pretraining must not be interpreted as same-day satellite matchups. Valid supervised matchups require independent scene-level temporal matching, radiometric quality control and spatially independent evaluation. This resource is intended to support aquatic remote sensing, self-supervised representation learning, reproducible geospatial machine learning and research on satellite-based water-quality assessment. Original datasets retain their respective provenance, attribution and reuse conditions. Related Research Resources This dataset is part of the AQUA-PRITHVI research ecosystem , which integrates aquatic satellite observations, domain-adapted geospatial foundation models and reproducible scientific workflows. Trained foundation model — Hugging Face: https://huggingface.co/freddyvillota/AQUA-PRITHVI-EO-2.0-300M-TL The repository provides the aquatic-domain-adapted Prithvi-EO-2.0-300M-TL model weights, model documentation and loading instructions for aquatic multispectral representation learning and spectral reconstruction. Source code and scientific documentation — GitHub: https://github.com/FreddyHVG/AQUA-PRITHVI-DAPT-V2 The repository contains methodological documentation, preprocessing workflows, quality-control procedures, experimental results and reproducibility resources. Its availability does not imply validated predictive performance for chlorophyll-a, suspended solids or other water-quality variables. summary: Code2Video uses agent-authored 3D proxies to guide video generation, enabling explicit control over structure and dynamics. However, how to construct proxies and prompts for optimal downstream quality remains underexplored, as do the capabilities and limitations of this paradigm. Through controlled experiments and blinded human evaluation, we study proxy granularity, physics simulation, and prompting. The results reveal task-dependent trade-offs: coarse proxies favor natural motion, while medium-grained proxies favor consistency. Physics simulation and proxy-aligned prompting further improve average quality. Guided by these findings, we introduce Coda-DaVinci, a task-adaptive agentic framework for Code2Video generation that selects between proxy-guided and direct generation, adapts modeling granularity to each entity, and coordinates simulation with proxy-grounded prompting. Its multi-agent harness preserves scene assets and guides repairs through visual inspection and independent review. Experiments demonstrate leading instruction following on VTR and scene consistency on R2M, improved physical plausibility over direct generation, and higher visual realism than the compared Code2Video baselines. Long-video evaluations further show gains in event structure and consistency across successive interactions, while revealing limitations in transition stability and adherence to scene settings.
title: Coda-DaVinci: Reimagining Video Generation with Code2Video

summary: Multimodal trajectory forecasting must cover diverse future behaviors without sacrificing dynamical coherence. Most generative forecasters evolve frame-wise positions directly, leaving the relationships among position, velocity, and acceleration implicit. We present SpecFlow, a conditional flow-matching framework that treats the Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) coefficients of future accelerations as its generative state. SpecFlow learns a transport from Gaussian noise to acceleration spectra and reconstructs velocity and position through fixed analytical integration initialized by the last observed state. A joint phase-space objective supervises all three kinematic levels. To represent destination uncertainty without future information, an endpoint predictor produces candidate destinations and confidence scores solely from observed context, and the highest-confidence candidate conditions the spectral denoiser. Alternating attention over trajectory hypotheses and agents captures multimodality and interaction. Under best-of-20 evaluation, SpecFlow achieves average minADE/minFDE of 0.15/0.22 on ETH/UCY, 0.69/0.86 at four seconds on NBA, and 7.38/11.57 on SDD. It establishes state-of-the-art results across all five ETH/UCY scenes and achieves the lowest four-second ADE on NBA with a tied-best FDE, while remaining competitive on SDD. Together, these results demonstrate that acceleration-spectrum flow matching provides an effective structured generative state across smooth pedestrian motion, coordinated multi-agent sports dynamics, and heterogeneous outdoor trajectories. Code will be made publicly available.
title: SpecFlow: Flow Matching in the Acceleration Spectrum for Multi-Agent Trajectory Forecasting

summary: Effective travel planning requires handling multiple information sources, managing constraints, and tailoring recommendations to user preferences. While LLMs have introduced dynamic, context-aware decision-making, single-agent models often struggle with complex multi-step reasoning, constraint adherence, and modular execution. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hierarchical multi-agent framework where a supervising chatbot agent coordinates specialized agents for schedule validation, user query formulation, real-time data retrieval, and constraint-aware itinerary generation. By integrating LLM reasoning, external APIs, and iterative refinement mechanisms based on a deterministic, multi-dimensional scoring framework, our approach ensures adaptability, efficiency, and personalization. Evaluations on the well-known TravelPlanner benchmark demonstrate improvements in Budget Constraint planning by 10\%, wider constraints set-based planning by 25\%, and personalized planning results by 45\%. compared to the ReAct baseline. Our code is available at https://github.com/nimashaklaa/TravelPlanner_Research
title: LM-based Personalized Travel Planner

summary: Following AFTD's negative answer dated November 5, 2026, to Hausmann's Question 5.4 in Weighted Max Cut in Subcubic Graphs (arXiv:2611.05178v1, Section 5), we give a different counterexample with an exact residual-order calculation: the generalized Petersen graph GP(7,2) has odd girth five, but deleting any independent set leaves a component with at least four vertices. We prove this by classifying its maximal independent sets into five symmetry classes. The bound four is attained on this graph. The same classification gives an obstruction to the nonempty-independent-side version of Question 5.3; its printed quantifiers admit an empty-side solution.
title: Residual order four in GP(7,2): an alternative proof for Hausmann's Question 5.4 (arXiv:2611.05178v1, Section 5), after AFTD (2026)

We prove this by classifying its maximal independent sets into five symmetry classes. The bound four is attained on this graph. The same classification gives an obstruction to the nonempty-independent-side version of Question 5.3; its printed quantifiers admit an empty-side solution.
title: Residual order four in GP(7,2): an alternative proof for Hausmann's Question 5.4 (arXiv:2611.05178v1, Section 5), after AFTD (2026)

summary: Abstract Purpose: Glioblastoma immunotherapy trials routinely assess tumor immunity based on a single surgical biopsy. We wanted to know how often biopsy location would reverse a relatively immune-rich or immune-poor classification. We also wanted to know whether CD8 T cell expression correlated with antigen-presenting gene expression and which immune programs remain consistent across regions after accounting for overall leukocyte infiltration. Methods: We scored 14 predefined immune expression programs across 75 magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)–localized, nonnecrotic biopsies from 19 patients with isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH)–wild-type glioblastoma, alongside 122 microdissected samples from 10 glioblastomas and two multiregion hepatocellular carcinoma cohorts. Intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) measured regional agreement relative to between-patient differences before and after adjusting for a 12-gene leukocyte score. Results: Regional scores fell on both sides of the fixed 141-biopsy reference mean in 7 of 19 patients (37%) for CD8 expression and 7 of 19 for leukocytes; only two crossed both. Within tumors, CD8 tracked supportive and inhibitory programs equally (mean r = 0.37 and 0.36) but barely tracked major histocompatibility complex class I (MHC-I) transcripts (r = 0.06). Leukocyte adjustment lowered median program ICC from 0.56 to 0.34. Interferon-associated expression retained the highest adjusted point estimate (0.70), though separation from MHC-I (0.47) remained uncertain; additional tumor-purity adjustment yielded similar ICCs (0.66 and 0.62). Conclusion: Biopsy location alone can reverse a glioblastoma’s relative immune-abundance classification. Measuring CD8, interferon, antigen-presentation, and inhibitory programs together across anatomically documented regions separates shared tumor-level features from local variation.
tags: Glioblastoma; Tumor microenvironment; Intratumoral heterogeneity; Tissue biomarkers; CD8 T lymphocytes; Interferon signaling
title: What a single biopsy reveals and misses about the glioblastoma immune microenvironment: Regional reproducibility of immune expression programs

summary: We extend Su's (2026) proof of Peter Bala's conjectures in OEIS A281428, COMMENTS, items 1–2 (displayed March 3, 2026), with factorial bounds and sharp onsets for the two accompanying examples. For a(n)=(2n)![x^(2n)]C(x), we prove v_p(a(n)) >= v_p((2n)!) for every prime p >= 5. The proof combines integral exponential coefficients with ordinary coefficients in Z[1/6], using the inverse cubic u-u^3/3=x. The exact eventual-zero onset modulo 385 is 6; modulo 27, the least eventual period is 18 and its earliest onset is 2. The same argument gives factorial bounds for every polynomial in the two differential-system solutions, including the companion A281427 and A052502.
title: Factorial bounds and sharp onsets for A281428: extending Su (2026) on Bala's COMMENTS, items 1–2

summary: Reconstructing a fragmentary manuscript of a known text rests on prior knowledge that editors apply implicitly and never evaluate. We formalise this knowledge as four priors (the reference text, the scribe's orthography and letter metrics, the physical geometry of the roll, and a rule for reading ambiguous ink) and combine them with large language model (LLM) agents and a constrained alignment model in a three-stage pipeline: reading, placement and layout. We evaluate it on the Greek Deuteronomy roll P. Fouad 266b (Rahlfs 848), which survives in some 140 fragments. An LLM agent, tuned by reflective prompt evolution, transcribes the plates and restores them against the reference text, missing 1 of 943 present letters on held-out plates. Fragments are placed by a banded, information-weighted edit distance with scribal substitution costs, chained across rows by a line-advance model and committed only above a confidence threshold. On a two-fold, plate-level split the placement model places 88% of held-out units (110 of 125) with no false placement (95% upper bound on the error rate about 3%). A deterministic constraint solver then rebuilds 85 columns that keep all 6,736 inked letters at their text positions. Unplaced units are mostly too short to place; the four that no setting places depart in wording from both reference texts, so the model's failures locate textual variants rather than errors. Transferred unchanged to a second roll, P. Fouad 266c (847), it places one unidentified fragment.
title: Reconstructing a Fragmentary Text from Priors: Language-Model Agents and Learned Alignment for P. Fouad 266b (848)
