summary: Reconstruction-based anomaly detection on the NASA CMAPSS FD001 turbofan dataset. An LSTM autoencoder trained on healthy sliding windows is compared on 20 held-out engines with a cycle-count score, PCA reconstruction, an Isolation Forest and a one-class SVM, with bootstrap intervals over engines, paired comparisons of warning time at equal false-alarm rates and a causal alarm rule. The model is served through a typed FastAPI service and a Streamlit demo in a multi-stage Docker stack.
title: Anomaly Detection API: Autoencoder + FastAPI + Docker

For a quasi-elastic response, strain is the ratio of stress to modulus under a declared small-strain regime. Each door begins with a distinct local investigation and asks why that problem matters, how the most serious competing explanation could account for the visible pattern, and what a successor could do with a simple independent witness. Across gel stiffness, migration, degradation, pore transport and remodeling, the language and scale change. Controllers must abstain when calibration disappears. Hardware or material intervention cannot proceed merely because a prediction model is confident. Each door begins with a distinct local investigation and asks why that problem matters, how the most serious competing explanation could account for the visible pattern, and what a successor could do with a simple independent witness. Across gel stiffness, migration, degradation, pore transport and remodeling, the language and scale change. Some doors begin from an intriguing contour, others from a physical contradiction or a failed denominator. Some describe a world in which swelling accounts for everything. Others imagine a pore network that is beautiful but disconnected, an apparently motile cell that is actually being carried by its gel, or a stable feedback trace that conceals tissue identity loss. Their future plans ask for blind sample exchange, matched budget controls, withheld perturbations, new batches, sealed negative specimens and automatic refusal. The failure scenario is therefore not an embarrassment; it is an inheritance. The archive should preserve it with the same care as the favored result. Their names suggest instrument exchanges, counterfactual matrix libraries, pore-network tomography challenges, mechanical memory loops, independent material reference standards and new methods for storing negative outcomes. Each idea includes a minimum test and a reason to retire it. In a mature autonomous experimental environment, this has consequences beyond documentation. Controllers must abstain when calibration disappears. Hardware or material intervention cannot proceed merely because a prediction model is confident. Human permission, biological source provenance and contamination controls remain external authority constraints. A system that pauses when its assumptions collapse is often more useful than one that always returns an answer. The same principle applies to writing and publication: a research program can be inspirational without presenting synthetic models as achieved biological capabilities. The open scientific record grows stronger when authors state what has not yet been built, measured or validated. In a material-focused family, the same argument has multiple forms. An excellent modulus map is not morphogenesis. A migrating centroid is not necessarily a migrating cell. Published work on organoid hydrogels, synthetic matrices, viscoelasticity and dynamic mechanics offers methodological precedents. Those sources do not experimentally verify the five new STARLI couplings. This research family offers a plan for making such claims testable, including measurements, strong baselines, uncertainty accounting, data reconstruction and stopping conditions. The long-term goal is not to build a library of conclusions that cannot be questioned, but an open architecture of precise experimental doors. Each generation should be free to improve the questions, reject a mistaken mechanism and keep whatever remains genuinely useful. Let beauty have the ability to continue happening. A fall in wet weight is not always polymer cleavage. A large apparent flux is not necessarily oxygen supply to living tissue. And a stable material signal is not proof of organ-specific homeostasis. Published work on organoid hydrogels, synthetic matrices, viscoelasticity and dynamic mechanics offers methodological precedents. Those sources do not experimentally verify the five new STARLI couplings. This research family offers a plan for making such claims testable, including measurements, strong baselines, uncertainty accounting, data reconstruction and stopping conditions. The long-term goal is not to build a library of conclusions that cannot be questioned, but an open architecture of precise experimental doors. Each generation should be free to improve the questions, reject a mistaken mechanism and keep whatever remains genuinely useful. Let beauty have the ability to continue happening. summary: The work continues the geometric model of the distribution of primes [2] and the work “The Number Arrow and the Line 1/2” [1]. The geometric formula for the number of odd composites up to p², N(p) = 1 + 3(p − 1)(p − 3)/8, is treated as the first level of a ladder in which the scale is squared at each step: 5² → 5⁴ → 5⁸ → 5¹⁶. It is shown that this formula is the best quadratic formula for the level up to 5⁴: it is exact everywhere except for one compensating pair of misses (p = 15 and p = 17). The quadratic lattice of a level holds up to the basis 7 inclusive and breaks down right after it. The error of the formula splits into two superimposed tables: a smooth level correction and an oscillation which, in the explicit formula, is a sum of cosines over the zeros of the zeta function. The main result is a law of levels, checked on exact values of π (x) up to 3³² ≈ 1.9 · 10¹⁵: when the scale is squared, the relative error of the prime count is squared, and the error itself is inverse to the linear scale p = √x obtained from the difference of squares: ε · p stays of order one at all checked steps. The law holding at all steps is equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis (von Koch, 1901). The author puts forward the hypothesis that the self-similarity of the ladder may become a route to its proof: for this one must show that the step structure itself does not allow ε · p to grow faster than a power of the logarithm. This step is named but not taken. The method may become the basis for an exact count of prime density by levels without the exponential and the logarithm in the level formula. Section 7 gives a geometric reading for a reader without mathematical training: why the basis of the model is 2, 3, 5, 7, how the seam 8–9 links the linear and the quadratic levels, why the centres of the seam differ by exactly ¼ and how π arises from all the differences together, where zero is on the arrow and why the whole arrow projects into one circle. The similarity with the construction of the Birth of Dimensions model is shown. Section 8 shows that the accumulated mismatch over the seams is Euler's sine at one half ( π ), while accumulation over the primes gives γ (Mertens); that the error of the prime count at a step is of the order of the square root of the mismatch of the frame; and that the transfer of the observer changes nothing if and only if all zeros lie on the axis 1/2 — this is the Hilbert — Pólya programme. Each seam is a right triangle in a circle: the centre along the line is the radius, the centre on the circle the cosine, the hole the sine, and sin² + cos² = 1. The author believes that this work can become a proof of the Riemann hypothesis; the missing step is to show that the unity of the process makes the transfer of the observer a symmetry. The work is laid out as a programme of proof: the missing step is formulated as a target statement resting on the birth of the arrow — a pure projection from one unit, the product over the primes. The missing step is also written as a statement about positivity: from Mertens' square 2(1 + cos θ )², which pushes the zeros away from 1, to the square of Weil's energy, which must hold them on ½ and forbid pairs of zeros on opposite sides of the circle. The work rests on classical results — Pell–Lagrange, Legendre's sieve, the explicit formula of Riemann and von Mangoldt — and proposes a new linking of them: the geometry of the seam as a model of the process linking the primes. The author's answer to Riemann's question is geometric: on each range chosen in a definite way, the process of the link of the primes is seen as the unit circle and a sinusoid around it; for his work the author regards this answer as a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, and what in it is accepted as an initial
title: The Fractal Ladder of Prime Density: Quadratic Scale and Linear Error

summary: This dataset accompanies the manuscript entitled "Cross-model TEAD inhibitor resistance programs and their clinical associations in pleural mesothelioma". The Excel workbook provides derived supplementary data supporting the cross-model analysis of TEAD inhibitor resistance in pleural mesothelioma. It includes: Table S1: Study cohorts, sample characteristics, and analysis roles. Table S2: Fixed gene-program memberships and scoring definitions. Table S3: Cross-model differential expression results for 15,508 comparable genes and pathway enrichment analyses. Table S4: Patient malignant-cell state comparisons and program coverage. Table S5: TCGA-MESO histological associations, expression correlations, and overall survival analyses. Table S6: Sensitivity analyses, model diagnostics, and spatial transcriptomic results. The public dataset retains the 223-gene Shared_up program, the 200-gene Hallmark EMT set, and the reported statistical results. A total of 675 third-party tS/tE and meS/meE gene-membership records were excluded from the public workbook because redistribution permissions could not be independently confirmed. Their original sources and reconstruction procedures are documented in the accompanying README. The dataset contains derived research results, not raw sequencing data or directly identifying patient information. Source datasets, analytical conventions, attribution, and reuse information are described in README.txt. The associated manuscript was prepared for submission to Clinical and Translational Oncology.
title: Derived supplementary data for cross-model TEAD inhibitor resistance programs in pleural mesothelioma

summary: Version v6.0-jbi accompanies the submission of the article to the Journal of Biomedical Informatics (Elsevier). It adds manuscript_jbi/, which builds the shortened journal version (body of about 5,980 words, two figures, six tables) and its supplementary material from the v5.0 manuscript, a graphical abstract (figures/Graphical_abstract_JBI_DNFR.png), and check_numbers.py, which verifies that every number in the journal version occurs in the v5.0 manuscript or supplement generated from the result files. It also adds the ratings of a second, blinded clinical rater (a physician; results/expert_review2_filled.xlsx with the rater’s name withheld, and the agreement and discrimination statistics in results/expert_review2.json). Models, data and the main results are unchanged from v5.0. Code, derived data and result files for Differentiable Neuro-Fuzzy Reasoning (DNFR), a path-based link predictor that learns degree-aware edge memberships, a Schweizer–Sklar t-norm per metapath and metapath reliabilities, and aggregates paths by noisy-OR, used as an instrument for a controlled component analysis on medical knowledge graphs. Tasks: drug repurposing in Hetionet v1.0 and PrimeKG, disease–symptom prediction in Hetionet and in the graded health knowledge graph of Rotmensch et al. (2017), and a secondary test on a NHANES fuzzy relation, under leave-dyad-out random and disease-centred splits. Comparators: fixed t-norms, component ablations, restarts of the t-norm parameter, DWPC with logistic regression (with and without degree and prior features), a degree-preserving edge prior, popularity, AnyBURL, truncated and soft-thresholded SVD and knowledge graph embeddings. Version v4.0 (fourth revision) completes 10 leave-dyad-out splits on Hetionet compound–treats–disease for the fixed Hamacher product, fixed degree terms, annealing, frozen memberships, DNFR 2.0, the shared and fixed t-norm parameters and AnyBURL; adds an ablation without metapaths that contain the target relation, a fact-level attribution of DWPC-LR next to DNFR's, the evidence share by metapath class, an information-content check with matched spread, a profile of the t-norm parameter extended to p > 0 and run on Hetionet disease–symptom, a tuning grid for NBFNet, a script that re-runs a key result from a clean checkout (scripts/verify_clean.sh), and the sheet for a clinical assessment of the explanations (dnfr/expert_sheet.py, dnfr/expert_summary.py). The secondary NHANES test was removed from the article. Version v3.0-rev3 (third revision) added DNFR 2.0, four refinements tested one at a time and in combination (overlap-aware aggregation, Gumbel-softmax operator choice, an information-content hub discount and membership annealing), a fixed t-norm selected on validation data, a converged L-BFGS profile of the t-norm parameter, an unbounded parameterisation, a compact NBFNet baseline, an exact edge-level Shapley attribution of the explanations, a mechanistic classification of the drug-repurposing explanations, a sparsity variant that keeps the target relation, and 10 leave-dyad-out splits for the main comparisons on Hetionet compound–treats–disease, Hetionet disease–symptom and the graded health knowledge graph. Version 1.1.0 (second revision) added a profile analysis of the t-norm parameter, training without early stopping, additional splits, equivalence tests, the edge prior, share-matched and edge-level explanation tests, unit tests and the script that builds the manuscript from the statistics files. Includes per-query ranks for every method and split, trained models, path explanations, and the statistics files from which every number in the manuscript is read. Hetionet and PrimeKG are downloaded by download_data.py with MD5 checks.
title: Code and derived results for: Which parts of a neuro-fuzzy path reasoner should be learned? A controlled component analysis on medical knowledge graphs

It also adds the ratings of a second, blinded clinical rater (a physician; results/expert_review2_filled.xlsx with the rater’s name withheld, and the agreement and discrimination statistics in results/expert_review2.json). Models, data and the main results are unchanged from v5.0. Code, derived data and result files for Differentiable Neuro-Fuzzy Reasoning (DNFR), a path-based link predictor that learns degree-aware edge memberships, a Schweizer–Sklar t-norm per metapath and metapath reliabilities, and aggregates paths by noisy-OR, used as an instrument for a controlled component analysis on medical knowledge graphs. Tasks: drug repurposing in Hetionet v1.0 and PrimeKG, disease–symptom prediction in Hetionet and in the graded health knowledge graph of Rotmensch et al. (2017), and a secondary test on a NHANES fuzzy relation, under leave-dyad-out random and disease-centred splits. Comparators: fixed t-norms, component ablations, restarts of the t-norm parameter, DWPC with logistic regression (with and without degree and prior features), a degree-preserving edge prior, popularity, AnyBURL, truncated and soft-thresholded SVD and knowledge graph embeddings. Version v4.0 (fourth revision) completes 10 leave-dyad-out splits on Hetionet compound–treats–disease for the fixed Hamacher product, fixed degree terms, annealing, frozen memberships, DNFR 2.0, the shared and fixed t-norm parameters and AnyBURL; adds an ablation without metapaths that contain the target relation, a fact-level attribution of DWPC-LR next to DNFR's, the evidence share by metapath class, an information-content check with matched spread, a profile of the t-norm parameter extended to p > 0 and run on Hetionet disease–symptom, a tuning grid for NBFNet, a script that re-runs a key result from a clean checkout (scripts/verify_clean.sh), and the sheet for a clinical assessment of the explanations (dnfr/expert_sheet.py, dnfr/expert_summary.py). The secondary NHANES test was removed from the article. Version v3.0-rev3 (third revision) added DNFR 2.0, four refinements tested one at a time and in combination (overlap-aware aggregation, Gumbel-softmax operator choice, an information-content hub discount and membership annealing), a fixed t-norm selected on validation data, a converged L-BFGS profile of the t-norm parameter, an unbounded parameterisation, a compact NBFNet baseline, an exact edge-level Shapley attribution of the explanations, a mechanistic classification of the drug-repurposing explanations, a sparsity variant that keeps the target relation, and 10 leave-dyad-out splits for the main comparisons on Hetionet compound–treats–disease, Hetionet disease–symptom and the graded health knowledge graph. Version 1.1.0 (second revision) added a profile analysis of the t-norm parameter, training without early stopping, additional splits, equivalence tests, the edge prior, share-matched and edge-level explanation tests, unit tests and the script that builds the manuscript from the statistics files. Includes per-query ranks for every method and split, trained models, path explanations, and the statistics files from which every number in the manuscript is read. summary: Electrons can change subband in quantum transport, holes can be solved by it too, the package makes quality triangle meshes, the quantum channel on meshes keeps band steps where the mesh puts them, and scattering lifetimes and mobility of a 2D gas are computed from its own wavefunction. The examples print what they printed before, except example 58 (the quantum channel on a mesh, now closer to the tensor grid); examples 62 to 65 are new. Added Device.negf(..., coupled_modes=M) : NEGF in coupled mode space, the lowest M states of every column joined by their overlaps, so electrons change subband where the channel's profile across it changes; with all modes it is the full 2D problem (ballistic only). kpenvelope.negf adds Slab , slab_transport and lead_surface_green (leads by decimation). Device.negf(..., carrier="holes") : the holes of a QuantumChannel with holes=(m_z, m_inplane, ...) , with or without scattering, uncoupled or coupled; Slab(mass_x=) for a mass along x of its own. kpenvelope.mesh.quality_mesh(regions, h, min_angle) : quality meshes of polygon regions by Delaunay refinement (every boundary and interface an edge, no node in a segment's diametral circle, smallest angle up to 34 degrees, a size field). kpenvelope.scattering.Subband : transport and quantum lifetimes and the mobility of one subband from acoustic phonons, alloy disorder, interface roughness (Gaussian or exponential correlation) and screened charged impurities (sheets or profiles), with your material numbers. Changed The quantum channel on meshes: the material on each sample of a line is the mean over its share of the line. Before, a node on a band step took its whole share from the one region it belongs to, which moved the step by up to half a spacing, differently on each line: on a quality mesh the confined sheet was 1.6 to 2.0 percent off a fine tensor grid at every mesh size; now 0.54, 0.20 and 0.10 percent at 1, 0.5 and 0.25 nm. On a mesh made from a tensor grid with a band step inside the window, the result now differs from the tensor grid's by that half-spacing effect of the tensor grid. Device(grid=...) refuses nodes closer than 1e-6 nm with a clear message (a near-duplicate node made the Poisson solve fail). Not included (see docs/limits.md) Scattering in coupled mode space; phonon self-energies in NEGF; NEGF on triangle meshes; both carriers in NEGF at once. Polar optical phonon and intersubband scattering in the lifetimes. The hot-electron model's limit at zero relaxation time with velocity saturation, the plasma's own chemistry, oxide shapes that follow the flow, elasticity, electronic stopping beyond Lindhard-Scharff, tunneling paths that bend with the field, tunneling and heat inside one Newton solve, and the Peltier heat in Fermi-Dirac form are as in 0.26.0. The app does not have the new features yet. Checks (tests) 15 new tests (372 in all; docs/checks.md has the tolerances): the leads by decimation against the exact chain lead; coupled mode space against the dense real-space inverse, mode counting, the sum of chains without mixing, and the uncoupled device; holes against the mirror image of electrons and the QuantumChannel's holes; a slab with a mass along x of its own; the quality mesh's angles, areas, conformity and diametral circles, and a ring resistor converging at second order; the quantum channel on a quality mesh against a fine tensor grid; the scattering rates against closed forms (Fang-Howard and square-well overlaps, Price's acoustic rate, the alloy rate), an independent integral with the closed-form Fang-Howard form factors, the far-away-charge limits, the Hellmann-Feynman shift of a level, and the thermal average. All 65 documented examples were rerun.
title: kpenvelope: interface charges, misfit-dislocation charge, two-dimensional electron and hole gases and device curves of wurtzite nitride stacks, with a self-consistent six-band k.p solver

summary: Replication package for the paper "Collation Drift and Turkish Case Mapping in PostgreSQL: Effects on Lookups and Uniqueness". It contains the scripts, the Dockerfile, the raw outputs, and the decision log of the PostgreSQL 18.6 experiments: emulated and real (Ubuntu 18.04, 20.04, 22.04) changes of glibc collation data under existing unique B-tree indexes, three repair paths, the C.UTF-8 sort order across Ubuntu releases, and a matrix of ten case-insensitive unique keys in six database locales. make numbers regenerates every number and both tables of the paper from the deposited results. Code: MIT License. Data and documentation: CC BY 4.0.

Contents: - pfi_bundle_analysis.py: analysis script (Python 3). - data/: four public input files: the HM Treasury dataset of PFI and PF2 projects as at 31 March 2025, the HM Treasury list of signed PFI projects (March 2012), NHS Digital ERIC 2015/16 PFI data and the Bank of England 10-year gilt yield series IUAAMNPY. - project_data.xlsx: derived contract-level data, including the hand-made link table between ERIC 2015/16 PFI sites and HM Treasury contracts. - README.txt: sources and instructions. Run: pip install pandas numpy scipy statsmodels matplotlib odfpy xlrd openpyxl, then python pfi_bundle_analysis.py (about 30 minutes; results are written to the folder out/). The input data are published under the Open Government Licence v3.0.

summary: A finite record can leave equally many states possible after each observation and still resolve one question perfectly while giving little information about another. For a specified answer map, the nonempty cells of its joint table with the record characterize exact recovery. If a state law is given, the largest cell mass in each row determines optimal one-guess accuracy. If only the record law and a statewise loss are given, row minima and maxima give attainable bounds on the mean loss. We prove the relations between fiber size, mass and conditional diversity, including their dependence on uniform input, and give finite witnesses to their limits. For composition and updates, we determine when a count or a next record follows from the retained information. Two dice give records of the same diversity but accuracies of one and one sixth for the same question. In an office occupancy series, an added sensor bit lowers training error, yet a fixed decoder incurs more errors in both test periods. summary: 中文摘要 空间旋转、观察者涡度、内部规范场的旋转结构以及时空挠率往往被放在同一概念框架中,但它们在对称性、规范变换和动力学上并不等价。本文综合一系列关于 “ 真实旋转自由度能否构成普通质量引力之必要动力学来源 ” 的模型检验,首先指出球对称单一时间类矢量场满足 ,因而其投影涡度为零;特定平直空间切片上的纯环向差分旋转度规还受到弱能量条件与零能量条件的限制。其次,以已知 Einstein–Yang–Mills 和 Einstein–Yang–Mills–Higgs 模型为对照,说明内部规范旋转能够形成正则、球对称的自引力构型,但并未导出独立的度规引力动力学。本文的主要技术焦点是固定空间三标架下三支 Abelian 横向矢量场的静态交换:当源仅由标量密度线性、局域解析地构成,并同时满足守恒及对角   不变性时,源顶点在零动量至少含一阶导数,树级源 — 源核不具有非零系数的   牛顿红外极点。与此对照,非局域横向投影   可在正的自由场能量下产生吸引性   静态核;带质量 Proca 空间源也可产生吸引的 Yukawa 势,但伴随非守恒源、优选切片或奇异的无质量极限。这些结果排除或限定了若干最小模型,却没有构造出局域、协变、健康且满足红移、光偏折、等效原理与引力波要求的完整旋转起源引力理论。 Abstract   — We critically synthesize a sequence of model-level investigations into whether a genuine rotational degree of freedom can be a necessary dynamical origin of ordinary gravity. Spatial coordinate rotation, the vorticity of a chosen timelike congruence, internal gauge curvature and spacetime torsion are treated as distinct objects. A spherically symmetric single timelike one-form is hypersurface orthogonal, whereas familiar Einstein–Yang–Mills–Higgs solutions demonstrate that non-Abelian internal structure can coexist with regular, positive-energy self-gravitating configurations without establishing a new origin of metric dynamics. Our central conditional result concerns a static triplet of positive-kinetic Abelian vector fields on a fixed spatial slice. If their conserved sources are linear in a scalar mass density, analytic near zero momentum and invariant under a diagonal , the tree-level source–source kernel has no Newtonian  infrared pole. A spatially nonlocal transverse-projection source provides an explicit counterexample to any broader impossibility claim: it produces an attractive static interaction, but presupposes an inverse Laplacian and a preferred slicing. Massive Proca couplings admit additional attractive Yukawa examples while raising different consistency issues. None of these constructions establishes a complete local, covariant and observationally viable theory in which spatial rotation necessarily generates all gravitational phenomena.

summary: 中文摘要 空间旋转、观察者涡度、内部规范场的旋转结构以及时空挠率往往被放在同一概念框架中,但它们在对称性、规范变换和动力学上并不等价。本文综合一系列关于 “ 真实旋转自由度能否构成普通质量引力之必要动力学来源 ” 的模型检验,首先指出球对称单一时间类矢量场满足 ,因而其投影涡度为零;特定平直空间切片上的纯环向差分旋转度规还受到弱能量条件与零能量条件的限制。其次,以已知 Einstein–Yang–Mills 和 Einstein–Yang–Mills–Higgs 模型为对照,说明内部规范旋转能够形成正则、球对称的自引力构型,但并未导出独立的度规引力动力学。本文的主要技术焦点是固定空间三标架下三支 Abelian 横向矢量场的静态交换:当源仅由标量密度线性、局域解析地构成,并同时满足守恒及对角   不变性时,源顶点在零动量至少含一阶导数,树级源 — 源核不具有非零系数的   牛顿红外极点。与此对照,非局域横向投影   可在正的自由场能量下产生吸引性   静态核;带质量 Proca 空间源也可产生吸引的 Yukawa 势,但伴随非守恒源、优选切片或奇异的无质量极限。这些结果排除或限定了若干最小模型,却没有构造出局域、协变、健康且满足红移、光偏折、等效原理与引力波要求的完整旋转起源引力理论。 Abstract   — We critically synthesize a sequence of model-level investigations into whether a genuine rotational degree of freedom can be a necessary dynamical origin of ordinary gravity. Spatial coordinate rotation, the vorticity of a chosen timelike congruence, internal gauge curvature and spacetime torsion are treated as distinct objects. A spherically symmetric single timelike one-form is hypersurface orthogonal, whereas familiar Einstein–Yang–Mills–Higgs solutions demonstrate that non-Abelian internal structure can coexist with regular, positive-energy self-gravitating configurations without establishing a new origin of metric dynamics. Our central conditional result concerns a static triplet of positive-kinetic Abelian vector fields on a fixed spatial slice. If their conserved sources are linear in a scalar mass density, analytic near zero momentum and invariant under a diagonal , the tree-level source–source kernel has no Newtonian  infrared pole. A spatially nonlocal transverse-projection source provides an explicit counterexample to any broader impossibility claim: it produces an attractive static interaction, but presupposes an inverse Laplacian and a preferred slicing. Massive Proca couplings admit additional attractive Yukawa examples while raising different consistency issues. None of these constructions establishes a complete local, covariant and observationally viable theory in which spatial rotation necessarily generates all gravitational phenomena.

summary: 中文摘要 空间旋转、观察者涡度、内部规范场的旋转结构以及时空挠率往往被放在同一概念框架中,但它们在对称性、规范变换和动力学上并不等价。本文综合一系列关于 “ 真实旋转自由度能否构成普通质量引力之必要动力学来源 ” 的模型检验,首先指出球对称单一时间类矢量场满足 ,因而其投影涡度为零;特定平直空间切片上的纯环向差分旋转度规还受到弱能量条件与零能量条件的限制。其次,以已知 Einstein–Yang–Mills 和 Einstein–Yang–Mills–Higgs 模型为对照,说明内部规范旋转能够形成正则、球对称的自引力构型,但并未导出独立的度规引力动力学。本文的主要技术焦点是固定空间三标架下三支 Abelian 横向矢量场的静态交换:当源仅由标量密度线性、局域解析地构成,并同时满足守恒及对角   不变性时,源顶点在零动量至少含一阶导数,树级源 — 源核不具有非零系数的   牛顿红外极点。与此对照,非局域横向投影   可在正的自由场能量下产生吸引性   静态核;带质量 Proca 空间源也可产生吸引的 Yukawa 势,但伴随非守恒源、优选切片或奇异的无质量极限。这些结果排除或限定了若干最小模型,却没有构造出局域、协变、健康且满足红移、光偏折、等效原理与引力波要求的完整旋转起源引力理论。 Abstract   — We critically synthesize a sequence of model-level investigations into whether a genuine rotational degree of freedom can be a necessary dynamical origin of ordinary gravity. Spatial coordinate rotation, the vorticity of a chosen timelike congruence, internal gauge curvature and spacetime torsion are treated as distinct objects. A spherically symmetric single timelike one-form is hypersurface orthogonal, whereas familiar Einstein–Yang–Mills–Higgs solutions demonstrate that non-Abelian internal structure can coexist with regular, positive-energy self-gravitating configurations without establishing a new origin of metric dynamics. Our central conditional result concerns a static triplet of positive-kinetic Abelian vector fields on a fixed spatial slice. If their conserved sources are linear in a scalar mass density, analytic near zero momentum and invariant under a diagonal , the tree-level source–source kernel has no Newtonian  infrared pole. A spatially nonlocal transverse-projection source provides an explicit counterexample to any broader impossibility claim: it produces an attractive static interaction, but presupposes an inverse Laplacian and a preferred slicing. Massive Proca couplings admit additional attractive Yukawa examples while raising different consistency issues. None of these constructions establishes a complete local, covariant and observationally viable theory in which spatial rotation necessarily generates all gravitational phenomena.

summary: This deposit contains synthetic benchmark inputs, mathematical specifications, computational artifacts, saved results, and validation materials supporting the manuscript “Evaluating Delivery-Fee Policies in Omnichannel Retailing with Integrated Fulfillment and Last-Mile Routing.” The materials are organized into two distinct evidence streams. The expected-demand stream contains the five-group benchmark inputs and the archived computational materials used for the fixed-price operational model and the separate descriptive ALNS-LP/Hybrid comparison on generated instances. The realized-order stream documents Construction A, in which customer choices are frozen as indivisible 0.5-order-equivalent orders and vehicle routes are represented over physical address–slot visits. It compares only tariff policies B and C across baseline and low-Store-inventory scenarios using 500 paired replications (2,000 MILP solves in total). All benchmark data are synthetic. No real customer records, personally identifiable information, or confidential retailer data are included. The expected-demand and realized-order formulations are complementary but are not algebraically equivalent. The 52-policy finite comparison belongs to the expected-demand formulation; the realized-order experiment compares only B and C and does not re-evaluate all 52 policies. Net delivery contribution (NDC) excludes merchandise margins and should not be interpreted as total retailer profit. The archived computational outputs and validation materials are preserved as saved evidence. Their inclusion does not mean that the historical experiments were rerun during deposit preparation. Title clarification: The current manuscript supported by this deposit is titled “Evaluating Delivery-Fee Policies in Omnichannel Retailing with Integrated Fulfillment and Last-Mile Routing.” The legacy expected-demand package contains a historical manuscript-context file bearing an earlier working title (version v0.3, dated 13 November 2026, explicitly marked “Not for submission”). This file is retained solely as historical provenance for the earlier computational evidence and does not represent the current manuscript or its title.
title: Research Data and Computational Materials for: Evaluating Delivery-Fee Policies in Omnichannel Retailing with Integrated Fulfillment and Last-Mile Routing

summary: AQUA-PRITHVI v2 expands the previously published metadata-only aquatic Harmonized Landsat and Sentinel-2 (HLS) corpus into a reusable multispectral research dataset, accompanied by harmonized in situ water-quality observations and reproducibility tools. The aquatic HLS corpus comprises 29,079 original compressed NPZ microshards containing 169,907 materialized patch-period samples. A quality-controlled catalog identifies 169,429 approved observations from 2,389 spatial patches across eight global regions during 2018–2024. Each approved observation references six HLS reflectance bands (blue, green, red, narrow NIR, SWIR1, SWIR2), 224 × 224 pixels at 30 m spatial resolution, together with valid-pixel and water masks. Spatially independent train, validation and test partitions are provided. The original NPZ archives may also contain excluded observations; only records identified as approved in the accompanying catalog should be treated as quality-controlled samples. The companion water-quality dataset integrates 2,107,785 harmonized observations from CONAGUA RENAMECA (Mexico) and AquaMatch (United States and territories), covering chlorophyll-a, total suspended solids, turbidity and water transparency where available. Source provenance, measurement units, censoring information and quality indicators are preserved. The release also provides Python tools for reading HLS tensors, preparing candidate water-quality labels and planning satellite-scene searches. These tools support the future construction of reproducible HLS–in situ matchup datasets. Important limitation: The harmonized in situ observations are not yet paired with satellite scenes. The monthly HLS composites used for aquatic domain-adaptive pretraining must not be interpreted as same-day satellite matchups. Valid supervised matchups require independent scene-level temporal matching, radiometric quality control and spatially independent evaluation. This resource is intended to support aquatic remote sensing, self-supervised representation learning, reproducible geospatial machine learning and research on satellite-based water-quality assessment. Original datasets retain their respective provenance, attribution and reuse conditions. Related Research Resources This dataset is part of the AQUA-PRITHVI research ecosystem , which integrates aquatic satellite observations, domain-adapted geospatial foundation models and reproducible scientific workflows. Trained foundation model — Hugging Face: https://huggingface.co/freddyvillota/AQUA-PRITHVI-EO-2.0-300M-TL The repository provides the aquatic-domain-adapted Prithvi-EO-2.0-300M-TL model weights, model documentation and loading instructions for aquatic multispectral representation learning and spectral reconstruction. Source code and scientific documentation — GitHub: https://github.com/FreddyHVG/AQUA-PRITHVI-DAPT-V2 The repository contains methodological documentation, preprocessing workflows, quality-control procedures, experimental results and reproducibility resources. Together, these resources enable researchers to access the aquatic HLS dataset, reuse the adapted foundation model, and reproduce or extend the associated scientific workflows. Note: The adapted model has been evaluated for aquatic spectral reconstruction. Its availability does not imply validated predictive performance for chlorophyll-a, suspended solids or other water-quality variables. summary: Replication package for The Persistence of Taxonomic Entailments in Evolving Biomedical Ontologies. Version 2 rebuilds the study on every official release of nine OBO ontologies (698 releases of SO, PATO, HP, DOID, CL, ENVO, OBA, UBERON and MONDO; 872,217 incident entailments) and analyses 250 Gene Ontology releases separately. It contains the release lists with their provenance, the entailment survival corpora, the extraction and analysis code, all result tables and figures, the HPO annotation file and both code sets of the qualitative sample. The commit-sampled corpus of version 0.1 (311 snapshots of eight ontologies) is retained for the sensitivity analyses. code/verify_revision.py recomputes the corpus-level results and checks the manuscript against the released outputs (71 checks).
title: Replication package for The Persistence of Taxonomic Entailments in Evolving Biomedical Ontologies

summary: Abstract Purpose: Glioblastoma immunotherapy trials routinely assess tumor immunity based on a single surgical biopsy. We wanted to know how often biopsy location would reverse a relatively immune-rich or immune-poor classification. We also wanted to know whether CD8 T cell expression correlated with antigen-presenting gene expression and which immune programs remain consistent across regions after accounting for overall leukocyte infiltration. Methods: We scored 14 predefined immune expression programs across 75 magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)–localized, nonnecrotic biopsies from 19 patients with isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH)–wild-type glioblastoma, alongside 122 microdissected samples from 10 glioblastomas and two multiregion hepatocellular carcinoma cohorts. Intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) measured regional agreement relative to between-patient differences before and after adjusting for a 12-gene leukocyte score. Results: Regional scores fell on both sides of the fixed 141-biopsy reference mean in 7 of 19 patients (37%) for CD8 expression and 7 of 19 for leukocytes; only two crossed both. Within tumors, CD8 tracked supportive and inhibitory programs equally (mean r = 0.37 and 0.36) but barely tracked major histocompatibility complex class I (MHC-I) transcripts (r = 0.06). Leukocyte adjustment lowered median program ICC from 0.56 to 0.34. Interferon-associated expression retained the highest adjusted point estimate (0.70), though separation from MHC-I (0.47) remained uncertain; additional tumor-purity adjustment yielded similar ICCs (0.66 and 0.62). Conclusion: Biopsy location alone can reverse a glioblastoma’s relative immune-abundance classification. Measuring CD8, interferon, antigen-presentation, and inhibitory programs together across anatomically documented regions separates shared tumor-level features from local variation.
tags: Glioblastoma; Tumor microenvironment; Intratumoral heterogeneity; Tissue biomarkers; CD8 T lymphocytes; Interferon signaling
title: What a single biopsy reveals and misses about the glioblastoma immune microenvironment: Regional reproducibility of immune expression programs

ONE FAMILY, FIVE INCOMMENSURATE EVIDENCE STREAMS The first temptation in an integrated research civilization is to take five measurements and make one score. This is dangerous when their physical units have different meanings. A response in micrometers per kilopascal cannot be added meaningfully to a cell speed in micrometers per hour. Neither can be averaged with a degradation half-life in days or a pore oxygen flux in moles per unit surface and time. Even a dimensionless stability index requires an operational definition and a prespecified acceptable region. A scientifically defensible integration records the full vector and permits a hard stop when any essential component fails. Suppose a matrix allows quicker cell movement while the frequency of adverse changes in cell identity rises. An averaged numerical improvement might hide this problem. A research contract instead keeps separate thresholds for structural fidelity, independent physiology, matrix compatibility, calibrated uncertainty and process safety. The cross-family interface can share measured quantities and evidence packages while refusing to transfer conclusions that have not been independently established. That refusal is itself a form of technological maturity. THIRTY MATHEMATICAL PLATES AND FORTY-TWO RECONSTRUCTABLE SURFACES A formula becomes valuable when its domain of validity is written beside it. The third family preserves the source atlas's thirty candidate formula positions and distinguishes generic test-logic equations from specific physical companion interpretations. For a quasi-elastic response, strain is the ratio of stress to modulus under a declared small-strain regime. That is not enough to describe a hydrogel that relaxes, erodes and remodels while cells exert force. Migration tracking must remove moving substrate landmarks; degradation kinetics must separate dry polymer mass from swollen water; oxygen flux must connect gradient, diffusivity, tortuosity and the actual pore network; remodeling stability must declare how long a bounded trajectory is monitored. Forty-two synthetic three-dimensional models make sensitivities visible across registered parameter ranges. Each saved graph belongs to a CSV numeric grid and a reproducible Python reconstruction program, with units for all axes. They are proposed model objects, not measured cells. Their purpose is to help another investigator find a discontinuity, a nonidentifiable parameter combination or a wrong prediction before undertaking a biological assay. When a future experimental series disagrees with a curve, that discrepancy should be welcomed as evidence, not repaired away by changing the axis limits. TWO HUNDRED RESEARCH GATES AS A LIBRARY OF DISAGREEMENT The 200 Research Gates are not decorative questions. Each door begins with a distinct local investigation and asks why that problem matters, how the most serious competing explanation could account for the visible pattern, and what a successor could do with a simple independent witness. Across gel stiffness, migration, degradation, pore transport and remodeling, the language and scale change. Some doors begin from an intriguing contour, others from a physical contradiction or a failed denominator. Some describe a world in which swelling accounts for everything. Others imagine a pore network that is beautiful but disconnected, an apparently motile cell that is actually being carried by its gel, or a stable feedback trace that conceals tissue identity loss. Their future plans ask for blind sample exchange, matched budget controls, withheld perturbations, new batches, sealed negative specimens and automatic refusal. A Gate has done its work when it leaves a person outside the current research group with enough information to prove the attractive explanation wrong. The failure scenario is therefore not an embarrassment; it is an inheritance. The archive should preserve it with the same care as the favored result. THIRTY-THREE PHOENIX EMBRYOS AND A CIVILIZATION THAT CAN STOP The Phoenix possibilities develop small prototypes rather than claiming completed machines. Their names suggest instrument exchanges, counterfactual matrix libraries, pore-network tomography challenges, mechanical memory loops, independent material reference standards and new methods for storing negative outcomes. Each idea includes a minimum test and a reason to retire it. In a mature autonomous experimental environment, this has consequences beyond documentation. Controllers must abstain when calibration disappears. Hardware or material intervention cannot proceed merely because a prediction model is confident. Human permission, biological source provenance and contamination controls remain external authority constraints. A system that pauses when its assumptions collapse is often more useful than one that always returns an answer. The same principle applies to writing and publication: a research program can be inspirational without presenting synthetic models as achieved biological capabilities. The open scientific record grows stronger when authors state what has not yet been built, measured or validated. THE SCIENTIFIC INHERITANCE The supplied STARLI F18 organ-on-chip monograph reminds this family of a central distinction: geometric precision is not physiological function. In a material-focused family, the same argument has multiple forms. An excellent modulus map is not morphogenesis. A migrating centroid is not necessarily a migrating cell. A fall in wet weight is not always polymer cleavage. A large apparent flux is not necessarily oxygen supply to living tissue. And a stable material signal is not proof of organ-specific homeostasis. Published work on organoid hydrogels, synthetic matrices, viscoelasticity and dynamic mechanics offers methodological precedents. Those sources do not experimentally verify the five new STARLI couplings. This research family offers a plan for making such claims testable, including measurements, strong baselines, uncertainty accounting, data reconstruction and stopping conditions. The long-term goal is not to build a library of conclusions that cannot be questioned, but an open architecture of precise experimental doors. Each generation should be free to improve the questions, reject a mistaken mechanism and keep whatever remains genuinely useful. Let beauty have the ability to continue happening. summary: Reproducibility companion for a powder X-ray diffraction reference-library holdout audit. The package includes Python scripts, checksum-verified source provenance, nominal-label crosswalks, per-query and aggregate results, and figures. It compares the minimum total-variation error for selection of an eligible label with that for a convex blend, using scan/sample-ID, whole-recipe and (where applicable) filename-series holdouts. The nested Archive A bundle includes unchanged files from the Bickmore–Terry–Eberl archive (CC BY 4.0, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23692859). Archive B patterns are obtained separately from the Pabst et al. archive (CC BY 4.0, doi:10.5281/zenodo.18235708) and checksum-verified by the scripts. These are analyses of public measurements against nominal labels; no new measurements were collected. See README.txt and SOURCE-ATTRIBUTION.txt for reproduction and attribution.
title: Data and code for "Copying and blending reference compositions in powder diffraction: a two-archive holdout audit"

Research Unit I · F41–F45 F41 QUANTUM MATERIALS SIMULATION FOR SMART SKINCARE CARRIER DESIGN AT THE LIMIT — Tests facet-dependent adsorption energies against blind facet and solvent-model perturbations. Classical adsorption references and independent surface chemistry distinguish proposed electronic-structure effects from roughness or solvent confounding; unbounded model error blocks skin-performance inference. F42 QUANTUM SENSING AND CUTANEOUS BIOELECTRIC METROLOGY AT THE LIMIT — Measures weak magnetic-field error in traceable skin-like phantoms at equal bandwidth, shielding, time and energy. F43 QUANTUM-ENHANCED SPECTROSCOPY AND SKIN MOLECULAR ANALYSIS AT THE LIMIT — Challenges blinded analyte-identification rates and detection limits under matched incident-photon and acquisition budgets. F44 NANO-OPTICAL SENSING AND SKIN HYDRATION MONITORING AT THE LIMIT — Evaluates optical reconstruction of depth-resolved hydration in layered phantoms with concealed pigmentation and thickness changes. summary: M2-US: A Large-scale Multi-domain and Multi-task Ultrasound Image Dataset Ultrasound imaging is widely used across various clinical applications due to its real-time imaging capabilities, portability, and cost-effectiveness. In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) has demonstrated considerable potential in ultrasound image analysis. However, the development of generalizable AI models remains challenging due to variations in imaging devices, acquisition protocols, anatomical structures, and clinical tasks. Most existing ultrasound datasets focus on specific anatomical regions or individual prediction tasks, limiting their applicability to multi-domain and multi-task learning. To address these limitations, we introduce M2-US , a large-scale, multi-domain and multi-task ultrasound image dataset comprising 67,620 ultrasound images collected from publicly available datasets and retrospective clinical cohorts. The dataset covers more than 30 anatomical structures and pathological targets across diverse clinical applications, including maternal–fetal, cardiac, vascular, abdominal, pulmonary, breast, thyroid, and gynecological ultrasound imaging. The images originate from multiple countries and were acquired using approximately 24 ultrasound scanner models from more than 10 manufacturers, providing substantial diversity in imaging conditions and clinical settings. M2-US supports 26 subtasks across four major ultrasound image analysis tasks : segmentation (12 subtasks), classification (9 subtasks), object detection (2 subtasks), and landmark-based regression (3 subtasks). The dataset provides task-specific annotations, including pixel-wise segmentation masks, image-level classification labels, object bounding boxes, and anatomical landmark coordinates. All data are organized into predefined training, validation, and testing partitions, accompanied by standardized CSV metadata files to facilitate reproducible model development and evaluation. M2-US is designed to support research on task-specific deep learning models, multi-task learning, transfer learning, foundation model adaptation, and cross-domain generalization in ultrasound image analysis. By integrating diverse anatomical targets, imaging conditions, and annotation types within a unified benchmark, M2-US aims to facilitate the development and systematic evaluation of more robust and generalizable ultrasound AI methods. summary: Fixes for macOS 27.2, where v0.4.0 fails to compile native attention and returns wrong results from pivoted LU, plus a round of signal-processing, linear-algebra and special-function additions. 63 commits since v0.4.0. macOS 27.2 If you are on macOS 27.2, upgrade: v0.4.0 is affected by both of these. Native bridge programs compile again. The framework now rejects a bridge bundle with two or more weight files ( verifyBundleAtPath: invalid model ), which broke af.sdpa , causal decoder blocks and fused ONNX attention. Such a bundle is retried with its weights merged into one file (#309). A slice offset on the last axis no longer loses its offset. Two such slices at different offsets feeding matmuls in one fused program returned the wrong column or failed to compile on an M5 Pro, which made linalg.lu_pivoted , det , slogdet , solve and inv return wrong or non-finite results. The compiler now lowers a last-axis-offset slice_by_size (and so crop and static gather) off the last axis; ANEFORGE_ROUTE_WIDTH_SLICES=0 restores the old lowering (#311, #314). bench/slice_offset_probe.py shows whether a machine has the underlying behaviour (#313). Verified on an M5 Pro under macOS 27.2.1: the full on-device suite and the corpus are green. Other chips on 27.2 have not been checked. See the new "macOS 27.2" section of the FAQ. Signal processing dsp.hilbert (analytic signal, #265), dsp.detrend (#278), and the sawtooth , square and chirp generators (#264). Windows: flattop , blackmanharris , nuttall , cosine , gaussian (#268). fft.irfft (#261). Linear algebra and special functions linalg.kron (#262), linalg.polar (#259), linalg.matrix_rank and linalg.cond (#260). special.digamma and special.beta (#250), special.bessel_j1 and special.bessel_i1 (#251). Models and LLMs MPNet encoders (all-mpnet-base-v2) in the sentence-transformers drop-in (#255); RoBERTa-family encoders apply the pad_id + 1 position offset (#257). load_resnet accepts a Hugging Face repo id (#256). Qwen2/2.5 attention biases are loaded; the dense adapter dropped them (#253). Deep small-dimension models no longer hit the ANE op ceiling in decode (#254). MoE top-k selects exactly k experts on exact fp16 ties (#298). ONNX MeanVarianceNormalization , Hardmax and the hyperbolic ops (#263). onnx.coverage_report lists a model's unsupported ops before you try to compile it (#269). Compiler The compile cache is reused instead of forcing recompilation (#284). A compress= request that falls back to a wider encoding now warns (#249). Benchmarks Rooflines for M1 (MacBook Air), M2 Max, M4 Pro, M4 Max and M6, and a re-run of the M1 MacBook Pro. ANE power from the SMC rail where powermetrics reports none (#294), with follow-up fixes for chips whose rail or IOReport layout differs (#305, #307, #308). A run whose idle baseline was not idle is flagged, and its perf/W is withheld from the table (#306). Result files are strict JSON: no bare NaN (#307, #312). Examples Conway's Game of Life (#272), the Mandelbrot set (#273) and the Lorenz attractor (#274), each stepped on the ANE. The whisper.cpp backend exports a usable encoder bundle (#275, #276). Install: pip install -U aneforge (pretrained loaders: pip install "aneforge[models]" ).

summary: This replication package accompanies the manuscript “Reliability, Faithfulness, and Stability of Self-Directed Context Selection in Open-Weight Large Language Models.” It contains source code, experiment configurations, the frozen confirmatory item manifest, processed experimental outputs, statistical-analysis scripts, generated figures, and detailed reproduction instructions. The study evaluates self-directed evidence selection using Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, Phi-3.5-mini-instruct, and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 across HotpotQA, QASPER, and ERASER MultiRC. The confirmatory selection experiment comprises 7,650 model outputs. Raw copies of the public datasets are not redistributed.

summary: This dataset record contains seven curated microscopy image segmentation datasets with image files, corresponding mask annotation files, and predefined train, validation, and test splits. The datasets are derived from public or previously published sources cited in the associated manuscript: Grain (Warren et al., 2024), EMPS (Yildirim and Cole, 2021), Aachen-Heerlen (Iren et al., 2021), UHCS (DeCost et al., 2017), MetalDAM (Luengo et al., 2022), and Super/EBC (Stuckner et al., 2022). The files were reorganized for a unified benchmark, split into train, validation, and test subsets, and subjected to annotation review, supplementary annotation, and quality control. The depositor has confirmed that the curated files can be redistributed for research use. The deposit includes 3,625 image files, 3,625 mask label files, and 163,901 mask instances counted as 8-connected non-zero connected components within the label images. The datasets included are Aachen-Heerlen, EBC, EMPS, Grain, MetalDAM, Super, and UHCS. File-level checksums, dataset statistics, class-wise mask-instance counts, source mapping, and documentation are provided to support reuse and reproducibility.

summary: the zipped file is a self-contained replication package for the paper "The Cost of Restricting Access to Natural Areas: African Swine Fever Containment Zones and Local Income". The execution requires locally installed recent versions of both Stata and R and the download of a package of external data from official websites of the Government of Italy. All steps are documented in the readme file and discussed in the paper. ABSTRACT The spread of African Swine Fever in the European Union since 2014 has triggered a policy response that, in several cases, included severe restrictions on access to forests and other natural areas. In most cases, pig farming and, to a lesser degree, the agricultural sector were compensated for the costs incurred as a consequence of the disease and its containment measures. The indirect costs borne by outdoor-based local economies, on the contrary, have been typically excluded from compensation schemes and, for the most part, remain unmeasured. This paper estimates these costs in the context of the African Swine Fever outbreak that affected North-West Italy from 2022 onward. Using municipal-level taxable income data and a difference-in-differences design, we estimate the effect of access restrictions on local income. We find a decline of self-employment income per taxpayer of about 18–23 percent relative to control municipalities. The effect is weaker and below statistical significance for small business income and absent for wage income and pension income. The result is also unaffected by pre-outbreak pig-farming intensity in the municipality, indicating that the impact of direct costs is negligible. These findings suggest that the portion of containment policies that restricted access to natural areas shifted a significant part of the economic burden of disease control on sectors unrelated to pig farming and on municipalities where pig farming has a very limited presence. They also raise a compensation-design issue: containment policies generate broad public benefits, but also appropriable benefits for pig producers outside the outbreak zone. In those circumstances, when indirect costs remain uncompensated and sector-specific benefits from containment measures are not internalized by the beneficiaries we should expect distorted incentives and sub-optimal policy responses. The paper discusses policy options to improve both the efficiency and fairness of compensation for disease-containment measures that restrict access to natural areas.

summary: An open educational engineering module on hypersonic waverider aerodynamic design, cone-derived shock capture, and lift-to-drag maximization. Covers inverse design from conical shock flowfields, shock-riding leading edges, and zero-spillage lower-surface pressure capture; the osculating cones method for non-axisymmetric planforms and scramjet inlet integration; hypersonic drag polars, lift-to-drag (L/D) maximization, the Küchemann barrier, and leading-edge bluntness versus aerothermal heating trade-offs; worked numerical calculations for caret-waverider pressure lift, wave drag, and polar L/D; an interactive waverider L/D and shock-capture explorer; and conventional delta wing versus waverider comparisons. Aligned with Washington Accord graduate attributes (WA1–WA3) and published on Prep4Uni.Online.
title: Waverider Aerodynamic Design Explained: Cone-Derived Leading Edges & L/D Maximization

summary: This dataset contains the complete experimental sequencing data generated for the study "Thermodynamically Constrained Encoding Improves Reliability in DNA Data Storage" . The study investigates the impact of thermodynamic constraints, based on Gibbs free energy (ΔG), on the reliability and efficiency of DNA-based digital data storage. Two encoding strategies are compared: the reference JPEG DNA encoding and a thermodynamically constrained version designed to improve the representation and recovery of encoded information during DNA sequencing. DNA oligonucleotide pools were synthesized by three independent providers: Agilent SurePrint, Dynegene, and GenScript. The synthesized DNA was amplified and sequenced using Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) PromethION sequencing. Dataset contents The dataset comprises experimental data, including: Raw sequencing reads in FASTQ format from the three DNA synthesis providers. Sequencing data corresponding to both reference and thermodynamically constrained JPEG DNA encoding configurations. These data enable further investigation of sequence-dependent coverage biases, decoding efficiency, and the effects of thermodynamic constraints on the reliable reconstruction of digitally encoded images from synthetic DNA. Related resources A smaller subset of the FASTQ files, sufficient to decode the images synthesized by each provider, is also available on Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22712282

summary: Following AFTD's negative answer dated November 5, 2026, to Hausmann's Question 5.4 in Weighted Max Cut in Subcubic Graphs (arXiv:2611.05178v1, Section 5), we give a different counterexample with an exact residual-order calculation: the generalized Petersen graph GP(7,2) has odd girth five, but deleting any independent set leaves a component with at least four vertices. We prove this by classifying its maximal independent sets into five symmetry classes. The bound four is attained on this graph. The same classification gives an obstruction to the nonempty-independent-side version of Question 5.3; its printed quantifiers admit an empty-side solution.
title: Residual order four in GP(7,2): an alternative proof for Hausmann's Question 5.4 (arXiv:2611.05178v1, Section 5), after AFTD (2026)

summary: Abstract Purpose: Glioblastoma immunotherapy trials routinely assess tumor immunity based on a single surgical biopsy. We wanted to know how often biopsy location would reverse a relatively immune-rich or immune-poor classification. We also wanted to know whether CD8 T cell expression correlated with antigen-presenting gene expression and which immune programs remain consistent across regions after accounting for overall leukocyte infiltration. Methods: We scored 14 predefined immune expression programs across 75 magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)–localized, nonnecrotic biopsies from 19 patients with isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH)–wild-type glioblastoma, alongside 122 microdissected samples from 10 glioblastomas and two multiregion hepatocellular carcinoma cohorts. Intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) measured regional agreement relative to between-patient differences before and after adjusting for a 12-gene leukocyte score. Results: Regional scores fell on both sides of the fixed 141-biopsy reference mean in 7 of 19 patients (37%) for CD8 expression and 7 of 19 for leukocytes; only two crossed both. Within tumors, CD8 tracked supportive and inhibitory programs equally (mean r = 0.37 and 0.36) but barely tracked major histocompatibility complex class I (MHC-I) transcripts (r = 0.06). Leukocyte adjustment lowered median program ICC from 0.56 to 0.34. Interferon-associated expression retained the highest adjusted point estimate (0.70), though separation from MHC-I (0.47) remained uncertain; additional tumor-purity adjustment yielded similar ICCs (0.66 and 0.62). Conclusion: Biopsy location alone can reverse a glioblastoma’s relative immune-abundance classification. Measuring CD8, interferon, antigen-presentation, and inhibitory programs together across anatomically documented regions separates shared tumor-level features from local variation.
tags: Glioblastoma; Tumor microenvironment; Intratumoral heterogeneity; Tissue biomarkers; CD8 T lymphocytes; Interferon signaling
title: What a single biopsy reveals and misses about the glioblastoma immune microenvironment: Regional reproducibility of immune expression programs

ONE FAMILY, FIVE INCOMMENSURATE EVIDENCE STREAMS The first temptation in an integrated research civilization is to take five measurements and make one score. This is dangerous when their physical units have different meanings. A response in micrometers per kilopascal cannot be added meaningfully to a cell speed in micrometers per hour. Neither can be averaged with a degradation half-life in days or a pore oxygen flux in moles per unit surface and time. Even a dimensionless stability index requires an operational definition and a prespecified acceptable region. A scientifically defensible integration records the full vector and permits a hard stop when any essential component fails. Suppose a matrix allows quicker cell movement while the frequency of adverse changes in cell identity rises. An averaged numerical improvement might hide this problem. A research contract instead keeps separate thresholds for structural fidelity, independent physiology, matrix compatibility, calibrated uncertainty and process safety. The cross-family interface can share measured quantities and evidence packages while refusing to transfer conclusions that have not been independently established. That refusal is itself a form of technological maturity. THIRTY MATHEMATICAL PLATES AND FORTY-TWO RECONSTRUCTABLE SURFACES A formula becomes valuable when its domain of validity is written beside it. The third family preserves the source atlas's thirty candidate formula positions and distinguishes generic test-logic equations from specific physical companion interpretations. For a quasi-elastic response, strain is the ratio of stress to modulus under a declared small-strain regime. That is not enough to describe a hydrogel that relaxes, erodes and remodels while cells exert force. Migration tracking must remove moving substrate landmarks; degradation kinetics must separate dry polymer mass from swollen water; oxygen flux must connect gradient, diffusivity, tortuosity and the actual pore network; remodeling stability must declare how long a bounded trajectory is monitored. Forty-two synthetic three-dimensional models make sensitivities visible across registered parameter ranges. Each saved graph belongs to a CSV numeric grid and a reproducible Python reconstruction program, with units for all axes. They are proposed model objects, not measured cells. Their purpose is to help another investigator find a discontinuity, a nonidentifiable parameter combination or a wrong prediction before undertaking a biological assay. When a future experimental series disagrees with a curve, that discrepancy should be welcomed as evidence, not repaired away by changing the axis limits. TWO HUNDRED RESEARCH GATES AS A LIBRARY OF DISAGREEMENT The 200 Research Gates are not decorative questions. Each door begins with a distinct local investigation and asks why that problem matters, how the most serious competing explanation could account for the visible pattern, and what a successor could do with a simple independent witness. Across gel stiffness, migration, degradation, pore transport and remodeling, the language and scale change. Some doors begin from an intriguing contour, others from a physical contradiction or a failed denominator. Some describe a world in which swelling accounts for everything. Others imagine a pore network that is beautiful but disconnected, an apparently motile cell that is actually being carried by its gel, or a stable feedback trace that conceals tissue identity loss. Their future plans ask for blind sample exchange, matched budget controls, withheld perturbations, new batches, sealed negative specimens and automatic refusal. A Gate has done its work when it leaves a person outside the current research group with enough information to prove the attractive explanation wrong. The failure scenario is therefore not an embarrassment; it is an inheritance. The archive should preserve it with the same care as the favored result. THIRTY-THREE PHOENIX EMBRYOS AND A CIVILIZATION THAT CAN STOP The Phoenix possibilities develop small prototypes rather than claiming completed machines. Their names suggest instrument exchanges, counterfactual matrix libraries, pore-network tomography challenges, mechanical memory loops, independent material reference standards and new methods for storing negative outcomes. Each idea includes a minimum test and a reason to retire it. In a mature autonomous experimental environment, this has consequences beyond documentation. Controllers must abstain when calibration disappears. Hardware or material intervention cannot proceed merely because a prediction model is confident. Human permission, biological source provenance and contamination controls remain external authority constraints. A system that pauses when its assumptions collapse is often more useful than one that always returns an answer. The same principle applies to writing and publication: a research program can be inspirational without presenting synthetic models as achieved biological capabilities. The open scientific record grows stronger when authors state what has not yet been built, measured or validated. THE SCIENTIFIC INHERITANCE The supplied STARLI F18 organ-on-chip monograph reminds this family of a central distinction: geometric precision is not physiological function. In a material-focused family, the same argument has multiple forms. An excellent modulus map is not morphogenesis. A migrating centroid is not necessarily a migrating cell. A fall in wet weight is not always polymer cleavage. A large apparent flux is not necessarily oxygen supply to living tissue. And a stable material signal is not proof of organ-specific homeostasis. Published work on organoid hydrogels, synthetic matrices, viscoelasticity and dynamic mechanics offers methodological precedents. Those sources do not experimentally verify the five new STARLI couplings. This research family offers a plan for making such claims testable, including measurements, strong baselines, uncertainty accounting, data reconstruction and stopping conditions. The long-term goal is not to build a library of conclusions that cannot be questioned, but an open architecture of precise experimental doors. Each generation should be free to improve the questions, reject a mistaken mechanism and keep whatever remains genuinely useful. Let beauty have the ability to continue happening. summary: Reproducibility companion for a powder X-ray diffraction reference-library holdout audit. The package includes Python scripts, checksum-verified source provenance, nominal-label crosswalks, per-query and aggregate results, and figures. It compares the minimum total-variation error for selection of an eligible label with that for a convex blend, using scan/sample-ID, whole-recipe and (where applicable) filename-series holdouts. The nested Archive A bundle includes unchanged files from the Bickmore–Terry–Eberl archive (CC BY 4.0, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23692859). These are analyses of public measurements against nominal labels; no new measurements were collected. See README.txt and SOURCE-ATTRIBUTION.txt for reproduction and attribution.
