summary: The work continues the geometric model of the distribution of primes [2] and the work “The Number Arrow and the Line 1/2” [1]. The geometric formula for the number of odd composites up to p², N(p) = 1 + 3(p − 1)(p − 3)/8, is treated as the first level of a ladder in which the scale is squared at each step: 5² → 5⁴ → 5⁸ → 5¹⁶. It is shown that this formula is the best quadratic formula for the level up to 5⁴: it is exact everywhere except for one compensating pair of misses (p = 15 and p = 17). The quadratic lattice of a level holds up to the basis 7 inclusive and breaks down right after it. The error of the formula splits into two superimposed tables: a smooth level correction and an oscillation which, in the explicit formula, is a sum of cosines over the zeros of the zeta function. The main result is a law of levels, checked on exact values of π (x) up to 3³² ≈ 1.9 · 10¹⁵: when the scale is squared, the relative error of the prime count is squared, and the error itself is inverse to the linear scale p = √x obtained from the difference of squares: ε · p stays of order one at all checked steps. The law holding at all steps is equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis (von Koch, 1901). The author puts forward the hypothesis that the self-similarity of the ladder may become a route to its proof: for this one must show that the step structure itself does not allow ε · p to grow faster than a power of the logarithm. This step is named but not taken. The method may become the basis for an exact count of prime density by levels without the exponential and the logarithm in the level formula. Section 7 gives a geometric reading for a reader without mathematical training: why the basis of the model is 2, 3, 5, 7, how the seam 8–9 links the linear and the quadratic levels, why the centres of the seam differ by exactly ¼ and how π arises from all the differences together, where zero is on the arrow and why the whole arrow projects into one circle. The similarity with the construction of the Birth of Dimensions model is shown. Section 8 shows that the accumulated mismatch over the seams is Euler's sine at one half ( π ), while accumulation over the primes gives γ (Mertens); that the error of the prime count at a step is of the order of the square root of the mismatch of the frame; and that the transfer of the observer changes nothing if and only if all zeros lie on the axis 1/2 — this is the Hilbert — Pólya programme. Each seam is a right triangle in a circle: the centre along the line is the radius, the centre on the circle the cosine, the hole the sine, and sin² + cos² = 1. The author believes that this work can become a proof of the Riemann hypothesis; the missing step is to show that the unity of the process makes the transfer of the observer a symmetry. The work is laid out as a programme of proof: the missing step is formulated as a target statement resting on the birth of the arrow — a pure projection from one unit, the product over the primes. The missing step is also written as a statement about positivity: from Mertens' square 2(1 + cos θ )², which pushes the zeros away from 1, to the square of Weil's energy, which must hold them on ½ and forbid pairs of zeros on opposite sides of the circle. The work rests on classical results — Pell–Lagrange, Legendre's sieve, the explicit formula of Riemann and von Mangoldt — and proposes a new linking of them: the geometry of the seam as a model of the process linking the primes. The author's answer to Riemann's question is geometric: on each range chosen in a definite way, the process of the link of the primes is seen as the unit circle and a sinusoid around it; for his work the author regards this answer as a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, and what in it is accepted as an initial
title: The Fractal Ladder of Prime Density: Quadratic Scale and Linear Error

summary: Version v6.0-jbi accompanies the submission of the article to the Journal of Biomedical Informatics (Elsevier). It adds manuscript_jbi/, which builds the shortened journal version (body of about 5,980 words, two figures, six tables) and its supplementary material from the v5.0 manuscript, a graphical abstract (figures/Graphical_abstract_JBI_DNFR.png), and check_numbers.py, which verifies that every number in the journal version occurs in the v5.0 manuscript or supplement generated from the result files. It also adds the ratings of a second, blinded clinical rater (a physician; results/expert_review2_filled.xlsx with the rater’s name withheld, and the agreement and discrimination statistics in results/expert_review2.json). Models, data and the main results are unchanged from v5.0. Code, derived data and result files for Differentiable Neuro-Fuzzy Reasoning (DNFR), a path-based link predictor that learns degree-aware edge memberships, a Schweizer–Sklar t-norm per metapath and metapath reliabilities, and aggregates paths by noisy-OR, used as an instrument for a controlled component analysis on medical knowledge graphs. Tasks: drug repurposing in Hetionet v1.0 and PrimeKG, disease–symptom prediction in Hetionet and in the graded health knowledge graph of Rotmensch et al. (2017), and a secondary test on a NHANES fuzzy relation, under leave-dyad-out random and disease-centred splits. Comparators: fixed t-norms, component ablations, restarts of the t-norm parameter, DWPC with logistic regression (with and without degree and prior features), a degree-preserving edge prior, popularity, AnyBURL, truncated and soft-thresholded SVD and knowledge graph embeddings. Version v4.0 (fourth revision) completes 10 leave-dyad-out splits on Hetionet compound–treats–disease for the fixed Hamacher product, fixed degree terms, annealing, frozen memberships, DNFR 2.0, the shared and fixed t-norm parameters and AnyBURL; adds an ablation without metapaths that contain the target relation, a fact-level attribution of DWPC-LR next to DNFR's, the evidence share by metapath class, an information-content check with matched spread, a profile of the t-norm parameter extended to p > 0 and run on Hetionet disease–symptom, a tuning grid for NBFNet, a script that re-runs a key result from a clean checkout (scripts/verify_clean.sh), and the sheet for a clinical assessment of the explanations (dnfr/expert_sheet.py, dnfr/expert_summary.py). The secondary NHANES test was removed from the article. Version v3.0-rev3 (third revision) added DNFR 2.0, four refinements tested one at a time and in combination (overlap-aware aggregation, Gumbel-softmax operator choice, an information-content hub discount and membership annealing), a fixed t-norm selected on validation data, a converged L-BFGS profile of the t-norm parameter, an unbounded parameterisation, a compact NBFNet baseline, an exact edge-level Shapley attribution of the explanations, a mechanistic classification of the drug-repurposing explanations, a sparsity variant that keeps the target relation, and 10 leave-dyad-out splits for the main comparisons on Hetionet compound–treats–disease, Hetionet disease–symptom and the graded health knowledge graph. Version 1.1.0 (second revision) added a profile analysis of the t-norm parameter, training without early stopping, additional splits, equivalence tests, the edge prior, share-matched and edge-level explanation tests, unit tests and the script that builds the manuscript from the statistics files. Includes per-query ranks for every method and split, trained models, path explanations, and the statistics files from which every number in the manuscript is read. Hetionet and PrimeKG are downloaded by download_data.py with MD5 checks.
title: Code and derived results for: Which parts of a neuro-fuzzy path reasoner should be learned? A controlled component analysis on medical knowledge graphs

summary: Electrons can change subband in quantum transport, holes can be solved by it too, the package makes quality triangle meshes, the quantum channel on meshes keeps band steps where the mesh puts them, and scattering lifetimes and mobility of a 2D gas are computed from its own wavefunction. The examples print what they printed before, except example 58 (the quantum channel on a mesh, now closer to the tensor grid); examples 62 to 65 are new. Added Device.negf(..., coupled_modes=M) : NEGF in coupled mode space, the lowest M states of every column joined by their overlaps, so electrons change subband where the channel's profile across it changes; with all modes it is the full 2D problem (ballistic only). kpenvelope.negf adds Slab , slab_transport and lead_surface_green (leads by decimation). Device.negf(..., carrier="holes") : the holes of a QuantumChannel with holes=(m_z, m_inplane, ...) , with or without scattering, uncoupled or coupled; Slab(mass_x=) for a mass along x of its own. kpenvelope.mesh.quality_mesh(regions, h, min_angle) : quality meshes of polygon regions by Delaunay refinement (every boundary and interface an edge, no node in a segment's diametral circle, smallest angle up to 34 degrees, a size field). kpenvelope.scattering.Subband : transport and quantum lifetimes and the mobility of one subband from acoustic phonons, alloy disorder, interface roughness (Gaussian or exponential correlation) and screened charged impurities (sheets or profiles), with your material numbers. Changed The quantum channel on meshes: the material on each sample of a line is the mean over its share of the line. Before, a node on a band step took its whole share from the one region it belongs to, which moved the step by up to half a spacing, differently on each line: on a quality mesh the confined sheet was 1.6 to 2.0 percent off a fine tensor grid at every mesh size; now 0.54, 0.20 and 0.10 percent at 1, 0.5 and 0.25 nm. On a mesh made from a tensor grid with a band step inside the window, the result now differs from the tensor grid's by that half-spacing effect of the tensor grid. Device(grid=...) refuses nodes closer than 1e-6 nm with a clear message (a near-duplicate node made the Poisson solve fail). Not included (see docs/limits.md) Scattering in coupled mode space; phonon self-energies in NEGF; NEGF on triangle meshes; both carriers in NEGF at once. Polar optical phonon and intersubband scattering in the lifetimes. The hot-electron model's limit at zero relaxation time with velocity saturation, the plasma's own chemistry, oxide shapes that follow the flow, elasticity, electronic stopping beyond Lindhard-Scharff, tunneling paths that bend with the field, tunneling and heat inside one Newton solve, and the Peltier heat in Fermi-Dirac form are as in 0.26.0. The app does not have the new features yet. Checks (tests) 15 new tests (372 in all; docs/checks.md has the tolerances): the leads by decimation against the exact chain lead; coupled mode space against the dense real-space inverse, mode counting, the sum of chains without mixing, and the uncoupled device; holes against the mirror image of electrons and the QuantumChannel's holes; a slab with a mass along x of its own; the quality mesh's angles, areas, conformity and diametral circles, and a ring resistor converging at second order; the quantum channel on a quality mesh against a fine tensor grid; the scattering rates against closed forms (Fang-Howard and square-well overlaps, Price's acoustic rate, the alloy rate), an independent integral with the closed-form Fang-Howard form factors, the far-away-charge limits, the Hellmann-Feynman shift of a level, and the thermal average. All 65 documented examples were rerun.
title: kpenvelope: interface charges, misfit-dislocation charge, two-dimensional electron and hole gases and device curves of wurtzite nitride stacks, with a self-consistent six-band k.p solver

summary: STARLI | F051–F060 / 300 Flagship 13 Fission · Volume I · Quantum Sensing, Reference Integrity and Trustworthy Biosensor Qualification Author: 33  |  Nonclinical Research Design Working Edition v1.3  |  English Zenodo Ten-Volume Overview This ten-volume collection joins two five-theme research units from the STARLI 300-theme atlas. Research Unit I (F051–F055) examines long-term quantum-sensor stability, magnetic readout–motion decoupling, optical interface loss, autonomous fault diagnosis and multisite calibration. Research Unit II (F056–F060) develops common-mode failure identification, biological ground-truth validation, low-photodamage operation, trustworthy metrology and full-lifecycle qualification. The common challenge is whether a measured improvement survives independent references, hidden nuisance variables and resource-matched classical controls. The ten English working editions contain 7,770 PDF pages: 300 candidate mathematical plates, 820 chapter openings, 4,100 one-page investigations, 2,000 separate Research Gates and 330 Phoenix Answer Embryos. Version 1.3 revises the six notes beneath each Gate question: causal mechanism, independent witness, blinded falsifier, competing explanation, stop rule and successor interface. These numbers describe editorial architecture and proposed research designs, not experimentally established originality or quantum advantage. The Ten Research Directions F051  Microscale Quantum Sensor Long-Term Stability At The Limit — Studies whether sensitivity remains stable across prolonged acquisition, replacement references and biological-matrix changes. Compares a quantum channel with identical-optics quantum-off ablation; tracks detection limit, calibration drift and interval coverage. Hidden reference drift or undercoverage of blinded truth defeats the proposed advantage. F052  Quantum Magnetic-Field Sensing And Microrobotic Motion Decoupling At The Limit — Separates quantum magnetic-field readout from motion-induced field changes in microrobotic experiments. Tracks Allan deviation, field sensitivity and photon budget against a strong classical sensor. Equal-photon comparisons test whether an apparent gain comes from photon count rather than quantum coherence. F053  Quantum Optical Microfluidic Interface Loss At The Limit — Examines losses and nuisance coupling at an optical quantum-sensing interface within microfluidic systems. Uses recorded photon budgets, contrast, drift and a locked reference instrument to test end-to-end readout integrity. Post-selection and loss of reference identity are explicit rival or stopping conditions. F054  Quantum Biosensor Autonomous Fault Diagnosis At The Limit — Designs autonomous detection of biosensor failure states without equating a model alert with an independently verified fault. Hidden reference-drift challenges, quantum-off ablations and withheld measurements interrogate field sensitivity, contrast and coherence-time estimates. Uncalibrated uncertainty intervals must trigger abstention. F055  Multisite Quantum Sensing Network Calibration At The Limit — Proposes traceable calibration transfer between quantum sensing sites, including independent references and shared-drift injection. Compares sensitivity, Allan deviation and cross-site reproducibility with classical optical or magnetic sensors. A site-consistent improvement is insufficient if extra photons explain the difference. F056  Quantum Sensor Common-Mode Failure Identification At The Limit — Investigates common-mode faults that can make multiple quantum sensors agree while all are wrong. A locked reference instrument, masked reference substitution and covariance-aware uncertainty audits separate shared errors from true agreement. Missing reference identity or selective retention of good readings invalidates release. F057  Biological Sample Quantum Readout Truth

summary: Observable forms are frequently used to identify, classify, and evaluate systems. However, an observable form does not necessarily provide a complete account of the internal processes that produce or govern the system. In some situations, the external representation becomes the dominant basis for interpretation, replacing a more direct examination of the system's internal structure, functional relationships, and causal processes. The Surface-Process Inference Paradox (SPIP) is proposed as a general theoretical framework for examining this problem across different classes of observable systems. Its central question is whether what is externally observed adequately represents the system's actual internal processes, or whether the observer becomes restricted by the external form and consequently fails to understand what is occurring within the system. The framework distinguishes two principal pathways. The first is structural observational ambiguity, in which different internal processes can produce indistinguishable observable forms. The second is observer-mediated surface capture, in which the observer gives excessive interpretive importance to an external category or representation despite the availability of relevant process evidence. A primary case study, the Genre-Bound Musical Evaluation Case (GBMEC), is used to preserve the original observation concerning music genre and internal musical structure. The framework is then generalized to human behaviour, visual art, literature, social practices, institutions, software, artificial intelligence, biological systems, and physical systems. Mathematical formalization is developed through state-space models, observation functions, observer representations, process-inference errors, mutual information, observability, and controlled category interventions. Eight theoretical propositions, boundary conditions, hypotheses, and falsification criteria are established. SPIP is presented as a testable and potentially cross-disciplinary framework, not as a completed universal law. Its scientific contribution will depend on whether its mechanisms can be operationalized, distinguished from existing explanations, and independently reproduced across relevant domains.

summary: Processing code, derived maps and result tables for a study of urban expansion, summer land surface temperature (LST) and residents' potential surface-heat exposure in Baghdad, Basra and Erbil, Iraq, from 2000 to 2025. Contents: (1) the complete code, comprising a Python/Google Earth Engine pipeline with its full configuration, local robustness checks, a built-up agreement analysis and the scripts that draw every figure of the article; (2) a harmonised 30 m four-class land-cover series (GLC_FCS30D, 2000–2020) and annual built-up masks; (3) Landsat summer LST and NDVI epoch composites (2000–2025), also expressed as anomalies relative to a rural ring; (4) MODIS Terra/Aqua night-time LST composites (2005–2025); (5) hot-pixel frequency and Getis–Ord Gi* hotspot maps; (6) GHS-POP and WorldPop population grids clipped to each study area and scaled to the 2024 Iraq census; (7) analysis zones (core, new growth, rural ring) as GeoJSON; and (8) all result tables, including SUHI by zone, trends, matched conversion contrasts, exposure metrics, and the rural-reference, threshold, multiple-testing and placebo robustness checks. All files are derived from open datasets (Landsat, MODIS, GLC_FCS30D, GHSL, WSF Evolution, WorldPop, JRC Global Surface Water, SRTM, ERA5-Land). See 00_README.md for file contents, raster codes, limitations, run order and source citations.

Contents: (1) the complete code, comprising a Python/Google Earth Engine pipeline with its full configuration, local robustness checks, a built-up agreement analysis and the scripts that draw every figure of the article; (2) a harmonised 30 m four-class land-cover series (GLC_FCS30D, 2000–2020) and annual built-up masks; (3) Landsat summer LST and NDVI epoch composites (2000–2025), also expressed as anomalies relative to a rural ring; (4) MODIS Terra/Aqua night-time LST composites (2005–2025); (5) hot-pixel frequency and Getis–Ord Gi* hotspot maps; (6) GHS-POP and WorldPop population grids clipped to each study area and scaled to the 2024 Iraq census; (7) analysis zones (core, new growth, rural ring) as GeoJSON; and (8) all result tables, including SUHI by zone, trends, matched conversion contrasts, exposure metrics, and the rural-reference, threshold, multiple-testing and placebo robustness checks. All files are derived from open datasets (Landsat, MODIS, GLC_FCS30D, GHSL, WSF Evolution, WorldPop, JRC Global Surface Water, SRTM, ERA5-Land). See 00_README.md for file contents, raster codes, limitations, run order and source citations.

summary: THE DEVICE MUST EARN ITS RELEASE An Integrated Technical Guide to Trustworthy Autonomous Neural Nanomanufacturing STARLI / YULI | Research Family 16 | Flagships F151–F160 of 200 | Author: 33 / STARLI–YULI | Research Design and Technical Integration Edition | 7 November 2026 The central question of autonomous neural nanomanufacturing is not whether an intelligent manufacturing line can produce a visually convincing neural electrode. It is whether the line can demonstrate, by evidence accessible to an independent examiner, that the fabricated object meets its declared physical and functional criteria, that its apparent efficiency was not created by quietly excluding unsuccessful attempts, that its defect assessment is not dependent on a shared mistake, and that the machine would refuse an unsafe or unqualified decision even when the optimization algorithm prefers to continue. Neural nanomanufacturing brings a remarkable variety of engineering disciplines into contact. Lithography controls geometry; material preparation establishes the initial chemical state; microscopy and electrochemical measurements create partial views of a device; statistical models infer hidden quality; control systems change recipes; safety interlocks restrict what the equipment may do; and qualified people determine whether the resulting evidence is sufficient for release. Each discipline can work well in isolation while the complete manufacturing claim remains false. This guide proposes a way to make the interfaces between them scientifically accountable. The basis for this essay is a set of ten prospective STARLI / YULI research introductions, F151 through F160. Their research questions concern autonomous recipe selection, closed-loop nanoelectrode fabrication, intelligent nanomaterial quality control, adaptive microstructure formation, AI-based defect detection, process digital twins, cross-batch electrochemical stability, energy efficiency, autonomous stopping, and trustworthy release authority. Those ten investigations are treated here as interacting duties within one nonclinical experimental program, not as ten completed demonstrations and not as proof that an integrated factory already exists. Their common physical perimeter is a controlled neural nanoelectrode manufacturing bench, with coded material lots, instrument-calibration records, machine event logs, independent inspection, and hardware-level ability to stop. Their common scientific demand is falsifiability. A device receives no special status because its manufacturer calls the controller intelligent, autonomous, quantum, or advanced. Its status comes from comparisons with an appropriate conventional line, independent measurement and a complete record of the attempts that failed. A newcomer can enter the topic through a simple thought experiment. Imagine two production benches that receive nominally similar precursor materials and seek to produce a defined pattern of neural electrodes. The first follows a fixed qualified recipe and relies on manual inspection. The second can alter processing settings when a sensor reports a deviation. After a week, the adaptive line displays more attractive device images and announces lower production energy. Have we learned that it is better? Not until we know the denominator of attempted devices, the calibration condition of the metrology, the origin of its defect labels, whether defective parts were discarded before counting, whether the energy calculation included idling and rework, and whether a safety stop would still work if the optimizing software failed. The appropriate research object is therefore not a single successful coupon. It is the documented manufacturing episode, from material receipt to independent release or justified refusal. This episode becomes the basic unit that connects the ten flagships. 1. From a collection of manufacturing improvements to a single evidence contract The ten source themes are easier to understand when
title: STARLI / YULI / FAMILY 16 / F151 - F160 AUTONOMOUS NEURAL NANOMANUFACTURING - TEN RESEARCH DESIGNS F151 / Ai Autonomous Neural Nanomanufacturing At The Limit Primary endpoint: first-pass automated manufacturing yield [%]. Concealed challenge: concealed precursor material-lot replacement. Rival: selection of only the best finished coupons. Physical limitation: count all aborted runs and do not permit autonomous release. F152 / Closed-Loop Neural Nanoelectrode Fabrication At The Limit Primary endpoint: nanoelectrode patterned line-width error [um]. Concealed challenge: blinded exposure focal-plane displacement. Rival: machine-stage thermal drift. Physical limitation: reject any uncalibrated metrology feedback. F153 / Intelligent Quality Control Of Neural Nanomaterials At The Limit Primary endpoint: nanomaterial inspection false-negative rate [%]. Concealed challenge: blind seeding of trace-defect specimens. Rival: biased manual defect annotation. Physical limitation: stop if even one predefined safety-critical defect is not declared. F154 / Adaptive Neural Microstructure Manufacturing At The Limit Primary endpoint: adaptive microfeature height-following RMSE [nm]. Concealed challenge: concealed design-mask topology change. Rival: unreported manual post-processing. Physical limitation: stop if topography extrapolates beyond the height standard. F155 / Ai Defect Detection In Neural Interfaces At The Limit Primary endpoint: neural-interface defect-detection recall [%]. Concealed challenge: concealed introduction of unseen defect morphologies. Rival: learning illumination features instead of defects. Physical limitation: reject release when hidden critical defects are missed. Research method parent: supplied 780-page F02 research monograph. Structural and visual anchor: Family 10 F091-F100 v1.1. Science targets derive from the F101-F200 flagship atlas; all proposals are untested. STARLI / YULI / FAMILY 16 / F151 - F160 AUTONOMOUS NEURAL NANOMANUFACTURING - TEN RESEARCH DESIGNS F156 / Process Digital Twins For Neural Nanodevices At The Limit Primary endpoint: process digital-twin signed width residual [um]. Concealed challenge: blinded swap to a second manufacturing machine. Rival: leakage of reference measurements into the fitted twin. Physical limitation: recalibrate or abstain on unseen machine geometry. F157 / Cross-Batch Stability In Neural Nanomanufacturing At The Limit Primary endpoint: cross-lot electrode-impedance coefficient of variation [%]. Concealed challenge: concealed material supplier substitution. Rival: differences between impedance measurement fixtures. Physical limitation: reject cross-batch claims without independent EIS. F158 / Energy Efficiency Of Neural Nanomanufacturing At The Limit Primary endpoint: energy per independently qualified manufactured device [J/device]. Concealed challenge: blinded inclusion of idle and rework energy. Rival: lower reported energy through greater reject rates. Physical limitation: halt energy claims if defects or rejects rise. F159 / Autonomous Stop Conditions In Neural Nanomanufacturing At The Limit Primary endpoint: autonomous hardware hard-stop missed-event rate [%]. Concealed challenge: concealed injection of out-of-envelope process commands. Rival: counting delayed alarms as normal operation. Physical limitation: stop the bench immediately upon an interlock miss. F160 / Trustworthy Autonomous Neural Nanomanufacturing Platforms At The Limit Primary endpoint: independent quality-release assessor agreement [%]. Concealed challenge: blinded replacement of quality inspectors. Rival: false consensus from shared evaluator software. Physical limitation: no release without independently reconstructable adjudication. Release status: complete prospective research manuscripts with independent expert review pending on mathematical assumptions, semantic repetition and reproducibility. No clinical efficacy is asserted. Join the STARLI Research Community: https://zenodo.org/communities/starli-research-gate/ We do not need to know which door future generations will choose to open. We only hope that when they open it, they will find a little light to guide their way. 🌈🚪✨

summary: An execution-backed benchmark harness for AI code-review agents. It applies each reviewer's suggested patch in an isolated workspace, runs the required tests and validators, and scores detection separately from validated repair. It also ships CRA-Integrity, a track that asks whether a reviewer can tell a genuinely correct green pull request from one whose validation evidence was weakened.

summary: NumPy benchmark reporting 171 broad-sweep configurations across 13 labeled paradigm categories, 17 deep-ablation runs, and 4 follow-up runs. In the mixed prose/code ablation, HyenaDilated-d64 records 2.8177 average BPC at 2.78 microseconds per token with 29,312 parameters, versus Transformer-d128 at 2.9998 average BPC and 7.39 microseconds per token with 163,584 parameters. ConfGated-SSM+PPM-d128 records 1.9998 BPC on prose. The accompanying repository contains source code, result JSON files, and reproducibility material.
title: Beyond Transformers: A NumPy Benchmark of Language-Model Architectures Across 13 Paradigm Categories

summary: Flight safety and the reliability of aircraft operations under the extremely low temperatures of the Arctic Zone depend directly on the stability of the low-temperature properties of aviation fuels. The critical parameter determining the cold-flow properties and uninterrupted pumpability of fuel is the freezing point (the onset of crystallization, TNK); exceeding it leads to the precipitation of a solid phase and the risk of fuel filter blockage. This article presents a comparative analysis of the freezing point of TS-1 aviation kerosene produced by four leading Russian oil refineries (coded as A, B, V, and G). The tests were conducted in a certified laboratory using the GOST 5066 method with the "KRISTALL-20" automatic analyzer. Significant differences in coldflow properties depending on the manufacturer were revealed. Samples from manufacturers A, B, and V demonstrated high phase stability (freezing points from −62.3 °C to −66.8 °C), ensuring a reliable safety margin relative to GOST 10227 requirements (not higher than −60 °C) for polar aviation. The product from manufacturer G showed a freezing point of −58.7 °C, which meets the baseline standard but imposes operational limitations according to GOST 16350. Additionally, an analysis was conducted on the impact of seasonal temperature fluctuations in Arctic regions on the permissible storage duration of fuel at airfields without loss of low-temperature characteristics. Typical operational scenarios in remote airports, where the possibility of prompt replacement of a fuel batch is absent, were considered: under such conditions, even a slight deviation of the freezing point from optimal values can lead to a critical reduction in fuel system throughput. It was concluded that the manufacturer factor must be taken into account during the incoming quality control of aviation fuels for Arctic regions. It is recommended to include in acceptance procedures not only verification of compliance with baseline standards but also an assessment of the freezing point margin, taking into account forecast minimum temperatures in the area of operation. This approach will minimize the risk of fuel system failures and enhance the overall reliability of aviation equipment under extreme climatic conditions.

summary: This paper examines the emerging possibility of organised data marauders and data warriors for hire as a structural feature of the liquid order. Drawing on the analysis of trans-sovereign force, algorithmic neo-contractors, cyber-mercenaries and private sector offensive actors, it traces historical precedents of private violence and information operations through to contemporary zero-day markets, commercial spyware, narrative laundering and LLM data poisoning. These actors operate across strategic, infrastructural, algorithmic and cognitive domains, exploiting the inverse law of sovereign accountability. The paper connects this development to the rise of independent security constructors who offer Dual-Core compatible, contestable services rather than pure extraction. Within the Flow Sovereignty and Reserve of Humanity framework, such constructors can be integrated as peripheral agents whose morphisms remain auditable, while unconstrained data marauders constitute a cohomology threat. The analysis closes with architectural propositions for containing the former and constraining the latter under Permanent Systemic Instability. KSCCN article (3 pages).
